description_en: A wave-carved basalt outcrop on Jeju City's north shore that looks like a dragon's head rising from the sea, a few minutes from the airport. A short walk east brings you to Yongyeon, a narrow emerald pond in a cliff gorge crossed by a lit wooden suspension bridge (Yongyeon Cloud Bridge) that is popular for evening strolls.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated

description_en: The reconstructed seat of Jeju's Joseon-era provincial government, a walled compound of red-pillared halls and pavilions in the old city center. Next to its gate stands Gwandeokjeong, a 15th-century pavilion that is one of the oldest surviving buildings on the island.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30). Seasonal night opening May 1-Oct 31: 18:00-21:00, Wed-Sun only (closed Mon & Tue at night), free entry

description_en: A quiet, tree-shaded sacred site where, according to Jeju's founding myth, the three ancestors of the Tamna kingdom emerged from holes in the ground. The grounds include the three-hole depression, a shrine hall, and a small exhibition and video hall explaining the legend.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales end 17:30); opens 10:00 on Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: The national museum for Jeju's history and archaeology, tracing the island from prehistoric settlements and the Tamna kingdom through the Joseon era. Admission is free, and it also has an immersive media room and a children's museum.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30); children's museum 09:30-18:00; immersive media room 10:00-17:30

description_en: A provincial museum that explains how volcanic Jeju was formed and how islanders traditionally lived, with natural history, folk life, modern-life and marine galleries. Outside, a central garden displays rocks and stone carvings, including dol hareubang statues.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public/substitute holiday, the next non-holiday); Jan 1; Seollal; Chuseok; two fumigation periods per year (e.g., closed Nov 23-24, 2026)

description_en: Jeju's biggest and longest-running permanent market, a covered maze of stalls selling seafood, tangerines, local snacks and souvenirs just a few minutes from the old city centre. In the evening a street-food night market sets up inside the market (enter around Gate 8).
opening_hours: Market approx. 07:00-21:00 (average; varies by stall). Night market: Nov-Apr 18:00-24:00, May-Oct 19:00-24:00 (stalls close early when sold out)
closed_days: none (open year-round including holidays; individual stalls vary)

description_en: A wooded volcanic hill (about 148 m) beside Jeju Port, turned into a city park with pine-shaded paths, exercise areas, a pavilion and the Mochungsa memorial grounds. Its summit is a classic spot for watching the sun set over the harbour and city.
image_source: VISITJEJU (제주관광공사) official photo - licence terms not stated

description_en: A small 67 m volcanic cone right next to Jeju International Airport, reached by a short but steep path from Doduhang port. The grassy summit gives open views of the sea, the city and landing planes, plus the popular tree-framed 'Kisses Zone' photo spot.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (no set hours; access can occasionally be restricted)

description_en: The closest swimming beach to downtown Jeju and the airport, known for its grey-sand shore and the pair of red and white horse-shaped lighthouses on the breakwater. A pine grove with a campsite sits behind the sand, and it is a favourite spot for sunsets.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (beach area). Swimming only in the official season: 2026 season was Jun 24 - Sep 6, 10:00-19:00, with night swimming Jul 15 - Aug 15 until 21:00

description_en: A free, city-run arboretum on the slopes of Gwangi Oreum in Jeju City, with themed gardens of native and subtropical plants, a bamboo grove and a forest-bathing area. Paved walking loops make it an easy green escape, and the outdoor paths stay open into the evening.
image_source: VISITJEJU (제주관광공사) official photo - licence terms not stated
opening_hours: Outdoor gardens & paths: open year-round (official site says walkable until 23:00). Indoor halls: 09:00-18:00 (Mar-Nov), 09:00-17:00 (Dec-Feb)
closed_days: Outdoor: none. Indoor halls closed on Seollal and Chuseok (the day itself)

description_en: The province's main public art museum, a low concrete building with a reflecting pool set in green foothills on the road toward Hallasan. It shows Jeju and Korean modern art plus changing special exhibitions, and has a hall for painter Chang Ri-suok's donated works.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticketing ends 30 min before close); Jul-Sep 09:00-20:00. Temporary: during 2026 Jeju Biennale (Aug 25-Nov 15, 2026) 10:00-18:00 from Oct 1.
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public holiday, the next non-holiday weekday); Jan 1; Seollal; Chuseok

description_en: A shallow, calm white-sand beach with emerald water on Jeju's northeast coast, about 20 km east of the airport, backed by a lawn park and the green Seoubong hill. A paved seaside promenade and a small arched footbridge make it easy to stroll, and Seoubong's coastal trail is popular at sunset.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
opening_hours: 24h / always open. 2026 swimming season Jun 24-Sep 6, swimming 10:00-19:00 (no night swimming in 2026).

name_en: Jeju 4·3 Peace Park (Jeju 4·3 Peace Memorial Hall)
description_en: A large memorial park and museum on the lower slopes east of Jeju City that remembers the tens of thousands of civilians killed during the Jeju April 3rd Incident (1947-1954). The memorial hall tells the history through six themed galleries with multilingual commentary, while the grounds hold the memorial altar, victims' name stones, and burial-site monuments.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
opening_hours: Outdoor park: 24h / always open. Memorial Hall: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00).
closed_days: Park: none. Memorial Hall: 1st and 3rd Monday of each month (if a public/substitute holiday, the next non-holiday day).

description_en: A cool, shady forest of tall Japanese cedars on the lower slopes east of Jeju City, laced with gentle deck and mat-covered walking paths, a mineral spring and a pond. A steeper side trail climbs Jeolmul Oreum for views toward the sea.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown

description_en: A cluster of eight thatched-roof buildings near Jeju Port recreating the merchant inn run by Kim Man-deok, an 18th-century Jeju businesswoman remembered for using her fortune to feed islanders during a famine. Some buildings hold a small free exhibit on old Jeju life; the others work as a traditional tavern serving local dishes. The Kim Man-deok Memorial Hall is a short walk away.
closed_days: Mon (VisitJeju; weekly vs alternate-week Mondays conflicting)

description_en: Nexon's game museum in Jeju City reopened in May 2026 after a full renovation. The old computer-history museum is now a hands-on space about players and Nexon's online games, with playable arcade and co-op zones, a retro PC gaming archive, and a MapleStory-themed café in the basement.
opening_hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 (ticket sales close 17:30; Café MapleStory last order 17:30)
closed_days: Mon; Seollal (Lunar New Year's Day); Chuseok day

description_en: A huge open-air park and museum complex in the mid-mountain forest of Jocheon, dedicated to Jeju's volcanic stone culture and the island's creation myth of Seolmundae Halmang and her 500 sons. Walking routes link a sunken stone museum, outdoor stone-statue fields, a re-created thatched-roof village, and the Seolmundae Halmang Exhibition Hall that opened in 2025.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales close 17:00); no seasonal change listed
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public/substitute holiday, closed the next non-holiday day instead); Jan 1; Seollal day; Chuseok day; may also close temporarily for exhibit changes or bad weather

description_en: Jeju's largest traditional market, held only every five days near the airport, with about 1,000 stalls selling produce, fresh seafood, tangerines, local snacks and household goods. Locals do their real shopping here, and there is a section where elderly women sell their own produce rent-free.
opening_hours: Market days only, approx. 08:00-18:00 (per Korea Tourism Organization data); some guides say stalls close around 19:00. Mornings are busiest.
closed_days: Opens ONLY on dates ending in 2 or 7: the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of each month, whatever the weekday. Closed (no market) on all other dates. Holiday exceptions (e.g., Seollal/Chuseok) not confirmed.

description_en: A city-run nature park on the slopes of Geochin Oreum in Bonggae-dong where Jeju's wild roe deer live in the open. A fenced viewing area and small exhibition hall near the entrance make it easy to see deer up close, and a longer forest trail loops around the oreum with views toward Hallasan.
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, 골뱅이 (via Panoramio), CC BY-SA 3.0
opening_hours: Exhibition hall & permanent observation area (상시관찰원): 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00). Geochin Oreum observation trail: Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00); Nov-Feb 09:00-17:00 (tickets until 16:00). Entry may be limited by weather.

description_en: Jeju City's oldest downtown shopping street, once nicknamed Jeju's 'Myeong-dong', lined with clothing and shoe brand shops, cafés and small eateries. Part of it is a car-free pedestrian street, and it sits a short walk from Dongmun Market and Tapdong seafront. Nearby: about 80 m away is Jeju Central Underground Shopping Mall (제주 중앙지하상가), Jeju's only underground arcade, running beneath Jungang-ro from Dongmun Market to Gwandeokjeong with about 300 shops selling clothes, accessories and souvenirs, plus restaurants and rest areas - free to walk through, open 10:00-22:00 (varies by shop) and handy on rainy days.
image_source: 비짓제주 VISIT JEJU (제주관광공사) 제공 사진 - 공공누리 등 개방 라이선스 표시 확인 안 됨
opening_hours: Street always open; shop hours vary (roughly 10:00 to 18:00-22:00 depending on the shop)
closed_days: none (street open year-round; individual shops set their own days off)

description_en: A Yemeni/Middle Eastern restaurant run by a Yemeni chef and his Korean wife, serving mandi rice, kebab wraps, hummus and falafel, with a separately labelled vegan section and a prayer room.
closed_days: Wednesday (per Visit Jeju Muslim-friendly guide; HappyCow and Traveloka list different days, so confirm)

description_en: A small Thai-owned restaurant near Yongduam serving pad thai, rice-noodle soups and curries, where staff will make most dishes vegan on request.
A famous local soup house known for its thick Jeju-style bracken (gosari) and beef soup and for momguk seaweed-pork soup, served by the bowl from early morning.
closed_days: Listed as open year-round (연중무휴); holiday closures not confirmed

description_en: A long-running (since 2002) Jeju meat-noodle shop, now in a new building near Iho, known for pork-bone broth noodles topped with sliced boiled pork.
A large bakery café right on Hamdeok Beach, with sea-view terrace seating and coffee and pastries made with Jeju ingredients.
A busy local snack shop near Halla University known for cold yeolmu (young radish kimchi) noodles and anchovy-chili gimbap, with cheap single-portion dishes.
A quiet café in a converted old house with a hanok-style garden off Chilseong-ro, serving traditional teas, yakgwa and other Korean desserts, and coffee.

Jeju Monument No. 1: an altar on the site of the former Gyullim Seowon academy honoring five Joseon-era scholars and officials, exiled to or posted on Jeju, who advanced learning on the island. Nearby: about 80 m along the same lane is Jeju Fortress (제주성지), the old city wall, where roughly 150 m near Namsugak has been restored; most of the rest was dismantled in 1925-1928 to reclaim land at the port, so the two are easy to see together.

A spring-fed stream that runs through old downtown Jeju City past Dongmun Market to Jeju Port, lined with walking paths. The area is the start of Jeju Olle Route 18 and hosts the yearly Sanjicheon Festival.
A photography gallery made by joining and remodelling two old inn buildings beside Sanjicheon Stream, showing work by Jeju photographers and photographers who documented the island.
closed_days: Mon; public holidays; Apr 25 (foundation day); May 1 (Workers' Day)

description_en: A contemporary art museum in a former motel near Sanjicheon Stream that keeps traces of the old building while showing Korean and international contemporary art. One ticket covers this and the nearby Dongmun Motel 2.

A museum on the life of Kim Man-deok (1739-1812), a Jeju merchant who used her fortune to feed islanders during a famine, presented as Korea's first exhibition hall on the culture of sharing. Audio guides are available in English, Chinese and Japanese.
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok (if Mon is a public holiday, closed the next weekday instead)

description_en: A 136 m volcanic cone next to Sarabong with a cliffside path called Jangsuro that circles it, giving views over Jeju Port, passing ships and the sea. Rocks such as Goraegul cave sit at the foot of the northern cliffs.

A green park in central Jeju City with a wide lawn, tall trees, flower beds and spring cherry blossoms. It holds a monument to the 1988 Olympic torch arrival, a 1995 time capsule and memorials including the Jeju 4.3 Haewon Bangsatap.

The province's main performing-arts and exhibition venue, run by the Jeju Culture and Arts Promotion Agency, with a main hall, small theatre and exhibition rooms showing local artists. It is also home to the provincial dance troupe.
An old residential alley in Ildo 2-dong whose house walls have been covered with murals since 2008 public-art projects, keeping the look of old Jeju City.

Site of the seaside village of Gonheul-dong, which soldiers burned on 5-6 January 1949 during the Jeju April 3 Incident, killing many residents. The village was abandoned afterwards and is now a 4.3 memorial site on the coast east of Byeoldobong.
A roughly 220 m alley above Dongmun Market painted with murals of old Jeju and its scenery, close to the Jeju Fortress wall and Ohyeondan. Seeing all the paintings takes about 30 minutes.

Jeju's first school, a Joseon-era state Confucian academy founded in 1392 and moved to this Yongdam-dong site in 1827. Its halls, including Daeseongjeon (a national Treasure), Myeongnyundang and Gyeseongsa, still stand.

A contemporary art museum set in a former cinema in Jeju's old downtown near Tapdong, left largely unrenovated so traces of the old building remain. A 5th-floor cafe and shop look over the old town and Tapdong.

A long seafront plaza and promenade on the old-downtown coast, centered on the Tapdong Beach Stage outdoor amphitheater. Locals and visitors stroll here at night and catch buskers and events in summer.

A 60-year-old traditional market in the west of the old downtown, known for meat: buy cuts at the market's butcher shops and have them grilled at the meat restaurants in the market building for a table-setting fee. It also sells groceries, dried fish and fruit.

The seaside road (officially Seohaean-ro) running from near Yongduam Rock toward Dodubong along the coast north of the airport, part of Olle Route 17. It has small parks for stopping to look at the sea, night lighting on the water, and many cafes, hotels and raw-fish restaurants.

A long seaside park on the Yongdam coastal road with open sea views, lit up at night and on Olle Route 17. Poems and murals line its benches and seawall, and a Lorelei statue marks Jeju City's friendship with Germany's Loreley.
A free seaside leisure and sports park for Jeju residents beside the airport, with sports and convenience facilities; swimming and fishing are possible in summer. Expect aircraft noise.

A multi-purpose art space in the remodeled former Jeju National University Hospital building in the old downtown, on the site of a Joseon-era government office. Its galleries show painting, sculpture, video, installation and new-media art.
An old-downtown street where Jeju's annual spring king cherry blossom festival is held, with cafes and restaurants along the way.

A small harbor that Yongdam villagers made by breaking up the rocky shore, also called Dakkeune Port. Here you can see Deungmyeongdae, an old traditional lighthouse, and a spring-water well; the village emptied after the airport expanded.

The area around Jeju City's Plaza No. 7, popularly called Haetae Hill (Haetae Dongsan), where many people were killed during the Jeju April 3rd Incident. It is now a busy junction on the road from the airport to Sinjeju.
A stretch of the Yongdam-Iho coastal road near Jeju Airport whose seawall is painted in rainbow colors; a popular seaside photo and strolling spot.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

description_en: A car-free pedestrian street in Yeon-dong, Shin-Jeju, lined with restaurants, bars, clothing and souvenir shops; formerly called Baozen Street.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

name_en: Arboretum Theme Park (Night Market Street & LED Park)
description_en: An evening spot next to Halla Arboretum where a pine grove is lit with LED lights and a night market of food trucks, flea-market stalls and busking runs.
A low forested oreum (about 117 m relative height) in Ora-dong with a wooden-deck trail to the summit and a forest loop path midway, popular with locals for walks.
A small breakwater harbor between Yongduam Coastal Road and Iho Tewoo, near Jeju Airport, known for fishing boats and with restaurants and fishing shops nearby.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

description_en: A spring of cold, clear groundwater that is the symbol of Dodu village; in summer it feeds an outdoor pool, and there is also a small spring-water bathhouse.
A tiny harbor next to Iho Beach with sea-themed murals on the breakwater, a pavilion for resting, and views of the red and white horse lighthouses; popular with anglers at night.
A roughly 1.15 km coastal road from Iho Tewoo Beach to Aljakji pebble beach, part of the Olle Route 17 area, with open sea views especially at sunset.
An indoor immersive media-art exhibition themed around a 1980s neighborhood supermarket where a mysterious door has drained Jeju's colors.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, via ktriptips.com mirror; 공공누리 type not shown on mirror)

description_en: A Jeju April 3rd (4·3) heritage site in Ora-dong, where the May 1, 1948 'Ora-ri arson incident' helped wreck the peace talks; a village walking route marks the history.

Jeju black pork restaurant opened in 2006, known for thick geun-gogi cuts (neck and pork belly) grilled over yeontan briquettes. Staff grill the meat at your table; it is served with meljeot anchovy sauce, and kimchi stew is a popular finish.

Long-running local restaurant known for momguk, Jeju's thick soup of pork broth simmered with mojaban (gulfweed) seaweed. It also serves dombe-gogi (sliced boiled pork), momguk noodles and squid sashimi.
opening_hours: Late-night; last order 03:00 (opening time not stated by source)

description_en: Old-style Jeju home-cooking restaurant popular with locals and tourists, where you can hear the Jeju dialect around you. Its specialty is gakjaegi-guk, a soybean-paste soup made with horse mackerel; it also serves seafood hot pot.

Seafood restaurant in Dodu-dong near Jeju Airport, run by a haenyeo (woman diver) owner and her family. Famous for abalone mulhoe (cold raw seafood soup with a distinctive soybean-paste broth) and abalone/seafood hot pot.
Popular early-morning restaurant with a single menu item: beef haejangguk, a hearty Korean soup often eaten as a hangover cure. Lines are common; just tell the staff how many people.
Restaurant serving Jeju home-style set meals inspired by haenyeo recipes, centered on braised wild rockfish from its own fishing boat. Most ingredients and wrap vegetables are from Jeju.

name_en: e-Geumdonji Tong-Galchi Jorim Jeju Airport Main Branch
description_en: Restaurant near Jeju Airport specializing in braised whole hairtail (galchi jorim), a classic Jeju seafood dish, plus grilled hairtail.
Noodle restaurant so popular that even locals line up, serving kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) in a deep broth made with bomal (Jeju sea snails) and seaweed.
Evening restaurant near Jeju City Hall known for raw mackerel sashimi; live mackerel is prepared quickly so it tastes fresh and rich rather than fishy. Also serves braised hairtail.

Abalone specialty restaurant with over 20 years of history on the Tapdong waterfront, known for abalone porridge and abalone hot-stone-pot rice. Breakfast is available and there is a large parking area.
opening_hours: Breakfast available; last order 20:00 (opening time not stated)

description_en: Jeju home-style seafood restaurant in Ido-dong ('gaetgeot' means seafood in Jeju dialect), known for clear sea urchin seaweed soup and bomal (sea snail) soup, served with side dishes of locally gathered seaweed.

name_en: Malgogi Research Lab Jeju Airport Branch
description_en: Restaurant near Jeju Mokgwana offering approachable takes on Jeju horse meat, such as horse meat sausage (the signature), horse meat sushi and rice bowls.
opening_hours: Break 14:30-17:30; last order 21:00 (opening time not stated)

description_en: Small, inexpensive eatery in Boseong Market known for bingtteok, a Jeju snack of thin buckwheat crepe rolled around seasoned radish, made with 100% Jeju buckwheat.
Bakery near Jeju Sports Complex selling Jeju-style barley bread: plain barley bread, red bean barley bread and mugwort bread. Bulk and parcel orders are possible.
Cafe in a downtown cafe street, famous for green tea bingsu: shaved ice with green tea powder, injeolmi rice cake and nuts, topped with a tower of green tea ice cream. Also serves coffee and cakes.

A representative mountain wetland on the Hallasan plateau, with more than 16 scattered wetland areas linked by wooden nature trails. Information boards along the trails describe the local wildlife and plants.

The first national road opened in Jeju, linking Jeju City and Seogwipo. For about 1.2 km, evergreen and deciduous trees arch over the winding road to form a forest tunnel. The road is narrow with many curves, so drive slowly.

An indoor interactive exhibition with five themed zones on tangerines, stone, Gotjawal forest, sea and wind, featuring media art, sculptures and photo spaces. A school-themed indoor horror experience is also on site.
opening_hours: K-Island Jeju / School Ghost Story in Jeju / Running Man Jeju Branch: 09:00-19:00 (last entry 18:00); Tangerine Kart: 09:00-18:00 (maintenance 12:00-13:00)

description_en: A low oreum hill in Songdang-ri, Gujwa-eup, with a horseshoe-shaped crater, forested slopes, and wild flowers such as white and pink hepatica.

A horseshoe-shaped oreum in Pyoseon-myeon whose peak splits into two, giving it a shape like a pair of scissors. Its side peaks are hidden in thickets without marked trails, so hikers should wear long pants and take care.

A wind farm built on the Gasiri community pasture in Pyoseon-myeon, the first in Korea planned with local residents' participation. Large turbines stand over open grassland, and nearby canola fields are popular for drives in spring.

A short oreum in Daejeong-eup with a horseshoe-shaped crater open to the southwest. It is easy to climb, and a farm road reaches near the summit. It offers views of Mosulpo Oreum and the Daejeong area.

A tangerine orchard in Namwon-eup where visitors can pick tangerines and taste them fresh. It has appeared in various TV programs and is known for its good-tasting fruit grown with a special cultivation method.
closed_days: none; closed Feb to Aug (call ahead before visiting)

description_en: The fourth largest of Jeju's islands, Gapado is shaped like a stingray seen from above. Visitors can walk around the whole island in one to two hours, and a green barley festival is held each spring.

Located on Gapado, the fourth largest of Jeju's islands and shaped like a stingray from above. Visitors can walk around the island in about one to two hours, and the island is known for its green barley fields.
A parasitic volcanic cone with a cone-shaped crater. It is named after a rock on the summit. The northern slope is gentle and wooded, while the southern ridge is steep.

A natural pond at the foot of Namsanbong near Seongeup, said never to dry up even in drought. A small inner pond is surrounded by a round stone wall, and old stepping stones once used to reach the water remain. Nearby: Uri Horse Riding Ground (우리승마장, sight, about 80 m).

A three-generation studio at the foot of Sanbangsan in Sagye-ri that grows persimmons, makes and sells gal-ot traditional Jeju clothing, and offers natural dyeing experiences. A stone hareubang statue stands at the entrance.

A side volcanic cone in Donggwang-ri, Andeok-myeon, with a gentle slope and a horseshoe crater opening to the northeast, covered by pine forest. A 30-minute walk along a grassy trail leads to the summit, with views of Hallasan and Sanbangsan on clear days.
An oreum in Gasiri, Pyoseon-myeon, with a horseshoe-shaped crater opening to the southwest. The Gasinnae stream runs along its west side, and the quiet village of Gasiri lies nearby.

A clear stream in Gangjeong village, the southernmost village in Seogwipo, fed by natural rock water from Hallasan that flows all year. Visitors cool off here in summer, and ayu fish and mandarin ducks can be seen.

A port on Seogwipo's south coast beside a naval base, known for its sunrise and sunset views. The Hae Oreum Noeul Walkway runs along the coast, decorated with murals, and offers views of Gunsan Oreum and Sanbangsan.

A parasitic volcanic cone in Pyoseon-myeon with a flat top and a forested southeast slope planted with pine and cedar. Other slopes are grassland with wildflowers. Its name is said to come from its dog-like shape.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (some areas may be restricted; call ahead)

description_en: A cone-shaped volcanic hill beside Georin Saseum, separated from it by a steep mountain pass. A roadside rest area on the slope gives views of the southwest coast from Seogwipo to Mosulpo. A memorial cemetery for victims of a past tragedy lies on its south side.

A parasitic volcanic cone named after deer that once lived here, with a horseshoe crater opening to the west. Its slopes are covered in trees. Visitors can hike, enjoy city views of Seogwipo, and walk forest trails.
An oreum whose shape resembles a door latch, and whose surroundings were once home to many wildcats. A viewing platform on the summit overlooks Seogwipo city.

A parasitic volcanic cone that surrounds Seogwipo's new downtown, with a shallow round crater at the top. From the summit, visitors can see the sea and the Seogwipo area, and it is known for night views of the coast.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (some access may be restricted; call ahead)

description_en: A forest in Gwangpyeong-ri, Andeok-myeon, created to honor nature when the village lost during a past tragedy was rebuilt in 1955. Visitors can rest in hammocks and on benches among the trees.

name_en: Gosan Ilgwa Coastal Road (Ilgwa-ri Coastal Road)
description_en: A roughly 12 km coastal road from Chagwido Port through Sindo-ri to Ilgwa crossroads, also called the Sunset Coastal Road. Along the way, visitors pass fishing village scenes, Suwolbong Peak and the Eoreol coast.
A nature trail starting from the Gosali spring in Harye-ri, the first village at the foot of Hallasan's south side. The trail follows an ecological stream and shows the Gotjawal forest of Jeju.

A volcanic beach between Seongsan Ilchulbong and Seopjikoji, where Jeju Olle Course 1 ends and Course 2 begins. At low tide, rock formations and green moss appear, and sunrise can be photographed beside Seongsan Ilchulbong.

An oreum on the border between Gasiri and Gyorae-ri, with a steep, narrow slope and a horseshoe-shaped crater. Its slopes have natural forest and planted cedar and pine, and spring brings wildflowers to the summit.

A small port where only small boats dock, on Jeju Olle Course 6 between Soccheonji and Bomok Port. It is the closest point to Seopseom islet and a popular spot for sunset photos, snorkeling and diving.

A parasitic volcanic cone next to Nandeureu village on the Seogwipo coast, and the largest of its kind on Jeju. A paved road leads up, taking about 30 minutes to walk. From the top, visitors can see Hallasan, Jungmun, Mara Island and Sanbangsan.
A glass and concrete building on Seopjikoji by Japanese architect Tadao Ando. It houses a bakery cafe and a small goods shop, with sharp straight lines that reach out toward the sea.

A tangerine farm where visitors pick seasonal citrus each month from September to mid-May and can take home about 1 kg. Varieties change through the year, and visitors can taste the fruit fresh in the field.

An experience farm in Andeok-myeon offering handmade fruit syrup classes, with tangerine picking in autumn and winter and Hallabong picking in late winter. The farm is tidy and decorated with photo spots, and no reservation is needed to visit.
opening_hours: 11:00-17:00 (varies by season; check website or call)
closed_days: Tue, Wed, Thu (varies by season; check website or call)

description_en: A place to walk with camels in Pyoseon-myeon, using camels imported from Australia for the first time in Korea. Safety staff accompany guests, and reservations are accepted only for package tours or groups. Nearby: Jeju Arirang Hon (제주아리랑 혼, museum, about 30 m).
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 표선면 번영로 2564-21 (포니밸리) 내 낙타트레킹
closed_days: none (open year-round); check in advance if raining

description_en: A coastal cliff in Namwon-eup, about 30 m high and 200 m long, with two natural sea caves carved by waves. A 2 km walking trail, a viewing deck and rest facilities run along the cliff top. Nearby: Kumho Resort Jeju Aquana (금호리조트 제주아쿠아나, park, about 90 m).

A natural park in Daejeong-eup with flowers and trees through the seasons, including daffodils, plum, magnolia and camellia. Stone features, an artificial waterfall and an artificial lake are arranged in the park, and a pavilion in the pond is especially beautiful at sunset.

A roughly 12 km coastal road from Ilgwa-ri to Sindo 1-ri in Daejeong-eup, known for its sunset views. It is part of the Jeju bicycle road, shared by bicycles and cars, and is close to the main Jeju ring road.

A natural beach where freshwater springs flow into the sea, mixing salt and fresh water. A dike has been built to create a swimming pool and shower area for summer. Slippers or sandals are recommended to prevent injuries in the water.
opening_hours: Weekdays 10:00-19:00; weekends 10:00-19:00 (hours may change; call ahead)

description_en: A hydrangea garden in Wolpyeong-dong, Seogwipo, open during the bloom season near the Dongbyeongdeul bus stop. It has houses, benches, tables and small cabins as photo spots. Check the official SNS channel before visiting, as opening depends on the season and weather.
closed_days: none; open daily for the first month after opening; check official SNS for opening dates

description_en: A small port at the start of Jeju Olle Course 4, next to Pyoseon Haebichi Beach, the largest white sand beach on Jeju. A white lighthouse stands at the end of a path leading out to sea, and boats and views of the coast make it a good sunrise spot.

A round, steep oreum whose shape is said to resemble a deer, with a circular crater on the summit. Its slopes are covered in pine and cedar, and azaleas grow near the top. In autumn, a wide field of pampas grass draws many visitors.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (some areas may be closed; call ahead)

description_en: An oreum behind the Seongsan-eup office with gentle slopes and an oval crater near the summit. Most slopes are planted with cedar and pine, and remains of a Joseon-era beacon tower are on the summit. Some parts are private land, so call before visiting.

A wetland park on Olle Course 8 in Sangye-dong, Seogwipo. It is fed by the Daewangsu spring, whose flow stays steady even in drought. The park is a firefly protection area with an ecology experience center, and it is known for cherry blossoms in spring.

A Catholic holy site in Daejeong-eup where Jeong Nan-ju Maria, Jeju's first Catholic, is buried. She was exiled to Jeju and taught local residents with her learning despite hardship. Villagers built a memorial space for her, which later became a pilgrimage site.

A traditional Confucian school in Andeok-myeon, first built in 1416 and moved to its current site in 1653. It has a shrine hall and lecture hall in the traditional layout, with a simple, restrained design reflecting local history.

The start of Jeju Olle Course 9 and end of Course 8, Daepyeong Port is used by fishing boats. In the Goryeo period it was used to ship Jeju horses. A coastal path from the port leads to Parksugi Cliff, a 100 m high cliff. Nearby: Jeju Olle Course 9: Daepyeong-Hwasun Olle ([제주올레 9코스] 대평-화순 올레, sight, about 80 m).

A port in Daepo-dong on Jeju Olle Course 8, between Wolpyeong and Daepyeong. Visitors can take yacht tours or ride a jet boat that turns 360 degrees. The area is near the columnar joints of Jisatgae Coast and Yakcheonsa Temple. Nearby: Jeju Jet (Jungmun) (제주제트(중문), sight, about 80 m); JM Grand Blue Yacht (제이엠그랑블루요트, sight, about 70 m).

A coastal area in Daepo-dong with the columnar joints of Jisatgae Coast and Yakcheonsa Temple nearby. Yacht tours and 360-degree jet boat rides are available, and the coast sits along Jeju Olle Course 8.

A compound oreum with two craters on the border between Donggwang-ri and Geumak-ri. It is reached through a cattle ranch gate, and one crater is a deep horseshoe with forest while the other is a funnel-shaped crater at the eastern summit.

A valley in Seogwipo with emerald water and evergreen forest, where the 5 m high Wonang Falls splits into two streams. A 20-minute walk from the entrance leads to the falls, a popular summer spot for cooling off.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (access may be restricted in rain or high water)

description_en: An ecological art garden in Namwon-eup, opened in spring 2024 after 14 years of clearing wasteland. It features bonsai and stone art, more than 120 tree species and 200 wildflower species, with the sea to the south and Hallasan to the north.

A rural experience village in Donggwang-ri, Andeok-myeon, on the mid-mountain slopes below Hallasan, surrounded by oreum and forest. It has Jeju 4.3 Incident sites such as a memorial stone and a refuge cave, and offers farm activities like sledding and kite flying.

A camellia-themed farm garden in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, with white European-style buildings and camellia trees. Camellias bloom from November to February, and visitors can enjoy drinks and desserts in the cafe or take photos at a window photo spot.
closed_days: none; closed every year from March to October

description_en: A small fishing harbor in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, with a historic salt-making site and stone-walled village lanes. Visitors can stroll past the stone walls and fields and rest at a shelter inside the village.

A small park in Beopwhan-dong, Seogwipo, on the boundary between the Beopwhan and Gangjeong villages, with a view of Beomseom islet. Walking through the park, visitors see the sea on one side, with Seopseom and Munseom islets further away.

A double volcanic cone on the border of Sungsan-eup, Seogwipo, and Gujwa-eup, Jeju City, with cliffs along its eastern and southern rims. Its northwest slope is flat grassland, and the crater is covered with reeds.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (some oreum are private land and access may be restricted; call ahead)

description_en: A volcanic oreum in Gasi-ri, Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, with three craters and six peaks, known for its silver grass in autumn. Visitors walk across a wide plain and quiet paths, and the climb to the summit takes about 30 minutes.

A large night digital theme park in Seogwipo where visitors walk after dark through immersive experience zones. Its nine zones use media art and holograms to tell a story of the moon, with a Lunar Village and the Lunarian language.
opening_hours: 19:00-24:00 (last entry 23:00); hours change by season, call ahead

description_en: Regular passenger ferries serve Marado, South Korea's southernmost island, and Gapado. Ferries depart from Unjin Port, and visitors can choose Marado or Gapado, or visit both on the same day, depending on season and weather. Nearby: Unjin Port (운진항, sight, about 60 m).
closed_days: none (open year-round); check the schedule on the website

description_en: The Marado Lighthouse stands near the southern tip of South Korea, a white octagonal concrete tower 16 m tall, first built in 1915. Its light flashes every 10 seconds and can be seen from about 48 km away, and it sits beside Marado Catholic Church, a popular photo spot.
opening_hours: Marado Lighthouse 09:00-18:00; Unjin Port passenger terminal 09:40-15:50; ferry to Marado / Sanisudong Port 09:20-16:10; advance phone inquiry required

description_en: Marado, South Korea's southernmost island, is shaped like a sweet potato. It is mostly flat, with cliffs on its east side near the lighthouse. A boat from Unjin Port takes about 30 minutes, and silver grass covers the island in autumn.

A passenger ferry to Marado, South Korea's southernmost island, with views of the clear sea around Jeju. The crossing from the pier takes about 30 minutes each way, and the total time depends on how long you stay on the island.

A parasitic volcanic oreum in Sungsan-eup, Seogwipo, with a horseshoe-shaped crater and a well-kept trail along its ridge. Visitors can walk a cypress forest path, and a campground with a lawn lies on its western slope.
opening_hours: Some areas have restricted access; call ahead before visiting

description_en: An oreum in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, with a horseshoe-shaped crater open to the east. Its rim is said to look like a mother holding a child, which gives the oreum its name. Cedar forest covers the slopes halfway up, and grassland covers the summit.

A wetland oreum in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, whose crater, about 40 m deep, holds a marsh. Its forest trails through the Ramsar wetland stay cool in summer, and the misty scenery on rainy days is especially atmospheric.

A lava cave in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, with a total length of 1,700 m, of which 365 m is open to visitors. Its entrance formed when the ceiling collapsed, and inside you can see lava flow structures on the basalt walls. Nearby: Ilchul Land (일출랜드, park, about 60 m).

Cliffs in Daepyeong-ri, Seogwipo, with coastal scenery similar to the columnar joints of Jungmun and the cliffs of the Aewol coastal road. The start of Jeju Olle Trail Route 9 climbs above the cliffs through pine woods, overlooking Daepyeong Harbor.

A fossil site along the coast from Sangmo-ri in Daejeong-eup to Sagye-ri in Andeok-myeon, with human, deer, bird and elephant footprints preserved in rock. Designated a natural monument in 2005, it is the only place in Asia with human footprint fossils.

A church in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, designed by the Korean-Japanese architect Itami Jun, based on the story of Noah's Ark. Built in 2009 of wood and zinc, it appears to float on an artificial pond, and it is a popular photo spot.
opening_hours: Exterior: 24h / always open (lawn closed during services). Interior: Tue and Thu 09:00-17:00; Wed 13:00-17:00; Fri 09:00-14:00; closed at other times. Check service times on the website; call for details.

description_en: A broad, round oreum in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, named for the many medicinal herbs that grow in its crater. Visitors walk through Seongeup Pasture and climb for about 30 minutes to reach the summit, where a bowl-shaped crater appears.

A Buddhist temple in Seogwipo and a branch temple of Gwaneumsa in Jeju. It may date back to the Goryeo period or earlier, and excavations show it was rebuilt in the 13th century under Mongol rule, when it was especially important.

A harbor also called Maksukgae, named after General Choi Yeong, who camped his troops here in the late Goryeo period. It lies on Jeju Olle Trail Route 7 and offers views of several islets, plus a statue of haenyeo divers at Female Diver Plaza.

A group of three oreum peaks east of Cheonjeyeon Valley in Jungmun, named Dong Oreum, Seot Oreum and Manjiseom Oreum. The forest holds rare plants and is a designated natural monument, and Jeju Olle Trail Route 8 passes through it.

A farm in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, whose name is a Jeju dialect word meaning windy field. Visitors can see barley, buckwheat, tulips, canola, hydrangeas and lavender, plus chickens, cows, sheep and goats, and a cafe inside the farm. Nearby: Cafe Boreumwat (카페보롬왓, cafe, about 10 m).

A small fishing village between Soesokkak and Oedolgae on Jeju Olle Trail Route 6, about 4 km southeast of central Seogwipo. Visitors can watch sunrise and sunset from Jejigi Oreum, a small hill east of the harbor.

A harbor known for jari-mulhoe, a cold raw fish soup made with damselfish, and a damselfish festival held each May. Hallasan rises behind it, and the sunset over the islets of Munseom and Seopseom is a highlight, along with a stair path that is a popular photo spot.

A natural forest recreation area in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, surrounded by several oreum and left in its natural state. Its cedar forests over 50 years old, pine woods and natural forest offer seasonal scenery, from azaleas in spring to snow in winter.
opening_hours: Summer (Mar-Oct) 08:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00); winter (Nov-Feb) 09:00-17:00 (last entry 16:00); lodging check-in 15:00, check-out 12:00; camping check-in 13:00, check-out 12:00

description_en: A night theme park in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, built on the site of Jeju Folk Village. Visitors travel through theme zones with parades, characters from Jeju creation myths and a large multimedia show, led by Super Halmang Mago, a legendary guardian. Nearby: Jeju Folk Village (제주민속촌, museum, about 10 m).
opening_hours: Summer (Mar-Oct) 19:00-23:00 (last entry 22:30); winter (Nov-Feb) 18:00-22:00 (last entry 21:30); closes early in bad weather
closed_days: none (open year-round); may change with rain or other weather, check the website or call

description_en: An edutainment theme park in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, where children learn through play with Pororo and friends. It has various rides and character-based programs designed to stimulate emotion and learning.

A small park beside Sindo Harbor in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, with wide sea views where visitors can watch wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins from land. Information signs about this protected species stand in the park.

A small, quiet beach at the foot of Sanbangsan in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, where swimming is not allowed. From Jeju Olle Trail Route 10, visitors can see Sanbangsan, Hallasan and Yongmeori Coast, and at low tide unusual volcanic rocks appear. Nearby: Zen Hideaway (젠하이드어웨이, cafe, about 80 m).

An oreum on the south side of the Seongpanak trail to the top of Hallasan, on the border of Namwon-eup and Jocheon-eup. Its shallow crater lake sits at about 1,300 m; in the rainy season the crater fills with water, and in winter the lake freezes.
opening_hours: Access may be restricted; call for details

description_en: A cave temple halfway up Sanbangsan in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, set in a sea-carved cave about 150 m above sea level. The Buddha statue is enshrined in the innermost part, and the temple is said to date back to the Goryeo period.

A small amusement park in the Sanbangsan and Yongmeori Coast tourist area in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, with a tall viking ride, carousel, mini viking, rail sled, baseball batting cage and shooting range. It is popular with families and school groups.

Sanbangsan is a dome-shaped volcano rising above the flat southwestern plain of Jeju, one of the island's three major mountains along with Hallasan and Seongsan Ilchulbong. According to legend, the Jade Emperor threw a peak from Hallasan to form it. Nearby: Sanbangsan Rapeseed Flower Field (산방산유채꽃밭, sight, about 10 m).
opening_hours: 09:00-17:50 (last entry 17:30); only the trail from the Sanbangsan ticket office to Sanbanggulsa is open; times may change or close depending on sunset and weather, so check before visiting

description_en: A sightseeing cruise from Hwasun Harbor that runs about one hour past Sanbangsan, Yongmeori Coast, Songaksan, Marado and Gapado. It sails three times a day.

A small parasitic volcano west of central Seogwipo, whose three peaks are said to resemble plum blossoms. Terraced orchards cover its slopes, and the summit has an octagonal pavilion where Canopus, a star linked to longevity, can be seen in winter.

An arboretum of about 264,000 square meters in Seogwipo, at 400 m altitude, with views of Hallasan and the sea. It holds native Jeju plants and century-old trees, plus 16 themed gardens including a medicinal plant garden and a secret garden.
opening_hours: Mar-Sep: 09:00-19:00 (ticket sales end 18:00; Cafe Nugini 09:30-19:00; Korean restaurant 11:00-18:00). Oct-Feb: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales end 17:00; Cafe Nugini 09:00-18:00; Korean restaurant 11:00-18:00)

description_en: A cable-stayed footbridge linking Seogwipo Port and the uninhabited island of Saeseom, designed after a traditional Jeju raft and lit with LEDs. From the bridge you can see Seogwipo harbor, Munseom, Beomseom and Hallasan, and the island has walking paths through a protected warm-temperate forest. Nearby: Seogwipo Shellfish Fossil Site (서귀포 패류화석산지, park, about 70 m); Saeseom Park (새섬공원, park, about 70 m); Seogwipo Cruise New Paradise (서귀포유람선 뉴파라다이스호, heritage site, about 10 m).
opening_hours: 24h / always open (lighting hours apply; call for details)

description_en: A cultural complex inside the Jeju Center of the National Herbal Medicine Resources Center in Seogwipo, with exhibits and hands-on programs about herbal medicine. It has two floors and a rooftop healing garden, and visitors can join workshops such as herbal specimen framing, tea ceremony and terrarium making.
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok holidays; other days set by the center director for visitor safety, such as natural disasters

description_en: A small island off the coast near Jeju World Cup Stadium in Gangjeong-dong, Seogwipo, which can be reached on foot at low tide when the sea parts. Visitors dig for clams and octopus, and the tidal split is most pronounced during spring tides at full and new moon.
opening_hours: Available at low tide (check tide times before visiting)

description_en: A quiet, privately run tea plantation on the slopes of Hallasan at about 250 m, growing Jeju green tea. It has tree-lined paths, camellias, basalt sculptures and views of Hallasan. Shade covers are placed around May for the matcha harvest, which can limit viewing, so checking before your visit is recommended.

A Joseon-era defensive fortification, one of the Three Castles and Nine Garrisons of Jeju, first built around 1439 and moved to its current site in 1590. Parts of its original walls still survive as stone walls used by the village. Nearby: Soldongsan Pork Noodles (솔동산고기국수, restaurant, about 80 m).

name_en: Seogwipo Gasiri Village (Noksan-ro Canola Flower Road)
description_en: A 10 km scenic road through Gasiri Village in Seogwipo, lined with canola flowers and cherry blossoms, with views of Hallasan. It has been named one of Korea's 100 most beautiful roads, and nearby are a wind farm and a pony experience park. Nearby: Myeongmun Gasiri Restaurant (명문가시리식당, restaurant, about 100 m); Gasi Restaurant (가시식당, restaurant, about 40 m).

The former residence of scholar Kim Jeonghui (Chusa), who lived in exile here for nine years, from 1840 to 1848. The original house burned in 1948 and was rebuilt in 1984 based on historical research. Kim was a master of inscriptions and calligraphy, and his Chusa style is widely known. Nearby: Jeju Chusa Museum (제주 추사관, museum, about 30 m).
closed_days: none; closed on Jan 1 and on Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A rural experience village in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, run as an information village, where citrus orchards overlook the sea. It is the only village in Jeju where the entire village lies within 500 m of the coast.

An eco-village in Seogwipo with striking coastal scenery, where about 80% of households are farms. Traditional rural and fishing life is well preserved, with fireflies, many wildlife species, prehistoric sites and old place names still in use.

A calm village in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, below Andeok Valley, named for a field stretching to the sea where the Dragon King appeared. A red lighthouse with a statue of a girl stands by the harbor next to Baksugijeong Cliffs. Nearby: Jeju Haejone Bomal Seonggae Specialty Restaurant (제주해조네 보말성게전문점, restaurant, about 50 m).

A healing forest in Seogwipo at 320 to 760 m altitude, with subtropical, temperate and boreal forests, including cypress forests averaging over 60 years old, among the best in Korea. It is linked to nearby health care and tourism facilities.

Hanon Crater is Korea's only maar, a crater formed when underground gas or steam burst through the ground rather than by lava. It is an oval volcanic cone about 1.8 km by 1.3 km, with rice paddies on its flat floor.
opening_hours: [Hanon Crater] 24h / always open; [Hanon Crater Visitor Center] 09:00-18:00
closed_days: none; Visitor Center closed on public holidays

description_en: A natural recreation forest on the southwestern slopes of Hallasan, with dense cypress groves and forest-bathing trails. It offers walking paths, camping grounds, a lookout, a lawn and playgrounds, with seasonal scenery from azaleas to snow.
opening_hours: Recreation forest 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00); lodging check-in 15:00, check-out 12:00 the next day

description_en: A park on Jeju Olle Trail Route 6 that links Oendolgae rock with the coastal trail. Visitors can stroll, rest, and read stone inscriptions of poems and song lyrics about Seogwipo, among ponds and plants near Cheonjiyeon Falls.

Korea's southernmost port, where Hallasan helps keep the sea calm for most of the year except summer. Visitors can take a submarine tour or a cruise and jet boat ride, and see islands such as Munseom and Saeseom.
A garden displaying seokbujak, art pieces made by growing wild orchids and other plants on porous volcanic rock. The garden was opened to share the story of Jeju's natural environment.

name_en: Seokyewon Boncho Foot Bath Seongsan Branch
description_en: A self-service foot bath therapy using natural ingredients such as cosmetic sea salt, peppermint oil, and herbal medicinal water. It offers a place to rest tired feet after a long day of travel.

A Korean Taego Order Buddhist temple set against the coastal cliffs and sea caves of Namwon Keunneong. Founded in 1942, it was briefly abandoned after the 1948 Jeju April 3 Incident and later rebuilt.

An arched steel bridge in Jungmun-dong linking Cheonjeyeon Falls with the Jungmun resort area. Sculptures of seven fairies decorate its sides, and 34 stone lanterns along the railings light it at night.
A headland shaped like the tip of a nose, jutting out from the coast of Sinyang-ri in Seongsan-eup. Visitors follow a concrete road from the village to the tip, with wide sea views along the way.

A volcanic hill in Sangmo-ri, Daejeong-eup, with a Japanese-era anti-aircraft gun position on its summit and a massacre site from the Jeju 4.3 Incident on its southern slope. Many visitors come here to learn history.
A 180-meter volcanic cone formed about 5,000 years ago by an underwater eruption, now connected to land by sand and gravel. Its summit crater is famous for sunrise views.
opening_hours: Nov-Feb 06:00-18:00 (ticket sales end 17:00); Mar, Apr, Sep, Oct 05:00-19:00 (ticket sales end 18:00); May-Aug 04:30-20:00 (ticket sales end 19:00)
closed_days: Mon (1st Monday of each month); closed the next day if that Monday is a public holiday

description_en: A park beside Gwangchigi Beach with a walking path, a grassy meadow, and stone benches facing the sea, with views of Seongsan Ilchulbong. It sits on Jeju Olle Trail Route 1 and is a good rest stop for walkers.

A Catholic church that became a parish in 1973, praised as having the most scenic setting of any church in Korea, with Seongsan Ilchulbong and the sea in view. Its modern tiled roof appears cut open on one side, and its bell tower is lined with blue tiles.

A green tea farm on volcanic soil, with a cafe selling green tea rice cakes and ice cream. Visitors can try a foot bath and go-karting, and a small cave lies behind the tea fields. Nearby: Seongeup Nokcha Cave (성읍녹차동굴, sight, about 60 m); Oneul-eun Kart Racing (오늘은카트레이싱, sight, about 30 m); Oneul-eun Nokcha Hanjan (오늘은녹차한잔, cafe, about 60 m).

A preserved folk village at the foot of Hallasan that was the county seat of Jeongui during the Joseon period. It has traditional houses, a Confucian school, old government offices, and dolhareubang stone statues.
A very small harbor in Wimi-ri, Namwon-eup, named for its shape resembling a resting cow. It is known for plenty of small sea snails and calm, beautiful water, and attracts anglers and photographers.

A quiet beach on Jeju's southeast coast with silver sand and gentle, warm shallow water, popular with families. Visitors can catch sea snails and sea urchins. It is not an official swimming beach, so there are no lifeguards in summer.

A volcanic cliff of columnar joints on the Songsan-dong coast in Seogwipo, where fresh spring water flows out. The spring water feeds an outdoor open-air bath, and sea, forest, and stream all meet here.

A 1969 building shaped like a conch, set on a coastal cliff near Sojeongbang Falls in Seogwipo. It is now a book cafe with one side of glass facing the sea, and it hosts photo and art exhibitions. Nearby: Sojeongbang Falls (소정방폭포, sight, about 10 m).
A park with a sculpture path, a violin-playing dinosaur statue, flower zones, a kids' zone, and a camellia garden. A free mini train takes visitors around the walking trail.

A pool surrounded by rock formations on the coast of Bomok, said to resemble a miniature Heaven Lake on Baekdu Mountain. It is on Jeju Olle Trail Route 6, and its water is so clean that creatures found only in pristine water live here.
A recreation area with a forested valley that runs down to the sea. Visitors can walk the forest trails, rest at benches and pavilions, and see Beom Island. Children can splash in the shallow water.

A volcanic hill in central Seogwipo with views of Hallasan and the city. Pine, cedar, and cypress forests cover its slopes. Residents walk here, and tourists visit for the cypress forest and Hallasan views.

A hill on the southern coast of Daejeong-eup with 99 small peaks and a rare double crater. Walking its gentle paths, you can see grazing horses, Gapado, and the Hyeongje Islands, and on clear days Marado.
A 2.8 km circular trail around Songaksan, with gentle slopes that are good for families and pets. On clear days you can see Gapado, the Hyeongje Islands, and Marado.

Artificial caves dug into the Songaksan coastal cliff by the Japanese military in early 1945, with 15 tunnels built using forced labor from Jeju residents. Entry is currently banned due to collapse risk.
A deep estuary in Hahyo-dong, Seogwipo, where fresh river water mixes with seawater to form a deep pool. Lava-formed rock formations and pine forests frame its scenic views.
opening_hours: Estuary: 24h / always open; experiences: summer 09:00-18:00, winter 09:00-17:00 (suspended in bad weather)

description_en: A farm next to Soesokkak with a unique museum and vintage cafe inside a Hallabong greenhouse. Visitors can see farm tools, traditional Jeju timber, and an arch tunnel, and try citrus picking.

A 5.3 km one-way forest trail from the Mulyeongari Oreum side to the summit of Mahuni Oreum, through untouched primeval forest, cedar groves, and Jeju gotjawal. The walk takes 3-4 hours, so bring water and food.

A small Taego Order temple between Cheonjeyeon Falls and Beritneoreum in Jungmun, founded by the monk Bang Donghwa, who led the 1918 Muo Dharma Court anti-Japanese uprising. It is on Jeju Olle Trail Route 8.

A large pond on the Susan plain in Seongsan-eup, used for watering horses and cattle and as drinking water for residents. It is believed to date back to the Goryeo period, when Jeju was a horse-breeding site.
A cone-shaped volcano at the foot of Hallasan with a standing stone at its center. Its slopes are covered with planted pine and cedar forest.

A hill on the walking path between the Shilla and Parnas hotels in Jungmun, where the final scene of the 1999 film 'Swiri' was filmed. Visitors can sit on the Swiri bench and take photos of Jungmun Saekdal Beach and the sea.

name_en: Poet Lee Saengjin Poem Stone Park
description_en: An outdoor park on the coast of Seongsanpo with 20 poems by the poet Lee Saengjin carved in marble. Seongsan Ilchulbong is on one side and Udo Island on the other.
A harbor on Jeju Olle Trail Route 12, known for wild dolphins that can be seen from a stone viewing platform in the small park. Nearby are round lava pools holding seawater, small fish, and octopus.
A stone coastal wall built to block invaders arriving by sea, with about 600 m remaining on the south shore of Sinsan Ranch. The historical record Namsarok called it the 'Great Wall of Tamna'.
A crescent-shaped beach next to Seopjikoji in Seongsan, with calm, sheltered waves that are safe for children. It lies on the right before the climb up to Seopjikoji.

A quiet village near Seopjikoji with a beach known worldwide as an ideal spot for windsurfing. It has many guesthouses and pensions, and Seongsan Ilchulbong can be seen from the beach. Nearby: Haewat (해왓, restaurant, about 30 m); Gasiabang Noodles (가시아방국수, restaurant, about 60 m).

A coastal village known as Baram-koji, a place where the wind stays, with murals covering the walls of houses. Many murals show flowers and storybook characters, and a map is provided to guide visitors.

A grassland with open sea views along Jeju Olle Trail Route 3. It was once a grazing ranch and later a place where tangerine peels were dried on the grass, which attracted many tourists. Now it is valued for its scenery.
Jeju's largest indoor and outdoor water park, with 18 pools, wave and lazy river pools, slides, food outlets, and a jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse). It can hold up to 3,000 visitors at once.
opening_hours: Varies by season; see official website
closed_days: none; outdoor pools open May-Sep only

description_en: A theme park with characters from TUBAn, the studio behind 'Larva'. Visitors pass through Rotary Park and the jungle city of Oscar New World to reach Larva Adventure Village, with 12 thrill rides and attractions.
A valley near Gamsan-ri in Andeok-myeon, formed by the Changgo stream that flows into the sea. Half its length is steep cliffs, and its lower gorge has columnar and plate joint rock formations.

A volcanic cone in Gamsan-ri, Andeok-myeon, named for its moonlike shape, with two horseshoe-shaped craters and wooden boardwalks for easy hiking. From the summit you can see Sanbangsan, the Hwasun coast, and the Hyeongje Islands.

A residential village lane in Anseong-ri, Daejeong-eup, where hydrangeas planted by an elderly couple bloom along stone walls. In mid-June the walls are covered in blossoms. Please visit quietly, as people live here.

name_en: Alddeureu Airfield and Japanese Military Aircraft Hangars
description_en: A modern history site: a Japanese military airfield built as a forward base for the Second Sino-Japanese War, with 19 nearly intact aircraft hangars and anti-aircraft positions. Farmland now surrounds the hangars, and a full-size Zero fighter is displayed inside one of them.

A large Buddhist temple in Seogwipo, known for its Daejeokgwangjeon main hall, a single concrete building with an open interior. Its bell pavilion has a bell engraved with words and pictures on filial piety.

A traditional Jeju house, one of the few old homes on the island that are still well kept, inside a stone wall. Its three buildings are arranged in a U-shape facing a tangerine orchard, with camellia trees around the front.
opening_hours: Exterior viewing always open; owner's consent needed for entry, call ahead

description_en: One of Jeju's best-run farm experience villages, with a native pig pen, thatched houses, and a wedding hall. Visitors can learn Jeju dialect, try a traditional wedding, and experience farming and fishing. Nearby: Sinpung-ri Batdam Path (신풍리 밭담길, sight, about 10 m).

A valley east of the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun, with large rocks and steep terrain. Rapeseed flowers bloom along its slopes in spring. It is on Jeju Olle Trail Route 8 and is also called Jungmun Moonlight Walk Park.
A 50-meter waterfall hidden in the forest that appears after heavy rain in the mountains (70 mm or more). It is normally a dry stream bed, surrounded by cliffs and a natural subtropical forest.
A botanical garden with a large greenhouse at its center, outdoor gardens in Korean, Japanese, Italian, and French styles, and about 2,300 plant species. In autumn the trees turn red and yellow.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales end 17:30); outdoor garden until sunset; Nov-Feb entry by 17:00 for full garden access

description_en: A tropical fruit farm in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, growing bananas, papayas, pineapples and mangosteens. Visitors can join farm tours, feed animals, sample fruit and pick bananas.

A parasitic volcanic cone in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, with a horseshoe-shaped crater. Visitors climb a long staircase nicknamed the 'Stairway to Heaven' and enjoy views of pastures, Seongeup village and Ilchulbong from the summit.
A small harbor on Jeju Olle Trail Route 8, with views of Sanbangsan and the Hyeongje Islands. Visitors can see lighthouses and jar artworks inscribed with poems along the coastal road.

A premium hot spring spa in Seogwipo, the only one in Jeju designated a medicinal spring by the government. Visitors can soak in carbonated spring water, use an infinity pool, outdoor baths and an aroma sauna.
opening_hours: Hot spring 10:00-22:00 (ticket sales end 21:00); aqua zone indoor 10:00-21:30; aqua zone outdoor 10:00-21:00; jjimjilbang 10:00-21:30; see website for details

description_en: A rocky valley on Hallasan near the Yeongsil trail, where stone pillars stand among dense forest and look like generals or statues of arhats. It is one of the three sacred sites of Hallasan.
opening_hours: Yeongsil trail entry and exit times apply; check Hallasan National Park official notices for trail closures before visiting

description_en: A coastal village in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, offering sea cruises, fishing and homestays. Visitors can taste fresh seafood caught by haenyeo divers and take quiet walks past green fields, colorful roofs and low stone walls. Nearby: Ojo Haenyeo House (오조해녀의집, restaurant, about 70 m).

A quiet port in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, with views of Seongsan Ilchulbong across the water. Visitors can stroll a wooden bridge that seems to float over the sea and a walking trail around the village. It lies on Jeju Olle Trail Route 2.

A harbor in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, where a traditional stone lighthouse called Dodae is preserved. Only seven remain in Jeju. The port marks the end of Jeju Olle Trail Route 2 and the start of Route 3, and Honinji is nearby.

A 20-meter rock pillar standing alone in the sea at the start of Jeju Olle Trail Route 7. Also called Janggunseok or Halmang Bawi, it is linked to a legend of General Choe Yeong, who disguised it as a general to defeat Yuan forces.

A coastal area below Sanbangsan where sandstone layers and wave-cut cliffs form dramatic scenery. Visitors walk down from the Sanbangsan rest area to see cave-like hollows and eroded rock walls, which are said to resemble a dragon lifting its head.
opening_hours: 09:00-17:00 (may be closed due to weather; call before visiting)
closed_days: none (open year-round); may close due to weather

description_en: A submarine trip where visitors see Jeju marine life, including damselfish, colorful sea peacocks and schools of fish swimming over the seabed. The tour also aims to promote Jeju's haenyeo diving culture. Nearby: Seongsanpo Cruise (성산포유람선, heritage site, about 10 m).

A coastal area below the eastern cliffs of Seongsan Ilchulbong, with black sand formed when lava reached the sea and was worn by waves. Visitors can explore it for free without buying a ticket for the Ilchulbong climb. Nearby: Seongsanpo Haenyeo Diving Performance Hall (성산포 해녀물질공연장, museum, about 60 m).
A small, picturesque port in Wolpyeong, Seogwipo. It lies on Jeju Olle Trail Route 7 and marks the start of Route 8. Its calm, sheltered waters glow red at sunset.

A farming and fishing village surrounded by tangerine orchards, with the uninhabited island of Jiguido offshore. Visitors can try scuba diving or spearfishing in the tourist fishing area, and play basketball or sepak takraw in a small marine park.

A camellia grove planted by Grandmother Hyeon Maeng-chun, who bought barren land and planted camellia seeds from Hallasan to shield it from strong winds. Evergreen camellias and tangerine groves give the area a distinctly Jeju atmosphere.

A national fishing port in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, known for crystal-clear water, early cherry blossoms and beautiful sunsets. It is on Jeju Olle Trail Route 5, with a tourist fishing area for hands-on learning and fishing.

A canola flower field on a narrow strip of land linking Seongsan Ilchulbong, with sea on both sides. It is a popular photo spot, especially in spring, when the yellow flowers meet the blue sea. Nearby are Seongsanpo Port and Seopjikoji.

A rural experience training center in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, next to Keunsaseum-i Oreum. It has seven guest rooms, two log cabins, a cafe, seminar rooms and a grass plaza, and is popular for small workshops and retreats.

An indoor theme park in Seogwipo with five themed attractions: a mirror maze, an Egyptian pyramid experience, an optical illusion photo zone, a love lock jewelry room and a tornado-style black hole ride. It is close to Sanbangsan and Yongmeori Beach. Nearby: Seogwang Kart Experience Center (서광카트체험장, sight, about 40 m).

A volcanic cone in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, named for its resemblance to a wildcat, with a horseshoe-shaped crater open to the east. Dense forest covers its ridges, and the loop trail offers cherry blossoms in spring, autumn colors and snowy cedar trees in winter.

The restored home where the painter I Jungseop lived after evacuating to Seogwipo. Nearby, the 360-meter I Jungseop Street runs from the Jeongbang-dong Maeil Market entrance to Soldongsan. Nearby: I Jungseop Culture Street (이중섭 문화거리, heritage site, about 10 m); I Jungseop Art Museum (이중섭 미술관, museum, about 40 m).

A canola flower field between Seongsan Ilchulbong and Gwangchigi Beach, with the sea and Hallasan visible in the distance. The flowers usually bloom from December to March, though timing varies each year, and sunset visits are recommended.

An art park with a walking trail in Seogwipo, with sculptures and artworks throughout. The observation deck overlooks Seopseom island, Seogwipo Port and Mun Island, and the park is lit at night. A freshwater bathing area at the end lets visitors dip their feet.
A village home to the largest herd of elephants in Korea, where the animals live and rest freely. Visitors can attend daily ecology talks, an elephant parade and family sports events.

A summer swimming spot upstream of Jeongbang Falls, in a forest near Seogwipo Port. Cold natural spring water flows year-round, and the pool has shallow and deep areas suited to families. In peak summer, life jackets are free to rent and lifeguards are on duty. Nearby: Seobok Exhibition Hall (서복전시관, museum, about 10 m); Heukdwaeji Haemul Samhap (흑돼지해물삼합, restaurant, about 90 m).

One of Jeju's three major waterfalls, and the only one in Korea that falls directly from land into the sea. Sunlight on the spray can create rainbows over the blue water. Legend says the Qin envoy Seobul carved an inscription on its cliff while searching for an elixir of immortality. Nearby: Walchong Art Museum (왈종미술관, museum, about 80 m).

A stone fortress around Seongeup village in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, built in 1423 when the county seat moved here. It had gates with watchtowers and twelve dolharubang stone guardians at the government office gate. Nearby: Jeju Seongeup Village Go Pyeong-o House (제주 성읍마을 고평오 고택, heritage site, about 90 m); Ieodo Restaurant (이어도식당, restaurant, about 90 m).
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 표선면 성읍리 성읍민속마을 공영주차장 인근

description_en: A mountain village in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, with 300 years of history, centered on a camellia grove designated as a provincial monument. Visitors can see ancient camellia trees, buy camellia oil, and join camellia craft, camellia cooking and natural soap experiences.

A public carbonated hot spring in Seogwipo, uncommon in Korea. Its traditional name, Gumyeongsu, means water that saved people. Local stories say the water is good for blood pressure, heart health and skin care. Nearby: Sanbangsan-Yongmeori Geological Trail (산방산‧용머리해안 지질트레일, sight, about 30 m).
opening_hours: Indoor hot spring 06:00-23:00; jjimjilbang 06:00-22:00; outdoor pool 10:00-22:00

description_en: Korea's largest tea-growing area, with wide tea fields near Sanbangsan. It is run by AmorePacific and sits close to the O'sulloc Tea Museum, the Chusa Exile Site and the Gotjawal forest. Nearby: O'sulloc Tea Museum (오설록 티뮤지엄, museum, about 20 m).
opening_hours: Summer 09:00-19:00; winter 09:00-18:00 (may close early in bad weather; call before visiting)

description_en: A coastal port in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, serving ferries to Udo island and sightseeing cruises past the Seongsanpo and Udo coastlines. It also handles cargo and seafood.

name_en: Jeju Seongeup Village Go Chang-hwan House
description_en: A traditional house in Seongeup village, built around the early 1800s next to the Jeongui Hyanggyo school. It once served as an inn for travelers, so locals still call it the inn house. The main house is a classic three-room Jeju design. Nearby: Jeongui Hyanggyo (정의향교, heritage site, about 40 m).

A chocolate-themed attraction in Jungmun Tourist Complex, with chocolate art from around the world, a country-by-country chocolate exhibit, a children's photo zone and a viewing deck. Visitors can make chocolates and macarons.

A provincial park in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, centered on gotjawal, a forest growing on irregular lava rock with diverse wildlife. It has five trails, two forest talks each day and a viewing deck, plus an exhibition room and cafe.
opening_hours: Mar-Oct: entry 09:00-16:30, trails 09:00-18:00; Nov-Feb: entry 09:00-15:00, trails 09:00-17:30

name_en: Jeju Dawon Green Tea Maze Park
description_en: A tea garden on Jeju's Second Mountain Road, about 500 meters above sea level, offering green tea and coffee with snacks. Visitors can see Seogwipo, Munseom and Beomseom islands, Jungmun Resort, Marado and Gapado.

A traditional pottery village in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, where artisans keep Jeju's pottery tradition alive. It has six kilns, including Norangul, a stone kiln restored in 2000 after two decades of research, which makes unglazed natural pottery fired by flame.

An arboretum in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, with hundreds of round-shaped camellia trees grown from cuttings since 1977 by the great-grandson of the Wimi grove founder. Visitors can see camellia varieties, wildflowers, ponds, sculptures and a fountain.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00); operates mid-November to late February, see website or call for details

description_en: A European-style resort in Seogwipo surrounded by forest, with hotel-style jacuzzi rooms and Finnish-made detached cabins. All rooms face south toward the sea, with Hallasan behind. Facilities include an outdoor pool, an indoor bubble bath and concierge service.

Korea's first immersive media theme park using water, with 12 themed spaces featuring media art and varied content. Water is heated in autumn and winter so it can be enjoyed year-round. Photo spots suit families and adults alike.

An ecological park in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, where visitors can see birds of prey that cannot return to the wild and feed roe deer. Visitors can also touch small animals such as lizards and frogs, and make crafts from hinoki cypress and acorns.

A citrus farm in Jungmun Tourist Complex, Seogwipo, where visitors can pick tangerines such as Hallabong, Hwanggeumhyang, Redhyang and Cheonhyehyang. The farm sells fresh carrot juice, citrus snacks and chocolate, and ships citrus nationwide.

A herb garden in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo, with about 180 herb varieties and native wildflowers in themed gardens. It also has a hands-on citrus farm, a walking path, an herb shop, a cafe with herb-based dishes and an herb experience hall.

A volcanic cone in Bomok-dong, Seogwipo, with a steep south face, large rocks and a bare summit covered in silver grass. Its gentler north side has two ridges, and a large rock cave sits midway up the south slope.
opening_hours: Some areas may be closed; call before visiting

description_en: A pony experience park in Gasi-ri, Pyoseon-myeon, on the site of the Gapma stable that bred top horses in the Joseon era. It includes a pony museum, Ttarabi riding grounds, a cafe, an art shop, an experience hall and a festival space.

A canola field beside the Place Camp near Seongsan Ilchulbong, where Ilchulbong, Udo and a reed field can be seen together. Horseback riding around the field is possible. Paid areas are fuller and better maintained than free ones, and a heart-shaped frame is set up for photos.
closed_days: none; closed late March to early November

description_en: A coastal area near Jungmun Tourist Complex where dark, hexagonal basalt columns stand like a folding screen. Designated a national natural monument, it offers dramatic waves that can rise over 20 meters when the sea is rough.

A crescent-shaped beach about 560 meters long in Jungmun Tourist Complex, lined with palm trees and volcanic stones. Its sand comes in black, gray, red and white shades, and it draws more than one million visitors a year for water sports.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (may close due to weather)
closed_days: none (open year-round); may close due to weather

description_en: An international resort area in Jungmun, Daepo and Saekdal, Seogwipo, with nine hotels and attractions such as Yeomiji Botanical Garden, the Teddy Bear Museum, Jeju Chocolate Land and Cheonjiyeon Falls. Its beach and ocean-view cafes are popular for water sports.

A maze park in Jungmun with hedges of Leyland cypress, where visitors find their way through the maze to a golden lion statue at its end. The park also offers tangerine experiences, animals and a canola field.

A privately managed canola flower field in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, with walking paths and photo zones among the flowers. Visitors can buy coffee, tea and selfie sticks, and there is ample parking. It is close to Gwangchigi Beach and Seopjikoji.

A waterfall formed by the Jungmun Stream flowing from Hallasan to the sea, in the Jungmun Tourist Complex. It splits into three falls, and the first drops from columnar joint cliffs into an emerald pool.
opening_hours: 09:00-17:50 (last entry 17:10); may change with sunset time and weather

description_en: An ecological park upstream of Cheonjiyeon Falls in Seogwipo, showing how people and nature can live together. It has observation areas for aquatic plants, wetlands, plum and wildflowers, and wild birds, plus wooden walking paths.

Tall cliffs of trachyandesite rise above Cheonjiyeon Falls in Seogwipo, creating a dreamlike scene. Below the falls lie volcanic and marine sediment layers, and lava erupted about 400,000 years ago covers them.
A citrus picking farm in Namwon-eup, the southernmost part of Seogwipo, open for tangerine picking in all seasons. The farm also runs family programs, sells citrus products, and has photo spots.

Camellia Hill in Andeok-myeon has about 6,000 camellia trees of over 500 kinds from around the world, including the largest and earliest-blooming types. It is also a garden with palms and landscape trees, a wildflower corner, a lawn, a pond, and cottage lodgings.
opening_hours: Summer and transitional (Mar-Nov): 08:30-18:30 (last entry 17:30); Winter (Nov-Feb): 08:30-18:00 (last entry 17:00)

description_en: Taeutgae is in Wimi-ri, Namwon-eup, on Jeju Olle Course 5. Freshwater springs rise from holes along the coast, and visitors swim in a natural spring pool or snorkel in the clear sea water next to it.

Tong Oreum in Seongsan-eup is named for its hollow, barrel-like shape. Its gentle slopes surround a nearly round crater with five low peaks, and a lava outflow on the west forms a horseshoe-shaped rim.

A hands-on farm in Andeok-myeon offering tangerine picking, horseback riding, and feeding animals for children. Each visitor fills one basket with tangerines, and samples are allowed during the activity. A souvenir shop sells snacks, bags and caps. Nearby: Jeju Sunmemil Makguksu (제주순메밀막국수, restaurant, about 70 m).
opening_hours: Tangerine picking 10:00-17:00 (last entry 16:00); open-field Hallabong picking 10:00-16:00 (last entry 15:30); varies by activity

description_en: A themed garden in Andeok-myeon with seasonal flowers such as canola, hydrangea, pink muhly and pampas grass. Visitors can pick tangerines, feed animals, and visit the Hobbit Village, the Stairway to Heaven and a sand playground. Seasonal festivals are held.

A marine culture complex built over the sea on Jungmun's beach road, run by a leisure affiliate of Hoban Group. It offers yacht and marina programs, seafood dining prepared by a former luxury-hotel chef, and cultural events.

Pyeonbaek Forest on Mount Goi in Namwon-eup is Jeju's largest hinoki cypress grove, with about 70,000 trees. Forest trails take 30 minutes to an hour, and a nearby ranch raises about 3,500 native black goats.

A wide, gently sloping sandy beach in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo. It is the widest beach on Jeju, and at low tide a sandbar forms a round white beach, while at high tide it becomes a shallow emerald lagoon. The shallow water suits children. Nearby: [Jeju Olle Course 4] Pyoseon-Namwon Olle ([제주올레 4코스] 표선-남원 올레, sight, about 80 m).

A cone-shaped oreum in Andeok-myeon named for the western breeze that blows there. It has no crater, with pines on top and a grassy area on the southwest side. The trail is thorny and rocky and hard to follow, so take care.
