A memorial on a seaside hill in front of Sanbanggulsa in Andeok-myeon, erected in 1980 to honor Hendrick Hamel and the friendship between the Netherlands and Korea. Hamel's ship drifted to Sagye-ri in 1653, and he stayed on the island for 13 years.

A sports park in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, opened in 2008 with an inline skating rink, outdoor exercise equipment, basketball and tennis courts, an athletics track and a reflexology walkway. It has shaded areas, a playground, night lighting and an outdoor stage. Nearby: [Jeju Olle Course 11] Moseulpo-Muneung Olle ([제주올레 11코스] 모슬포-무릉 올레, sight, about 30 m).

Hamo Beach, also called Moseulpo Beach, is near Moseulpo in Daejeong-eup. It was once a swimming beach but is now closed because of sand loss and exposed rocks. A campsite with more than 10 tent sites is nearby and needs advance booking in peak season.

Hallasan sits at the center of Jeju Island and is a young volcanic mountain whose eruptions lasted until about 25,000 years ago. Designated a natural monument in 1966, it has rich plant and animal life and many smaller volcanic cones called oreum.
closed_days: none (open year-round); closures possible in bad weather, call before visiting

description_en: Baengnokdam is a crater lake at the summit of Hallasan, an oval crater about 108 m deep at 1,841.7 m above sea level. It is the highest mountain crater lake in South Korea, and snow often lingers there into summer.
opening_hours: Advance reservation required for Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trails; seasonal entry and exit time limits apply; check and book on the Hallasan reservation system before visiting
closed_days: none (open year-round); entry may be banned and areas restricted in bad weather

description_en: The 5.8 km Yeongsil Trail takes about 2.5 hours and is often called the shortest and most beautiful route up Hallasan, suitable for beginners. Along the way are the Yeongsil rock formations, a dense forest, the Five Hundred Arhats rocks, Seonjakjiwat and Witseoreum.

A hands-on citrus farm in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, that grows fruit with organic fertilizer and no forced coloring or wax. Visitors can pick tangerines and other varieties by season from November to May, and buy the picked fruit or have it shipped.

A 20,000-pyeong garden near Seongsan Ilchulbong in Seogwipo, with cherry blossoms, azaleas, sunflowers and hydrangeas. It is one of Jeju's best-known hydrangea spots, and a cafe inside the garden is included with admission.

Uninhabited islets in front of Sanbangsan Mountain, south of Sagye Port. The low main island has a small sand beach, and the taller Otseom island shows fine columnar joint cliffs. The islands are popular for sunrise and sunset photos, fishing and diving.

A coastal road linking Sangmo-ri at Songak Mountain in Daejeong-eup with Sagye-ri in Andeok-myeon, with views of the sea, the Hyeongje Islands and Marado. It has been named one of Korea's 100 most beautiful roads, and nearby are Sagye Beach and footprint fossil sites.

A small pond where Tamna's founding deities, Go, Yang and Bu, held a joint wedding with three princesses from an eastern kingdom. Beside it is a small cave split into three branches, where the newlyweds set up their bridal chamber. Red lotus flowers bloom here in summer.

Gotjawal is a forest on Jeju's rugged volcanic rock, where uneven terrain creates different climate zones. At Hwasun Gotjawal, northern and southern plant species grow side by side, and about 50 rare species live here. Follow the signposts along the three trail courses.

A beach with dark, fine sand in Andeok-myeon, backed by Sanbangsan Mountain, with views of Gapado, Marado and the Hyeongje Islands. In summer an outdoor pool filled with cool spring water sits beside the sea, so visitors can swim in both sea and fresh water.

A coastal spot in Seogwipo on Jeju Olle Course 7, known for summer swimming, snorkeling and photos. The bay curves gently, with pillar-like rocks that block the waves, and its rounded coast gives the place its name, which means rainbow in Jeju dialect.

Twelve man-made caves on the southwest coast of Samaebong in Seogwipo, dug by Japanese forces during World War II to hide torpedo boats. Each is about 3 m high, and two of them connect inside in an H shape.

A small, simple Buddhist hall in a dense forest in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, with only a few small buildings. A moss-covered stone arch, called the Gate of Heaven, leads to an untouched valley, and Byeoli Falls is nearby.

A flower garden in Namwon-eup with views of Hallasan, holding flower festivals several times a year. Seasonal blooms include canola, plum, hydrangea, pink muhly and camellia. Children can feed animals and join seasonal activities such as Black Pig Play.

A renewable energy exhibition in Gujwa-eup, Jeju City, showing Jeju's energy policy and future energy city models. The second floor has an industrial revolution tunnel, a climate crisis hall, and a microgrid model of Gapa-do, a carbon-free island pilot.
closed_days: Sat, Sun; public holidays; Seollal and Chuseok; Apr 3 (4.3 Memorial Day)

description_en: A volcanic oreum behind Suryong-i village in Hallim-eup, Jeju City, about 500 m southeast of the village. Its shape resembles an overturned cauldron, and its gentle east slope opens into a horseshoe-shaped crater.

A small oreum without a crater, lying along a north-south ridge in Oramsam-dong, Jeju City, covered in pine forest. Its folk name, meaning puppy oreum, comes from a feng shui image of a pup beside its mother, and its northwest slope has long been considered auspicious.

Tomb site of Kang Yeong, a Joseon-era scholar who fled to Jeju after the Prince's Rebellion and taught local people in Hamdeok-ri. The site has the Jocheon Seowon academy buildings and is known for its double-petaled cherry blossoms in spring.
opening_hours: Open only during cherry blossom season (private land of the Jeju clan association)

description_en: A walking path in Pyeongdae-ri, Gujwa-eup, starting from the Jungdong village hall and passing through old village scenery. Its traditional Jeju stone field walls are stacked to withstand typhoons, shield crops from wind and keep out livestock. The path passes Gamsugul Well, named for its good-tasting water.

A citrus picking farm in Jocheon-eup where visitors can pick and eat tangerines. Seasonal flower gardens include pink muhly, autumn flowers, camellias and hydrangeas, and there are animal feeding experiences with alpacas, horses and goats. A cafe is on site.

A volcanic oreum with a broadcast tower on top, east of the Jeju pony ranch in Bonggae-dong, Jeju City. It has three peaks and two horseshoe-shaped craters, and its slopes are covered in natural forest of deciduous and evergreen trees.

A volcanic cluster in Jocheon-eup, Jeju City, and a UNESCO World Natural Heritage site. Lava flows carved a streamlined valley about 4 km long, and on the southeast pasture, cone-shaped hills formed by lava flows cluster together.
opening_hours: 09:00-14:00 (departures every 30 min; 11 tours a day); see official website for details
closed_days: Tue; Seollal and Chuseok; fully closed in severe weather

description_en: Geomi Oreum in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, has a ridge that looks like several hills from afar and slopes that spread out like a spider's web. Seen from Baengyak-i Oreum, it looks like a spider with raised legs.

A horseshoe-shaped oreum on Bija Forest Road in Gujwa-eup, Jeju City, named for a spring in its crater that flows back toward Hallasan. Paths run from the spring to the summit, and a flat loop trail passes torreya, cedar and cypress forests.

A small black-sand beach on Udo island off Seongsan Port, tucked into a gorge below Udobong Peak and about 100 m wide. Steps connect it to the road, and a cave at its end, said to have once been home to whales, is large enough for small concerts.

A small fishing port in Aewol-eup, Jeju City, on the Aewol coastal road with emerald sea views. Its long breakwater is popular with photographers and anglers, and the water is so clear that fish can be seen swimming. It marks the start of Olle Course 16 and the end of Course 15. Nearby: [Jeju Olle Course 16] Gonae-Gwangnyeong Olle ([제주올레 16코스] 고내-광령 올레, sight, about 10 m).

A ghost-themed park with a haunted house, a ghost maze and horror virtual reality, plus a holiday pension, seafood restaurant, cafe and convenience store. It is a fun spot for families and friends to visit together.

A popular beach in Aewol-eup, Jeju City, with a youth training center nearby and many group visitors in summer. At its end is the Gwamul open-air hot spring, divided into men's and women's pools, where visitors can soak after swimming.

A sunset spot in Sinheung-ri, Jocheon-eup, Jeju City, with walking paths and facilities for relaxing by the sea. The waves here are strong enough to overturn passing boats, which is why it is compared to Uldolmok, a strait with rough water. Nearby: Mungae Hangari Jocheon Main Branch (문개항아리 조천본점, restaurant, about 40 m).

Gwaneumsa is a major Buddhist temple on the slopes of Hallasan at about 650 m, overseeing about 30 temples in Jeju. Its records go back to the Goryeo period, and it was destroyed in 1702 under Joseon-era policy before being revived.

An oreum in Bongseong-ri, Aewol-eup, Jeju City, shaped like a curved cat's back, with a horseshoe-shaped crater opening to the north. Its slopes are wooded with natural forest, and orchids and wildflowers grow in the shade.

A village-wide tourism project in Gyorae-ri, Jocheon-eup, built around the spring source of Samdasu water. Pastures and volcanic cones stretch to the southeast, and forests and valleys to the southwest. Sights include Gyorae Gotjawal, Sangumburi crater and the Stone Culture Park.

A spring on the north slope of the castle hill in Aewol-eup, used as the drinking water source of the Sambyeolcho rebels. Its channel was made from wood and stone, and it is said that no one in the old fortress died of cholera.

A rare stone salt pan on Jeju's west coast in Gueomri, Aewol-eup, where flat lava rock was filled with seawater and dried in the sun to make sea salt. It was an important livelihood here and operated actively into the 1950s.

A small, picturesque port along the Aewol coastal road, popular for sunset views. Nearby, a traditional stone salt field on natural basalt rock shows how local residents once made salt. Nearby: Gueom Fishing Village Experience Village (구엄어촌체험마을, heritage site, about 90 m).
A Confucian academy in Jeju City with a shrine honoring the scholar Kim Jeong and a lecture hall. It began in 1578 as a memorial to Kim Jeong, a scholar exiled to Jeju and later executed.
An organic tangerine farm in Jocheon where chemical fertilizers and pesticides are not used. Visitors can join tangerine picking, farm tours, and picnics among the orchards.
A coastal walk along black basalt stone walls between Geumneung Beach and Geumneung Port in Hallim. It is part of Olle Trail Course 14 and has been a TV drama filming location.

A sculpture park with dol hareubang statues, haenyeo statues, and carvings of Jeju legends and folk life, created by stone master Jang Gong-ik. Replicas of dol hareubang given to visiting world leaders are on display.

A quiet beach in Hallim next to Hyeopjae Beach, with clear turquoise water and soft sand. It is less crowded than its neighbors, and the parking lot connects directly to the sand. Low tide reveals a wide beach. Nearby: Geumneung Port (금능포구, heritage site, about 90 m).

A Buddhist temple in Gujwa-eup that began as a prayer hall in 1930 and became a full temple after its main hall was built in 1975. The main hall enshrines Shakyamuni Buddha, with seven Buddhist paintings inside.

An evergreen subtropical forest of about 10,000 pyeong next to Nabeup village in Aewol, designated a natural monument. It is the only evergreen forest left on flat land in western Jeju City, with over 60 subtropical plant species.
A parasitic volcanic cone in the midland of western Jeju, with a large circular crater and two peaks. Its crater lake has dried up, and the name is linked to an old word meaning 'god'.
One of Jeju's largest sunflower farms, covering about 10,000 pyeong with around 750,000 sunflowers. It is open from mid-June to late November and is popular for summer photos.
Korea's first maze park, located between Manjanggul Cave and Gimnyeong Sagul in Jeju City. Tall trees form paths that are easy to get lost in, and the design was made with a British maze designer.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:30 (last entry 17:30); varies by season, check at the ticket office

description_en: A beach in Gimnyeong village, shaped like the Chinese character for flat when seen from above, with white sand and cobalt-blue water. Walkers can see the Gimnyeong wind turbines, and the rock shore is popular with anglers.

A harbor on Jeju's east coast with clear, deep water and a yacht marina, near Seongsegi Beach where camping is possible. Paddleboarding, snorkeling, and diving are popular, and the breakwater is good for fishing.
The highest oreum in its area, with a round crater that has three peaks along its rim. From the summit, visitors can see Darangshi, Geomi Oreum, and Baegyagi Oreum.

A gentle oreum that children and seniors can climb, reached by a forest path to an observation deck. On clear days the summit offers views across northwest Jeju, and the sunset over the coast is famous.
A nearly circular oreum in Gujwa-eup with a symmetrical cone shape and a deep funnel-shaped crater at the top. Its crater is said to be as deep as the Baengnokdam crater lake on Mt. Halla.

An uninhabited rocky island about 400 m off Bukchon village in northern Jeju, made of basalt with cracked rock formations and small sandbars. It is a protected natural monument and a major wintering site for mandarin ducks from December to February.

A green tea estate on about 60,000 pyeong in Seonheul-ri, Jocheon, producing eco-friendly tea. The outdoor garden uses small lava caves with a cave pond, a cave bridge, and an opening in the cave ceiling called Eve Hall.

A tangerine orchard in Namwon-eup known for sweet tangerines, with photo spots and a lookout. Visitors can pick tangerines and eat them at parasol tables, and a café with a red roof sits among the trees.
opening_hours: 10:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30); varies yearly, call for details

description_en: A coastal walk from the Dakmeoreu entrance to Sinchon Port, with wooden decks and a seaside pavilion. Its rock formation looks like a hen digging in the soil. It is quiet and best visited from autumn to early winter.

A cluster of large stacked stone towers on Udo Island's coastal road, built as lookouts during the 4.3 Incident. It also has a stone beacon tower, a white lighthouse, and a heart-shaped stone fish weir that is popular for photos.

A tuff cone at the end of Olle Trail Course 12, part of the Jeju geopark. Near the summit are a tortoise-shaped rock and an observation deck with views of the coast. It is one of Jeju's oldest volcanic cones.
A horse-themed park in Hallim offering horse riding, cart rides, and mounted performances that show Jeju horse culture. Its facilities suit families as well as visitors interested in horse culture.
opening_hours: Cart/horse riding: 09:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30); performances: 10:30-17:30; see website for details

description_en: A tangerine-picking farm in Jeju City, about 20 minutes from Jeju International Airport, with four sessions a day to limit crowds. Online booking and on-site payment are both available, and visitors can sample tangerines afterward.
An oreum next to Bichimi Oreum in Gujwa-eup, with a horseshoe-shaped crater and large lava rocks on the summit. Most of the slopes are grassland, and part of the crater has an artificial pasture.

A haenyeo (female diver) experience in Aewol that is open to people who cannot swim or are afraid of water. Instructors teach floating, breathing, and safety, and activities include diving lessons, seafood gathering, and underwater photos.

An alpaca ranch in a forest in Aewol, where visitors can walk and feed alpacas, rabbits, ponies, sheep, and goats. Walking trails feature seasonal flowers, including canola in spring and camellias in winter.
opening_hours: Summer (Feb 15-Nov): 10:00-18:00, last entry 17:00; Winter (Dec-Feb 14): 09:30-17:30, last entry 17:00
closed_days: none (open year-round); irregular closures are posted on the official Instagram

description_en: A hill in Gujwa-eup with a horseshoe-shaped crater open to the southwest and a view over the whole island from the top. It is not a major tourist spot, and parts of the climb are steep.

A sea path that appears at low tide off Gimnyeong, with a green carpet of land path through emerald water. Visitors can photograph it or walk into the sea when the water is just lapping. It is said to have been built for haenyeo divers.

A horse breeding farm in Jocheon run by the Korea Racing Authority, covering over 2 million square meters with stallion stables, an indoor arena, and a horse pool. Visitors can join a tractor wagon tour of the main facilities.

A lava tube cave in Gimnyeong about 7,400 m long, part of the Geomunoreum Lava Tubes World Natural Heritage site. Its main passage is about 18 m wide and 23 m high, and its natural form is well preserved.

A certified tangerine farm in Aewol growing several citrus varieties, with harvesting and citrus preserve-making experiences. Only booked visitors may join the picking activity, and children under 36 months may enter with a parent.

A craft brewery in Jeju founded by four friends who started it over beers in Gyeongnidan-gil, Seoul. Brewery tours are offered by reservation on weekday evenings and weekends, letting visitors see the full brewing process.

A theme park in Gujwa-eup with the longest stone maze, themed on Jeju's three abundances: stone, wind, and women. It includes stone mazes, an arborvitae wind maze, a maze puzzle museum, and stone statues of Jeju legends.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00; ticket sales end 17:00; hours vary by season, see official website

description_en: A pavilion in Hallim where late Joseon scholars and poets gathered to enjoy the arts and nature. It sits on a natural rock above a stream and has an octagonal three-tier stone base and a stone bridge built around 1910.

The former site of a fortress in Hallim, with gates on its east, south, and west sides and a spring inside. Myeongwolpo harbor was a landing point for military campaigns in 1270 and 1374, though the original structures are gone.

A shrine on Sarabong Park in Jeju City honoring those who took part in Jeju's righteous army uprising and anti-Japanese movements, and Kim Man-deok, who practiced charity and famine relief. A memorial tower and monuments stand on the grounds.

A pair of horse-shaped lighthouses at Ihotaeu Beach, the beach closest to downtown Jeju City, modeled on the local pony. The red and white lighthouses stand on the inner and outer breakwaters, each 12 m tall, and are popular for photos.

A stream about 25 km long, flowing from the Hallasan highlands to the sea off Oedo in Aewol, with a canyon formed where ancient lava flowed. Small waterfalls line the downstream route, and the valley is known for eight designated scenic spots.

A natural dyeing workshop in Hangyeong covering about 500 pyeong, with an exhibition room and dyeing experiences. Dyes come from local plants such as Jeju unripe persimmon, miscanthus, tangerine, tea leaves, and herbs.
A healing farm in Aewol offering programs such as field wall trekking, meditation, crop growing, and healing food. Visitors can join valley trekking and valley meditation to restore natural healing.
A café in Gwangnyeong-ri, Aewol, set in a converted tangerine warehouse with a vintage style and an outdoor garden. Tangerine picking is available during the harvest in mid-October.
An oreum in Gyorae-ri, Jocheon, named for the thorny bushes around it; in Jeju dialect it is also called Banong Oreum. Cedar forest covers much of it, and the crater has grass and shrubs.

A steep oreum in Eoeum-ri, Aewol, with pine trees on its slopes and a pasture on the west side. Its crater is said to resemble a bowl monks use for offerings, and the summit has several smaller oreums. Hiking shoes are recommended.

Stone towers built by a village to block bad luck and protect the community, located in Sinheung-ri, Jocheon. Five towers were built originally, and two remain, one of which birds use to nest in its top hollow.

A legendary gate on the Hancheon stream, said to be the passage between the immortal world and the human world. The forest trail at the valley entrance is open, but the valley itself is closed due to rockfall risk.
opening_hours: Forest trail at valley entrance open; valley closed due to rockfall risk; no entry where safety ropes are installed

description_en: A temple of the Korean Taego Buddhist Order in Aewol, open to all people and offering temple stays and youth education. Visitors can rest quietly and experience Korean Buddhist traditions.
opening_hours: 24h / always open; call ahead before visiting

description_en: A stone fortress in Gujwa-eup, designated a Jeju monument in 1973, with gates on its east, south, and west sides and a well inside. It was built in 1510 at a coastal spot where Japanese ships could easily approach.
A Buddhist temple in Jeju City, a branch temple of Gwaneumsa, founded in 1943. Its main hall enshrines a 17th-century wooden seated Buddha statue designated as a Jeju cultural heritage item.

A tangerine-picking farm in Wasan-ri, Jocheon-eup, where visitors can pick and taste fresh tangerines from August to January without a reservation. The farm also has photo spots, a playground and a cafe.
opening_hours: 10:00-17:00 (experiences available from August; call for details)
closed_days: Mon; closed off-season until August (see website for details)

description_en: A pair of stone Maitreya statues from the Joseon-era fortress period: the eastern one, Dongjabok, stands in a village, and the western one, Seojabok, is inside Yonghwasa temple. They were believed to guard the town.

An art park in Jocheon-eup with replicas of 48 traditional stone grandfather statues (dol hareubang) and more than 250 outdoor sculptures. A gotjawal forest trail lets visitors see native plants and trees.

A village trail in Bukchon, Jocheon-eup, a seaside village that suffered a major mass killing in January 1949 during the Jeju 4.3 incident, with about 300 residents lost. The trail is a place for learning about history, human rights and peace. Nearby: Neobeunsungi 4.3 Memorial Hall (너븐숭이 4.3기념관, museum, about 10 m); Old Bukchon (올드북촌, cafe, about 60 m).

A Buddhist temple at the foot of Wondangbong in Samyang-dong, Jeju City. Its five-story stone pagoda, the only Goryeo-era stone pagoda on Jeju, was designated a national treasure. Nearby: Wondangsa Temple Site (원당사지, heritage site, about 60 m).

A forest walk in Gujwa-eup, Jeju City, popular on social media for its photo spots. It features rare cypress trees, open grassland, stone walls and cabins, plus seasonal canola flowers and pink muhly grass.
closed_days: none (open year-round); see Instagram for closure dates

description_en: A small island off Hallim-eup on Jeju's west coast, the youngest of Jeju's volcanic formations. A walk around the island takes about two to three hours and passes lava coasts, giant volcanic bombs and rock formations. Nearby: Hallim Kalguksu Jeju Main Branch (한림칼국수 제주본점, restaurant, about 60 m).
A parasitic volcanic cone on Biyangdo Island, off Hallim-eup, with a large central crater and two smaller craters on its slope. Old records describe it rising from the sea in 1002.

A protected natural monument in Gujwa-eup with about 2,800 bija trees, some 500 to 800 years old, growing densely over 448,165 square meters. The forest is also home to rare orchids, and visitors can enjoy forest bathing here.

A family amusement park on the western mid-slopes of Jeju City with kayaking, a drift-kart track, a maze and forest walks. Seasonal flower events include a trumpet-vine and hydrangea festival in summer and winter camellias.
opening_hours: Summer 08:40-18:00; winter 08:40-17:30 (hours may change with conditions)

description_en: A memorial tower on Sarabong Hill honoring the 1909 Jeju Righteous Army movement against Japanese control. The hilltop offers views over Jeju City, Mount Hallasan and the sea.

A small harbor right behind Jeju International Airport, better known for its beautiful sunsets and the nearby cafe street. The coastal road from here leads to the horse-shaped Ihotteu Lighthouse and Rainbow Coastal Road. Nearby: Dodu Banjeom Jeju Sasu Branch (도두반점 제주사수점, restaurant, about 30 m).

A natural monument crater more than 2 km around, formed by a lava-free explosion, which makes it a rare maar volcano and the only one of its kind in Korea. Water drains through its floor, supporting a distinctive plant ecosystem.
opening_hours: Mar-Jun and Sep-Oct: 09:00-18:40 (last entry 18:00); Jul-Aug and Nov-Feb: 09:00-17:40 (last entry 17:00); closing times may change with weather

description_en: A gotjawal forest in Hangyeong-myeon with a Dalguji trail, a storybook village-style path with photo spots, and a 3.5 km forest trail through primeval woodland. The Dalguji route is accessible by wheelchair and stroller.

The office that runs the unmanned Sanji Lighthouse on the summit of Sarabong, overlooking Jeju Port. The original 1916 lighthouse was preserved in its original form, and a similar lighthouse now operates beside it. Nearby: Sanji Lighthouse (산지 등대, heritage site, about 30 m).
opening_hours: Summer 09:00-19:30; winter 09:00-18:00; no entry outside these hours for safety reasons

description_en: A grove of eight black pine trees about 8 km along the Jeju cross-island road from Jeju City, estimated at 500 to 600 years old. They are among the largest known trees on Jeju, some reaching 30 meters.

A city park in Yeondong, Jeju City, built on Bedeuri Oreum and known for a Mikado-type steam locomotive, now the only one remaining on Jeju. Residents walk and exercise here, and weeping cherry blossoms in spring draw visitors.
A lesser-known beach in Jeju City with clear water and fine, glittering black sand made of volcanic fragments. In summer, many visitors bury themselves in the sun-heated sand for a sand bath.
The shortest of Jeju's coastal roads, running from Samyang-dong village to Samyang Beach in northern Jeju City. Streetlights line the road, and its sunsets and night views attract many visitors.
A small oreum near Sancheondan in Jeju City with a round grassy crater at the top and a spring on its south slope. From the summit visitors enjoy wide views, and the trail is relatively gentle.
An exotic palm grove in Aewol-eup with shaded benches and photo spots. Cycads and palms stay green through every season, and nearby Gonae Port and the Hangdam coastal walk are easy to visit as well.

A Catholic pilgrimage site with a park depicting 12 key events in Jesus's life, a Trinity Cathedral and a large cross. It covers about 264,000 square meters, is open 24 hours for prayer, and can hold outdoor masses for about 5,000 people.

A well-known oreum in western Jeju with five peaks, named for standing alone like a morning star in the evening sky. In October the slopes fill with silver grass, which is easy to enjoy from the flat lower area.

A ranch across from Saebyeol Oreum in Aewol-eup where visitors can meet alpacas, horses, donkeys, sheep, black goats and rabbits. Carrot sticks can be bought for feeding alpacas and donkeys, and horseback riding and carriage rides are offered.
A low hill by the road in Hangyeong-myeon with a round crater about 20 meters across, containing farmland, grassland and graves. Pine trees and mixed shrubs cover the hill.
A natural pool east of Samyang Beach where fresh spring water meets the sea. The water is clear and cool at low tide, and at high tide the spring and sea water mix and the temperature rises.
opening_hours: 10:00-22:00 (no swimming, drinking or tents outside these hours)

description_en: A garden in Hangyeong-myeon meant for quiet reflection on oneself and one's life, where visitors can walk and rest in nature. It is built on the record of one person who tended the land for 60 years.

A short hidden forest path of about 200 meters beside Samdasoo Ranch in Jocheon-eup, lined with cypress trees and low stone walls. Sunlight filters through the branches, and it is popular for photos and wedding shoots.

A theme park in Jocheon-eup showing junk art, three-dimensional artworks made from recycled materials. Visitors can meet superheroes and animated characters in various sizes, with detailed craftsmanship up close.
closed_days: none (open year-round; hours may change for rain, snow or typhoons)

name_en: The Fairy and the Woodcutter Theme Park
description_en: An indoor theme park in Seonheul-ri, Jocheon-eup, that recreates old town scenes, including a former Seoul Station building, an old market, tea rooms and comic book shops. Vintage films play all day, free to watch.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00); may change with conditions, call before visiting

description_en: A temple in Aewol-eup along Jeju Olle Trail Course 15, with halls for Seolmundae Halmang and the Five Hundred Generals and a wish stone. Its lotus lanterns and night views, lit from around 7 p.m., are free to enjoy.

A gotjawal forest in Seonheul-ri, Jocheon-eup, recognized as a Ramsar wetland in 2011 and a world geopark site in 2014. Lava ridges, wetlands and caves lie within the evergreen forest, said to be the largest evergreen forest in Korea.
closed_days: none; closed on Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A small volcanic cone in Songdang-ri, Gujwa-eup, with a horseshoe-shaped crater. The trails around the hill loop back to the entrance, reached through a wide horse pasture.

A 15.8 km coastal road along the east end of Jeju, from Sehwa-ri in Gujwa-eup to Seongsan-ri in Seogwipo City, said to be the longest coastal road on Jeju. It has a bike lane, and nearby sights include Byeolbangjin Fortress, Hado Beach and Sehwa Beach.

A farm in Hallim-eup started in 1954 by Irish priest Father McGlinchey and known for racehorses and organic milk. Visitors can enjoy wide grasslands, historic buildings such as Tesphon, a cafe using the farm's milk, and a faith-themed walking trail.
closed_days: none (open year-round); Cafe Ujubudan closed on public holidays

description_en: A seaside spot in Kimnyeong-ri, Gujwa-eup, used as a filming site for the JTBC drama Welcome to Samdal-ri. It has a red lighthouse, wind turbines and emerald water, with a wide white sand beach at low tide and shallow water good for children and snorkeling. Nearby: Gimnyeong Orai (김녕오라이, restaurant, about 90 m); Jjokkeullak (쪼끌락, cafe, about 90 m).

A village in Gujwa-eup named a world best tourism village by UNWTO in 2023, known for haenyeo divers and traditional stone field walls. Visitors can join haenyeo tours, a Darangshi Oreum wellness tour and other village programs run by a cooperative. Nearby: Cafe 477 Plus (카페477플러스, cafe, about 10 m).
opening_hours: 09:00-17:00 (varies by program; see website for details)
closed_days: none; closed on the 1st of every month

description_en: A small beach between the Sehwa folk market and the Haenyeo Museum on Jeju Olle Trail Course 20. Though not an official swimming beach, it has clear blue water, and at low tide white sand and black basalt rock appear.

An oreum in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, said to resemble a miniature Mount Hallasan, hence its name meaning grandson of Hallasan. It is one of Jeju's top three oreum for autumn silver grass, and the path to the summit runs through dense grass.

A photo spot on Bijarim Road in Songdang-ri, with a broad green field framed by trees and cedar forest and oreum in the distance. It is reachable by intercity bus and often combined with nearby Anol Oreum.

An oreum by the road south of the Hanyang intersection in Hangyeong-myeon, with pines covering its slopes. At its base, beside a former water pond, stand two hackberry trees estimated to be over 100 years old.

A volcanic cone on Udo Island, shaped like a cow lying with its head raised, reached by ferry from Seongsan Port in about 15 minutes. Its southeast side drops straight into the sea, and a reservoir lies inside the crater.

A small volcanic cone in Susan-ri, Aewol-eup, with a round crater and a small pond on top. Its well-kept steps and paths on Jeju Olle Trail Course 16 make it popular with families, and the climb takes about 20 minutes.

A large artificial reservoir at the foot of Susanbong, with a 400-year-old black pine that is a natural monument and village guardian tree. The pine grows so close to the water that it seems to touch the surface.

A 77-meter viewpoint on Jeju's west coast with cliffs running about 2 km along the shore. Springs seep from the cliffs, a geological trail runs along the coast, and Gosan Weather Station stands on the summit. Nearby: Suwolbong (수월봉, oreum, about 80 m).

A small church on Jeju Olle Trail Course 13 in Hangyeong-myeon, said to be one of the smallest churches. It has no set service times and is open to all for quiet meditation, with the words Asked on the Road on its tower.

A Peanuts-themed garden house in Gujwa-eup with five themed halls, Cafe Snoopy and a Peanuts store. Visitors can explore everyday-life stories through the characters, and pets are welcome on Wednesdays.

A famous road in Jeju City where parked cars appear to roll uphill, an optical illusion created by a slight downhill slope of about three degrees. It has become a popular tourist spot, and safety features have been added to reduce accidents.

A coastal road along the western tip of Jeju, lined with wind turbines of an offshore wind farm along a winding shoreline. Visitors can see the white windmills, the emerald sea and Chagwido island in the distance. It is also known for beautiful sunsets.

Stone fortress ruins built during the Jeju 4.3 period in Sinchon village, Jocheon, where the Sinchon talks were held. The site is near the Dakmeoreu coast, part of Haean-nuri Trail course 50, which has sea-view walking paths.

A Joseon-era village office building in Sinchon, Jeju, moved to this site in 1805 and repaired many times. Its tiled hip-roof house has seven bays across the front, larger than typical Jeju homes, but its structure is similar to them.

A coastal park near the Sinchang windmills with an exotic landscape. Its name refers to local spring water, and an old bathhouse with separate stone walls for men and women is fed by clear, cool spring water. A bridge over the sea leads to a lighthouse.

A natural dyeing brand in Aewol-eup, Jeju, making eco-friendly clothing and accessories dyed with local flowers, leaves and onion skins. It offers natural dyeing classes, including flower dyeing, leaf dyeing and onion skin dyeing.

A small oreum with a round crater, located directly across from Darangshi Oreum in eastern Jeju. It is an easy walk of about 10 minutes, suitable for children, and its tall pampas grass is beautiful in autumn.

A tangerine picking experience farm and cafe with a nostalgic, analog feel. In tangerine season, visitors can pick tangerines from orchards grown without pesticides. The orchard has photo spots, and the cafe serves organic drinks.

A healing forest on the road from Jeju National University to Gwaneumsa Temple, and part of Ara-dong cultural history trail course 2. Visitors can enjoy forest bathing, quiet walks and barefoot walking. Smoking, camping and cooking are not allowed.

An interactive media-art playground by Arte Museum, opened in April 2024. It has 16 play areas, three media play spaces and an exhibition area for adults. Kids can join paid activities such as soap making and keyring crafts.

Korea's largest immersive media-art exhibition hall, housed in a former speaker factory in Aewol. Its roughly 1,400-pyeong space and ceilings up to 10 meters high host 16 media-art displays that combine light, sound and scent.
A gentle oreum in Gujwa-eup, eastern Jeju, with a bowl-shaped crater at its summit. It is easy to climb to the rim, and inside the crater a circle of cedar trees is a notable sight.

A dairy farm near Jeju Airport, founded in 1978 and designated a dairy experience farm in 2008. Admission is free. Visitors can feed calves by hand, enjoy views of Hallasan, and play traditional games and nature-friendly play areas.

A traditional farming village on Olle Trail course 13 in Hangyeong-myeon, named for its nine springs. Its fields grow barley, tomatoes and broccoli with groundwater drawn from 100 meters underground. Visitors can join farm experiences and see North Jeju's scenery.
A horseshoe-shaped crater oreum in Gujwa-eup, eastern Jeju, standing next to two other oreums. A dense natural forest grows only in the gully on its inner crater slope.

name_en: Anui Ullim International Singing Bowl Sound Therapy Institute
description_en: A healing center in Aewol-eup offering small-group singing bowl sound healing sessions and private healing programs. Visitors can relax in the deep resonance of Himalayan singing bowls, with programs for stress relief, relaxation and energy balance.
A parasitic volcanic cone in Gujwa-eup, about 192 meters high, named for its shape like a person sitting with legs apart. Its horseshoe-shaped crater opens to the north and has a wide grassy floor.

A pebble beach in Naedo-dong, Jeju City, made of round stones carried from Hallasan valleys by streams and polished by waves. It was designated a cultural heritage site in December 2003. Nearby: Doldam Neomeo Bada (돌담너머바다, restaurant, about 30 m).

A seaside park in Aewol-eup overlooking the sea, with a statue of a woman carrying a traditional water jar. It has free parking and a coastal walkway below, and it is near the Aewol cafe street. Olle Trail course 15 passes through the park. Nearby: Cheonga Clear Kayak (청아투명카약, sight, about 70 m); Tribe (트라이브, cafe, about 10 m); Galchi Sea Aewol (갈치바다 애월, restaurant, about 50 m).
A mixed experience complex for all ages, featuring indoor climbing called Clip and Climb and an eco-friendly kart track for thrilling rides. Many of its activities suit both children and adults.

A volcanic oreum in the mid-mountain area of northern Jeju with a round crater lake that does not always hold water. Remains of artillery installations built by the Japanese military during the colonial period sit on its summit, and Hanbit Reservoir lies at its northern foot.

A coastal area in Hangyeong-myeon, Jeju, designated one of Jeju City's 31 hidden views. Stretching about 2 km below Suwolbong, its sedimentary sea cliffs are known for beautiful sunsets and Gujeolcho wildflowers, and it is part of Olle Trail course 12.

A walking path along the cliffs from Suwolbong to Jagunae Port in Hangyeong-myeon, connected to Olle Trail course 12. Layers of volcanic ash meet the sea here, creating a striking view for a quiet stroll.

A theme park in the Gyorae gotjawal forest in Jocheon, where a train modeled on an 1800s steam locomotive takes visitors on a 4.5 km ride through about 30,000 pyeong of primeval forest. Insects, animals and plants of the forest can be seen along the way.
opening_hours: Park 08:30-19:30; Sky Park 09:30-17:20; Swan boat 10:00-17:00; Putipputi foot-bath cafe 09:30-17:00

description_en: A fishing harbor in Oedoi-dong, Jeju City, also known as Majiri Port, that preserves the look of old Jeju harbors. A haenyeo changing room displays diving tools such as tewak and mangsari. The coastal walkway is known for beautiful sunsets.

A Joseon-era pavilion on the Jocheon coast, designated a tangible cultural heritage of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. It was originally a guesthouse for visiting officials, located outside Jocheon Fortress.

A lotus pond in Aewol-eup, near Deoreok Branch School, named for its lotus flowers. At about 3,780 pyeong, it is the largest rain-fed pond on Jeju. It is used for farm irrigation and hosts lotus, water lilies and many aquatic plants and fish. Nearby: Modeul Hansang (모들한상, restaurant, about 90 m).

A forested oreum at 583 meters, the landmark of Ora-dong, located west of Jeju Science High School. Pine and cypress trees cover it, and a spring called Yeolanji Water lies on its southeast side. During the Jeju 4.3 period, the forest served as a refuge for residents.

An oreum in Bonggae-dong, Jeju City, with a pine forest on its north slope and grassland on the south. Its name comes from its shape, which resembles geese flying in a line. The grave of Go Iji, a pioneer of Myeongdo-am village, lies on its slopes.

A sunset and sunrise spot on Jeju's east coast in Haengwon-ri, Gujwa-eup, just past Haengwon Beach. It is a rock or small islet where waterbirds come to breed, with views of the blue sea and wind farm. Haenyeo statues stand along the shore.

A village enterprise in Suwon-ri, Hallim-eup, offering sea experiences such as teu raft fishing. A teu is a traditional raft-style fishing boat, and the activity takes about an hour and suits all ages. Hyeopjae Beach, Pyeongsu Port and Hallim Port are nearby.

A traditional farming village in Jocheon-eup on the northern slope of Hallasan, surrounded by oreums and wide grasslands. White buckwheat flowers bloom in May and October, and the village holds a festival each May.

A gentle oreum in Gujwa-eup, the only one of the roughly 360 oreums on Jeju with three craters. Grass covers it in spring and summer, and pampas grass in autumn and winter. Its soft ridges are popular with photographers.

A small park near Yongduam Rock in Jeju City, linked to the opposite side by the large Yongyeon Bridge, which is beautifully lit at night. The park has wooden benches and sculptures for resting while enjoying the sea view.

A large seawater spa and bathhouse near Yongduam Rock, set among palm trees for a tropical feel. Facilities include seawater saunas, a traditional dry sauna, a large waterfall, and a jjimjilbang rest area with coastal views.

A Catholic holy site at Yongsu Port in Hangyeong-myeon, where St. Andrew Kim Taegon drifted ashore after a storm while returning from Shanghai. It includes a memorial church, a memorial hall and a restored Raphael ship. The port is on Olle Trail courses 12 and 13. Nearby: Seong Kim Daegeon Sinbu Pyochak Memorial Hall (성김대건신부표착기념관, museum, about 10 m).
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (individual Mass bookings only in the afternoon)

description_en: Jeju's first lighthouse, first lit in March 1906, now a 16-meter round concrete tower on Udo Island. Its lighthouse park has a 3D navigation experience hall and 14 lighthouse models, including the Pharos Lighthouse, one of the Seven Wonders of the World.

A white-sand beach on the west side of Udo Island, known as Seobin Baeksa, where the sea changes color with depth. It is a swimming beach in summer and a photo spot in spring and autumn. Nearby cafes and restaurants serve local treats such as peanut ice cream.

A large island off Jeju's east coast, about 15 minutes by ferry from Seongsan or Jongdal port. It is 3.8 km long, and visitors can tour its popular sites by bus, bicycle or mini electric car. About 2 million tourists visit each year.

A village on Udo Island known for its scenic landscape, clean waters and eight famous views. Films such as 'Il Mare' and 'The Little Mermaid' were shot here, and it has drawn more attention in recent years.
A group of three oreums just below Hallasan's summit, along the Yeongsil trail near the Utse Oreum shelter. The three are called Red Oreum, Lying Oreum and Little Oreum.

A fishing port in Hallim-eup, Jeju, where many fishing boats still dock. Its breakwater and rocky reefs are popular with anglers, and it is quieter than nearby Hyeopjae Beach. The breakwater was built during Jeju 4.3, when young men were made to stack its stones. Nearby: Wolryeong Cactus Colony (월령 선인장군락지, park, about 80 m).

A Taego Order Buddhist temple in Sangwi-ri, Aewol-eup, on Pagunbong, where Samyeolcho rebels were said to have been defeated by Goryeo-Mongol forces. Founded in 1936, it was destroyed during the Jeju 4.3 incident and later rebuilt.

A beach in Woljeong-ri, Gujwa-eup, named for the moon that rests here, with emerald water that reflects the moonlight. Its shallow water suits families with children, and the area has many cafes, restaurants and lodgings.
opening_hours: Beach: 24h / always open; swimming area: day 10:00-19:00, night 10:00-20:00
closed_days: none (open year-round); swim season dates by phone

description_en: A scenic coastal drive officially called the Gimnyeong-Ojo Coastal Road, running from Gimnyeong to Ojo-ri in Seongsan. It offers windmill and emerald sea views. The Woljeong-ri section is busy with cafes and tourists, but the rest of the road is quiet.

Jeju's first Buddhist meditation hall, where a branch of the Joseon Buddhist center for Seon meditation was set up in 1938. It is a branch temple of Gwaneumsa in the Korean Jogye Order, and it suffered during the Jeju 4.3 incident.

A beach in Jeju City known for its pony lighthouse and red and white horse figures, a popular photo spot. It is close to the city center, has gently sloping sand and a pine forest suitable for camping. At low tide, traditional stone fish traps called wondam appear.

A dirt forest trail inside Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest in Jeju City, one of the city's 31 hidden views. Fallen leaves cushion the path, and bumpy stones and volcanic cinder gently massage the feet. Mushrooms and green plants thrive here in summer. Nearby: Sutmoreu Cypress Forest Trail (숫모르 편백숲길, sight, about 50 m).

An artists' village in Jeji-ri, Hangyeong-myeon, where many well-known artists create their works. Nearby are Thinking Park, the largest bonsai garden in the East, the gotjawal subtropical forest, and Bangrimwon, a garden full of wildflowers.

A steep, funnel-shaped crater cone beside the road in Jeji-ri, Hangyeong-myeon, about 900 meters around and 60 meters deep. Pine trees cover its outer slopes, and dense forest grows inside the crater, making access to the inside difficult.

A cherry blossom road in Samdo-ildong, Jeju City, about 10 minutes by car from Jeju Airport. Native Jeju royal cherry trees, 20 to over 100 years old, line the road and form a flower tunnel each spring, and a cherry blossom festival has been held here since 1992.

A rock at Yongsu-ri port in Hangyeong-myeon, Jeju City, set among subtropical trees such as camellia and evergreen species. Designated a Jeju provincial monument in 1981, it honors a local woman's devotion to her fisherman husband. Nearby: Yongsu Port (용수항, sight, about 80 m).
A small cone-shaped oreum on the western foot of Jeongmul Oreum, inside the Geumak Isidol Ranch area. It is known for Jeongmul Spring, whose clean, abundant water once drew villagers from far away.
Named after Jeongmul Spring at its foot, a clean and plentiful water source that villagers relied on in a land short of drinking water. Nearby is Isidol Ranch, one of Jeju's best-known ranches.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (some areas may be restricted; call ahead)

description_en: The entrance to Jedong Ranch, a privately owned ranch that visitors cannot enter. Its road lined with tall cedar trees has become a popular spot for photos and scenic drives.

A 26,046 sq m (8,500 pyeong) citrus orchard in Jeju City with open fields and greenhouses, certified for pesticide-free, GAP and low-carbon farming. Visitors can make citrus marmalade and cake in food therapy programs and try singing bowl meditation in the orchard.

The first natural recreation forest in Korea built in a gotjawal area, a forest of trees and rocks shaped by volcanic lava. Visitors can explore gotjawal ecology and traces of old life such as charcoal kiln sites, and stay in thatched cottages or a campground.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00; ecology trail last entry summer (Mar-Oct) 17:00, winter (Nov-Feb) 16:00; oreum trail last entry summer 16:00, winter 15:00; lodging 15:00-22:00; campground 13:00-20:00; no check-in after check-in time

description_en: A 52-hectare nature park opened in 2007 where visitors can watch roe deer roam freely from forest trails. In a close-up area, they can touch and feed the deer, and an exhibition hall covers Jeju's wildlife and deer ecology.

A quiet midland farming village in Bonggae-dong, surrounded by about 16 oreums, with natural ponds, wetlands and wide pastures where sheep roam. The village grows vegetables year-round using eco-friendly farming.

A coastal road in Dodu-il-dong about 10 minutes by car from the airport, with its guardrails painted in rainbow colors. Nearby you can see haenyeo statues, and Dodubong, a hill on Olle Trail with gentle slopes, is an easy walk away. Nearby: Cafe Namonamo Bakery (카페나모나모베이커리, cafe, about 70 m).
A prehistoric village site from the Bronze and early Iron Ages on a coastal plain, with remains of round and rectangular houses, storage pits, stone walls, dolmens and shell mounds.

A 15,000-pyeong park in the midlands around Hallasan with miniature replicas of landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower, Statue of Liberty and Colosseum, plus statues of historical figures. Its five themed zones include a dinosaur area and a go-kart track.
A hillside village of colorful shops and lodgings, with photo spots, craft workshops and small goods shops. Higher parts of the village reveal views of the Jeju sea, giving a storybook feel.

name_en: Jeju Udo Cheonjin Port Waiting Room
description_en: The waiting room at Cheonjin Port, the main gateway to Udo island at the eastern tip of Jeju, next to the Udo Rapeseed Flower Village information center. It has a ticket counter, seating, and a small shop selling snacks and souvenirs. Nearby: Jeju Olle Trail Course 1-1: Udo-Olle ([제주올레 1-1코스] 우도-올레, sight, about 10 m).
opening_hours: 07:30-18:00 (boats every 30 min; arrival port or timing may change or be delayed due to capacity, tides, cargo or weather)

description_en: A midland village about 15 km southwest of Jeju Airport, set among the Hyeongje-bong oreums and Yusuam Spring. Visitors can try tofu and omegi rice cake making, traditional crafts and horseback riding, and a simple farm stay is available.

A village on the Gotjawal lowlands in Hangyeong-myeon, home to wild plants and flowers and the largest habitat of the Unmunsan firefly. Residents practice eco-friendly farming and protect the forest, so the produce and environment are clean.

A habitat of Munjuran, a seaside plant that grows in sand inside rock walls on Rabbit Island just off the coast of Hado-ri, Gujwa-eup. It is Korea's only habitat of this plant and is protected as a natural monument at the northern edge of its range.

A winter refuge for migratory birds on the coast of Hado-ri, Gujwa-eup, with wetlands and abundant food. Visitors can watch black-faced spoonbills, swans, hawks, kestrels and ospreys, several of them protected, from an observation deck with telescopes.

name_en: Historic Site of Anti-Mongolian Struggle in Hangpadu-ri, Jeju
description_en: The site where the Sambyeolcho rebels made their last stand against Mongol forces, now a designated historic site with an exhibition hall, a monument and earthen walls. Nearby, Jangsumul spring is said to flow from the footprint of General Kim Tong-jeong.

A peace and human rights memorial park honoring victims of the Jeju 4.3 Incident and the island's suffering, opened in 2008. Inside are the 4.3 Peace Memorial Hall, a memorial altar, a memorial tower and an ossuary.
opening_hours: Outdoor park: always open; 4.3 Peace Memorial Hall: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00)
closed_days: Mon (1st and 3rd of each month, Memorial Hall only; if a holiday, the next non-holiday weekday); outdoor park open year-round

name_en: Jeju National University Cherry Blossom Road
description_en: One of Jeju's most famous cherry blossom spots, with trees lining the road to the entrance of Jeju National University. When in full bloom, the petals create a tunnel effect that makes a beautiful drive.

A volcanic island on the continental shelf about 90 km south of the Korean Peninsula, with its original volcanic landforms well preserved. Highlight sites such as Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong and Manjanggul are certified as UNESCO Global Geoparks. Nearby: Seonheul 2-ri Village (선흘2리마을, heritage site, about 10 m); Jeju World Natural Heritage Center (제주 세계자연유산센터, museum, about 40 m).

An open-air park in Songdang-ri, Gujwa-eup, at the heart of Jeju's eastern oreum cluster, covering about 30,000 pyeong. It displays over 200 traditional stone pieces, including child-shaped statues, and includes a farm life experience hall. Nearby: Mr. Milk Songdang Branch (미스터밀크 송당점, cafe, about 70 m).

A grazing area near the 5.16 Road where native Jeju horses, a designated natural monument, roam wide grasslands. Entry into the pasture is restricted, but visitors can watch the horses from designated viewing areas.

A brewery in Hallim-eup that combines the brewing know-how of Brooklyn Brewery with a brewer of over 15 years' experience. Docent-guided tours let visitors explore the facility, which has some of the best brewing equipment in Korea.
closed_days: Mon, Tue; Seollal and Chuseok eve and day

description_en: An indoor sea experience center in Gimnyeong-ri, Gujwa-eup, where visitors can catch octopus, shells and fish by hand and feed sharks, regardless of weather. Waterproof fishing gear is provided, so no equipment is needed.

name_en: Jeju Starlight World Park and Planetarium
description_en: A space science facility for stargazing and astronomy learning, with a 4D theater, a planetarium dome showing seasonal constellations, a solar system exhibit and an observatory open only at night on clear nights.
opening_hours: Summer (Apr-Sep) 15:00-23:00; winter (Oct-Mar) 14:00-22:00 (last entry 1 hr 30 min before closing)
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok (if Monday is a public holiday, the first weekday after it)

description_en: A night festival attraction open since 2017, featuring LED lights and artistic installations. It was selected as one of the top 10 night tourism spots in Jeju by the Jeju Tourism Organization.
opening_hours: 17:00-24:00 (last entry 23:00); may close early in bad weather

description_en: A brewery in Aewol-eup reviving traditional Jeju liquors made with pure underground rock water, adapted to modern tastes. Visitors can taste gosori and omegi liquors and try experiences such as making omegi rice cakes and cocktails.
closed_days: none; closed for Seollal and Chuseok holidays

description_en: A village in Worryeong-ri, Hallim-eup, where native prickly pear cacti grow in patches along the coast. Nearby, the Jeju Specialty Products Development Institute makes cactus extract, prickly pear and granule products. Nearby: Jeju Dolmaeul Park Stone Exhibition Hall (제주돌마을공원 수석전시관, museum, about 90 m).

A citrus farm about 15 minutes by car from Jeju International Airport, where visitors can pick tangerines and buy Hallabong, Cheonhyang, Redhyang and Hwanggeumhyang. Orange and yellow citrus hats and sunglasses are free to use for photos.
opening_hours: 10:00-17:00 (last entry 16:00); closed after the experience season, check website or call
closed_days: none; closed after the experience season (check website or call)

description_en: A quiet, less crowded beach on Olle Trail Course 19 in Jocheon-eup, with newly built changing rooms and showers and a cafe right next to the beach. Lifeguards are on duty in summer, and Seou-bong can be seen in the distance.
A three-story safety experience center in Aewol-eup, opened in November 2020 as the eighth such center in Korea. It offers hands-on programs for learning how to experience and overcome disasters.
closed_days: Mon (if Monday is a public holiday, closed the next day); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A nature-friendly ranch in Aewol-eup with sheep, goats, horses and pigs. Visitors can feed the animals, enjoy goat milk coffee at the ranch cafe, and stay in log cabins, making it a fuller experience than many farm attractions.

A palm-lined park beside Iho Tewoo Beach on Olle Trail Course 17, close to Jeju Airport. Lavender, hydrangea, verbena and cosmos bloom through the seasons, and visitors can photograph low-flying planes or the Iho Tewoo horse lighthouse.

A virtual-nation theme park in Geumak-ri, Hallim-eup, where visitors pass an immigration desk, get a visa at the entrance cafe and can buy passport-style annual tickets. The park uses its own currency, which is spent only on site.

An international trade port about 15 minutes by car from Jeju International Airport, handling about 70% of the island's cargo. Ferries sail to Mokpo, Yeosu, Busan and Wando, letting travelers bring their own cars to Jeju.

name_en: Jeju Haenyeo Anti-Japanese Movement Memorial Tower
description_en: A memorial tower honoring the 1932 Jeju Haenyeo Anti-Japanese Movement, the largest anti-Japanese movement in Korea and the only one led by women. It stands at the second gathering site used by the divers who took part.

name_en: Jeju Healing Meditation Center (Longevity Theme Park)
description_en: A theme park in Aewol-eup overlooking Hallim Beach and Biyangdo, offering healing and meditation programs based on Korean breathing and meditation traditions. Visitors can walk through gardens, a historic park and a nature rest area, and there is a traditional archery range.

A memorial park in Jocheon-eup on the site of the Jocheon March 1st Movement, one of Jeju's three major anti-Japanese movements. It includes a patriots' memorial tower shaped like a jeongnang (traditional Jeju gate), a March 1st monument and an anti-Japanese museum.

A coastal road of about 4.5 km linking Jocheon and Hamdeok. Starting from Hamdeok brings you closer to the sea, and the road passes Gwangot, where the night view of Jeju City is beautiful. Hamdeok Seoubong Beach has emerald water and palm trees. Nearby: Baekgane Jeju Hansang Hamdeok Main Branch (백가네제주한상 함덕본점, restaurant, about 70 m).

An oreum in Aewol-eup where visitors can enjoy forest trails and climbing. It is paired with the larger Nokkome Oreum and the two are called 'brother oreums'. Although its name means 'small', it is not as easy to climb as it sounds.

A coastal road of about 11.2 km from Gwangchigi Beach to Hado Beach, known as a sunrise drive. Hydrangeas line the route from late May through June, and Udo and Seongsan Ilchulbong appear in turn as the road winds.

A themed street in the quiet village of Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, lined with hydrangeas whose color changes from sky blue to pink depending on soil acidity. They usually bloom from mid to late June, sometimes until late July, along the sea road.

A small harbor on the coast road past Hado Beach, also called Dumunpo Port, with small fishing boats moored in it. Ferries to Udo sail from here, and the harbor offers views of Seongsan Ilchulbong, Udo and Jimi Peak. Nearby: Jongdalri Beach (종달리해변, beach, about 30 m).

A volcanic oreum in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, on Olle Trail Course 21, with a conical east peak as its main summit. From the top you can see Seongsan Ilchulbong, Udo and the sea off Jongdal, and traces of an old beacon fire site remain.

An uninhabited island off Gosan-ri in Hangyeong-myeon, the largest uninhabited island in Jeju, reached by boat in about 10 minutes from Jagunae Port. It is home to 82 plant species and surrounded by rich fishing grounds.

A sightseeing boat at Gosan-ri in Hangyeong-myeon, combining a walk on the Chagwi Island trail with a cruise past rock formations such as Beomba-wi and Janggunbawi. It is not a scheduled service, so advance phone booking is required. Nearby: Jagunae Port (자구내포구, sight, about 50 m).
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (may change due to weather or operator circumstances; check website or call)

description_en: A rock near the Bukchon Hwanhae Jangseong wall and the Bukchon Yongmul spring on the coast of Jocheon-eup. The rock has a hole pierced through it, and visitors often photograph each other through the opening with the sea and breakwater behind.

An oreum on the west side of Eoseungsaengak within the Sinenseom ranch, with a small horseshoe-shaped crater. Its valley has a stream and a forest of azalea and maple trees, and the oreum has a gentle slope.

A traditional temple beneath Geumbong Valley, one of the 99 valleys east of Eoseungsaengak on Hallasan. Behind the main hall is a large rock called Yongbawi, and a stream beside the temple leads up to a waterfall said to be the only one on Hallasan.
A spring where groundwater rises from beneath the lava plateau near the coast of Kimnyeong in Gujwa-eup. It is known as the coldest of the several springs along the Kimnyeong shore.
A pristine forest growing on lava terrain, known as the largest habitat of Unmunsan fireflies on Jeju. In the evening visitors can see the fireflies glowing, though viewing depends on the weather.

A handmade candy shop in Jocheon-eup, opened in 2014 and said to be the largest of its kind in the world. Exhibits show the history of candy and rare sweets from around the world, and children can try a candy-making class.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (closing times may differ by season; check the website or call)

description_en: A small beach with shallow emerald water and lava rocks that split the sea into pools of different depths, near Woljeongri Beach on the east coast. Many visitors come to walk along the scenic path and watch the sunset.

A scenic oreum in Aewol-eup on the west side of Jeju City, with steep slopes and a horseshoe-shaped crater. Its summit has a wooden deck observation platform where many visitors stay for a long time to watch the sunset.

A tangerine-picking farm in Hagari, Aewol-eup, where visitors can pick and eat fresh tangerines or buy them. No reservation is needed, though experiences vary by season, and a guesthouse next to the farm lets you combine a stay with the visit.

A cafe and cooking experience space with separate cooking labs for adults and children. Visitors can make dishes such as chicken, lasagna, cookies and baked goods, using ingredients from the on-site garden. The walls are glass, and the cafe is good for a relaxed tea break.

A harbor on Jeju's west coast known as a snorkeling spot, with clear water over a sandy bottom. In summer, local young residents rent out snorkel gear, and showers, paddle boats and life vests are also available.

A small, quiet beach between Woljeongri and Sehwa beaches on Jeju's east coast, on the route of Jeju Olle Trail Course 20. The water is so clear that the sandy bottom is visible, and it suits children who want to play in sand and water.
A hemisphere-shaped Buddhist temple completed in 1998 to pray for national unification and world peace. Its 33-meter pagoda symbolizes the Heaven of Thirty-Three in Buddhism.

Jeju's largest safari theme park, with life-size moving dinosaurs and a stamp mission. Visitors can enjoy photo zones, animal feeding and petting, painting, indoor play areas and rest spaces for adults. Children can ride on animal models.

A volcanic oreum in Bongseong-ri, Aewol-eup, near the entrance road to Hyomyeong Ranch. Its slopes are gentle and covered in grass, and the summit has a horseshoe-shaped vent with two cone-shaped vents to the southwest.

A beach about 400 meters long on Udo Island, split in two by an exposed rock coast. The sand is soft and the water shallow, so it suits families with children. Guesthouses, restaurants and changing facilities are nearby. Nearby: Seomsonai (섬소나이, restaurant, about 100 m).

A scenic coastal drive of about 9 km along Jeju's northwest coast, about 10 km from the airport. It has separate bike lanes and walking paths, and it is part of Jeju Olle Trail Course 16. Nearby: Haeseong Dottuli (해성도뚜리, restaurant, about 90 m).

A fishing village facing Udo Island, with its natural coastline and local fishing culture largely intact. It is home to the natural habitat of the munjuran (sea daffodil) on Tokki Island and a stop for migratory birds, and it has a historic fort and a haenyeo (women divers) museum.
opening_hours: 10:00-17:00 (may change in bad weather; reservation required)
closed_days: none; closed every year from November to March

description_en: A wide sandy beach along the Haemaji coastal road in Hado-ri, Gujwa-eup, with a view of Udo Island. Visitors can walk, swim, kayak and enjoy other sea sports. It is not a designated swimming beach, so check the weather and sea conditions first.

A port in the middle of Udo Island, close to the white coral sand of Seobinbaeksa. It is smaller than Cheonjin Port, and with a ticket you can board ferries at both ports, so it is a good alternative for the return trip.
opening_hours: 07:30-18:00 (departures every 30 min; arrival port and times may change due to capacity, tides, cargo or weather)
closed_days: none (open year-round); check ferry times before travel

description_en: A 1,800-pyeong cultural complex in Aewol-eup with a 10-meter marble bar and a large blue artwork on the first floor. Its cafe, The Commissary, has a pine grove and lawn in the back garden and serves local banana pudding and non-alcoholic draft beer.

A coastal stretch in northwest Jeju running from Aewol to Gwakji, known for clear water and volcanic rock. It was named one of Jeju City's 31 hidden scenic spots in 2009. The 1.2 km walking path is lined with canola flowers in spring. Nearby: Jeju Kayak Olle (제주카약올레, sight, about 60 m); Bomnal Cafe (봄날카페, cafe, about 50 m); Nolmaen (놀맨, restaurant, about 30 m).

A 1.2 km walking path along the coast from Aewol Port to Gwakji Gwamul Beach, also called Gwakgeum Olle. It passes rocks shaped by hardened lava and a winding black-rock shore, and it is one of Jeju City's 31 hidden scenic spots. Nearby: Goijeong (고이정, restaurant, about 70 m).

A densely forested oreum on the eastern slope of Hallasan, the largest single-eruption volcanic cone in that area. Seongpanak Rest Area sits at the highest point of the 5.16 Road between Jeju City and Seogwipo.

An ecological forest on former grazing land, planted with subtropical, temperate and subalpine plants. Its gotjawal and natural forest areas are protected as gene conservation zones, and it also works as a research forest for Jeju's native trees.

A park founded in 1971 on former sandy wasteland, with rows of palm trees, a stone and bonsai garden, and a folk village that shows old Jeju life. It faces Hyeopjae and Geumneung beaches and Biyangdo island. Nearby: Ssangyong Cave (Hallim Park) (쌍용굴(한림공원), sight, about 90 m).

A port in Hallim with ferries to Biyangdo island, which lies about 3 km off Jeju's main island. Visitors can walk a trail around Biyangdo, known as the 'island of a thousand years'. Ferries run only four times a day, so check the timetable. Nearby: Biyangdo Pier (비양도선착장, sight, about 10 m); [Jeju Olle Course 15] Hallim-Gonae Olle (A) ([제주올레 15코스] 한림-고내 올레 (A), sight, about 10 m); [Jeju Olle Course 15] Hallim-Gonae Olle (B) ([제주올레 15코스] 한림-고내 올레 (B), sight, about 20 m).

A tour boat with a transparent window below the deck, so passengers can see the seabed. Go down a few steps to view the underwater world, then climb up for a yacht ride. Only one group rides at a time, and dolphins are sometimes seen.

A coastal road of about 27.8 km on Jeju's east side, from Gimnyeong in Gujwa-eup to Ojo in Seongsan-eup. It passes Seongsan Ilchulbong, a famous sunrise spot, and connects many cafes, restaurants and sights. It is part of Jeju Olle Trail Course 21.

A traditional Joseon-era hall tucked into an alley of Jeju City's old downtown. Local elders once gathered here for archery and banquets and to discuss community matters. The current building was restored in 1981. Nearby: Eumpa (음파, cafe, about 60 m); Hagwi Jeongdam (하귀정담, restaurant, about 80 m).

A lava and limestone cave inside Hallim Park, one of the main lava caves of Jeju. Stalactites and stalagmites fill the interior, and lime deposits cover the walls, giving it the look of a huge painting.
opening_hours: Mar-Oct 08:30-17:30; Jun-Aug 09:00-18:00; Nov-Feb 09:00-16:30 (times vary with sunset)

description_en: A harbor with emerald water and a wide sandy beach beside it. A small lighthouse stands at the end of the breakwater, with a view of Biyangdo island across the sea. Anglers come here, and snorkeling and banana boat rides are offered in season.

A beach beside Hallim Park on Jeju's west coast, with white sand mixed with shell fragments, Biyangdo island offshore and cobalt-blue water. The water is shallow and gently sloped, and changing rooms, showers and restrooms are available. Pine forest lies behind the beach.

A harbor known for its poetry-lined lighthouse path. Poems about the lighthouse, the port and the sea, written by students, line the breakwater all the way to the lighthouse. Tourists take photos there, and locals often walk here in the evening.

A hands-on bird park in Aewol-eup where visitors can see birds and gentle small animals such as alpacas up close and touch them. Four bird ecology talks are held daily, and visitors can feed rabbits, carp and miniature horses.

A primeval gotjawal forest on lava terrain, where southern and northern plant species grow side by side. Walking among ferns and large tree roots feels like stepping into another world. Nearby: Myohan Restaurant (묘한식당, restaurant, about 80 m).

A volcanic oreum also called Dwigubeuni Oreum, named for its bent back. It is within easy walking distance of Songdang village, the center of Jeju's oreum. Most of the slopes are grassland, with planted cedar and pine trees on one side.
opening_hours: 24h / always open (some areas may be restricted)

description_en: An eco-healing forest park opened in 2017 by the Jeju City Forestry Cooperative. Visitors can try seedling planting, forest camping, glamping and caravan stays. It also has a forest cafe, a wine shop and a steam experience using pine wood-chip enzyme.

A street of restaurants specializing in Jeju black pork, near Tapdong Square at Jeju Port. A pig statue and a street sign mark the entrance. Diners often eat the grilled pork dipped in flower anchovy sauce. Nearby: Dombedon (돔베돈, restaurant, about 20 m).

An exhibition, tea and hands-on space inspired by Jeju's gotjawal forest, with large windows that bring natural light inside. Its signature program is making an edible forest-style dessert with crumble, chocolate and granola, then tasting it with a blended tea.

A public museum in Seogwipo dedicated to Jeju's tangerine, covering its history, culture, industry and the lives of farmers through panels, videos and exhibits. A glass greenhouse displays 84 citrus varieties from around the world.
closed_days: none; closed on Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: An adults-only museum displaying about 5,000 sex-related artifacts and artworks collected from around the world. It also offers books and exhibits that present sexuality as part of culture, education and everyday life.

A digital art exhibition that reinterprets Van Gogh's works with modern technology. Unlike a typical show, visitors can see, hear and touch parts of the exhibit, and the focus is on Van Gogh as a person.

A gallery holding about 20 years of photographs by Kim Young-gap, who devoted his life to capturing Jeju. Works include images of Yongnunie Oreum and Mara Island, and his personal belongings are displayed in a separate room.
opening_hours: Mar-Jun and Sep-Oct 09:30-18:00; Jul-Aug 09:30-18:30; Nov-Feb 09:30-17:00 (entry closes 30 min before)

description_en: A private Christmas museum in Andeok-myeon in a building styled after German architecture. It displays decorations and items the owners collected while traveling. Each December, a month-long Christmas market brings many sellers.

A youth center opened in 2005 that runs cultural and educational programs and activity support for local teenagers. It has a multi-purpose hall, reading room and video editing room, plus a creative workshop, music room and dance room. Nearby: Daedeulbo (대들보, restaurant, about 70 m); Beophwan Fishing Village Raw Fish Restaurant (법환어촌계횟집, restaurant, about 90 m).

A museum designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Tadao Ando, using exposed concrete, light and water. Its two spaces display traditional crafts and contemporary art, designed to harmonize with the Jeju landscape.

A cultural institute founded in 1996 that researches and preserves local heritage sites, from Seongsan Ilchulbong to Songak Mountain, including Gapa and Marado islands. It also runs culture schools, clubs and a choir.

A city art museum opened in 1987 on land donated by Gidang Kang Gu-beom, a Jeju-born Japanese-Korean businessman. The building is designed to resemble a rice stack, with a spiral route through the galleries and traditional-style rafter ceilings. Nearby: Sammaebong Library (삼매봉도서관, museum, about 70 m).

A performing arts center opened in 2014 with a large theater, a small theater, exhibition halls and rehearsal rooms. Its design is inspired by the crater of an oreum, and it is Seogwipo's only comprehensive arts venue.
closed_days: none; closed on Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok

name_en: Seogwipo Astronomy and Science Culture Center
description_en: An observatory in Seogwipo for viewing Canopus, a winter star that is hard to see from most of the Northern Hemisphere. It has telescopes, exhibits and a planetarium that shows digital night skies.
opening_hours: 14:00-22:00 (program times vary by month; check the website)
closed_days: Mon (next non-holiday if Monday is a holiday); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok; temporary closures

description_en: A museum in Seogwipo collecting historical brewing tools and vanishing traditional liquors. It shows the changing history of Korean liquors and bottles, and displays spirits from France, Scotland, Ireland, the US, Canada, Russia, Mexico and Germany.
The museum displays about 100 cars from different eras collected worldwide, showing how automobiles developed over time. It also includes Korea's first piano museum, opened in 2019.

A museum in Seogwipo showing more than 8,800 kinds of colorful shells and coral collected from around the world over 41 years. Artist-designed displays combine the shells and coral with bronze pieces.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:30 (ticket sales end 17:30); subject to change, call ahead

description_en: A large aquarium beside Seongsan Ilchulbong in eastern Jeju, with about 45,000 marine animals on display. Its main tank holds up to 6,000 tons of seawater and includes around 27,000 fish that visitors can view from the front.

A museum in Jungmun Tourist Complex, Seogwipo, dedicated to African culture, moved to its current building in 2004. The building is modeled on the Great Mosque of Djenne in Mali, the world's largest mud-brick structure. Nearby: Daegijeong (대기정, restaurant, about 70 m).
Opened in June 2017 inside Phoenix Jeju at Seopjikoji, this is Korea's only museum devoted to Art Nouveau glass craft. The concrete building was designed by world-renowned architect Tadao Ando.
closed_days: Tue (1st of each month); open as usual on national and traditional holidays

description_en: A photo gallery in Seogwipo's Pyoseon area, housed in a former elementary school with a large exhibition hall. Photographer Seo Jae-cheol's works show Jeju's volcanic landscapes, oreum and folk culture.

Jeju's main international conference venue on the Jungmun coast in Seogwipo, opened in March 2003. Its oval exterior reflects the shape of Jeju island, and glass walls inside offer views of Mount Hallasan.

A peace-themed center in Jungmun Tourist Complex, Seogwipo, built after Jeju was officially designated an island of world peace in 2005. Its exhibition halls use audiovisual displays to explain the political, geographic and environmental reasons behind the designation.
closed_days: Mon (2nd and 4th of each month); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A permanent circus venue in Seogwipo's Andeok area, opened in January 2004 as Korea's first venue for Chinese circus and motorcycle shows. The show with about 40 performers includes motorcycle stunts, bicycle acts and Chinese acrobatics, with lights and music.
closed_days: none (open year-round); days and show times may change, call ahead

description_en: Korea's only museum specializing in glass, with glass artworks displayed in a spacious setting. Visitors can watch work in the kiln and blowing rooms, and try workshops such as glass blowing and candle making.

A coffee museum at the foot of Daesusan peak in Seongsan, on Olle Trail Route 2. The first floor shows coffee beans from many countries and brewing tools, and advance booking allows a barista experience. The second floor is a cafe. Nearby: Light Bunker (빛의 벙커, museum, about 40 m).

An aerospace museum in Andeok, Seogwipo, with an aviation history hall displaying 26 real aircraft, an astronomy and space hall, and a theme hall with hands-on experiences. It offers exhibitions and education programs for students and visitors.

A museum in Seongsan, Seogwipo, where visitors learn about marine animals such as whale sharks, ocean sunfish and spider crabs through education and hands-on experiences. It displays about 10,000 specimens of roughly 800 marine animal species that visitors can observe up close.

The studio and exhibition space of well-known teddy bear artist Joan Oh in Jungmun Tourist Complex, Seogwipo. It displays teddy bears made from natural materials, and the hilltop grounds have about 50 pine trees over 100 years old and traditional stone walls.

A chocolate museum in Daejeong, Seogwipo, built with Jeju volcanic scoria in a style resembling a European castle. It traces the history of chocolate and cacao, and is the second-largest museum of its kind in the world and the first in Asia.

A large cultural complex on the coast facing the sea at Seongsan, with open ocean views. It has a restaurant serving steak, pizza, hot dogs and brunch, a cafe for drinks and desserts, and a goods shop selling its own products.
opening_hours: Local Seafood Market 11:30-21:30; Cafe & Bakery 10:30-19:30; KOKO Goods Shop 10:30-21:30

description_en: A theme museum in Jungmun, Seogwipo, combining teddy bears with Seoul's history, 20th-century world history, art and travel. It is Korea's first and largest display on the history of the teddy bear, which began in 1902.

A museum in Andeok, Seogwipo, opened in April 2021, focusing on diversity, the global environment and the voices of socially marginalized groups. It runs its own program, Salon de PODO, and has a cafe and gift shop on the first floor.

A museum in Andeok, Seogwipo, filled with action figures, movie statues and life-size movie character figures, along with upcycled healing art. It features figures from films, games and animation that appeal to all generations.

A baseball museum in Gangchanghak Sports Park in Seogwipo, opened in 1995. Its exhibits cover Korean and international baseball history with photos, gloves and bats, plus items from star players and an early MLB World Series ticket. Nearby: Seogwipo City Youth Training Center (서귀포시청소년수련관, sight, about 20 m).
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok holidays

name_en: Heonma Gongsin Kim Man-il Memorial Hall
description_en: A memorial hall in Seogwipo dedicated to Kim Man-il, a horse breeder who supplied thousands of war horses during national crises such as the Imjin War. The hall has screen riding and other horse experiences, exhibits on his achievements, and photo spots.
