A theme museum in Andeok, Seogwipo, celebrating 40 years of Hello Kitty with an exhibition hall, a 3D theater and a special gallery. The second floor has a Hello Kitty cafe, and the brand shop sells Hello Kitty goods.

An exhibition on gat making, the craft of the traditional horsehair hat once worn by yangban to shield from sun and rain. The craft was designated an Important Intangible Cultural Heritage in 1964, and Jeju was its center until the late Joseon period.

A hands-on museum in Hallim, Jeju, with replicas of masterpiece paintings and marble sculptures from the Louvre and Vatican museums that visitors can touch. A Greek village lets visitors dress as Greeks and join interactive exhibits.

A library in Jeju City donated by the late Kim Yeong-su, a graduate of Jeju Buk Elementary School. Since 2018 it has served both students and local residents as a school and community library. Nearby: Jeju City Saeuri (제주시새우리, restaurant, about 70 m).
opening_hours: School library: weekdays 08:30-16:30; community library: weekdays 17:00-21:00, weekends 10:00-18:00 (hours differ for students and residents, check before visiting)
closed_days: Sat, Sun, public holidays (school library); Tue, public holidays (community library)

description_en: A museum in Hallim, Jeju, with works by Kim Chang-yeol, known as the 'water drop painter', who donated 220 key pieces to found it. Architect Hong Jae-seung designed the building as eight large cube-shaped structures around a central courtyard.
opening_hours: Summer (Jul-Sep) 09:00-19:00; winter (Oct-Jun) 09:00-18:00 (last entry 30 minutes before closing)
closed_days: Mon (closed the next day if Monday is a public holiday); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: Opened in December 2019 in Jocheon, Jeju, to showcase the life and works of painter Kim Taek-hwa (1940-2006), who painted Jeju landscapes. It displays 122 of his oil paintings, and the second-floor cafe is set in a studio with large windows.

A small independent bookshop in a Samyang alley in Jeju City, with handwritten notes describing each book. Books are sorted by topic and include Jeju-related titles, indie publications and foreign books, and visitors can enjoy coffee while reading. Nearby: Warda Restaurant (와르다레스토랑, restaurant, about 80 m); Yunjae Coffee (윤재커피, cafe, about 60 m); Goyo Sanchaek (고요산책, cafe, about 40 m).

An independent bookshop in Hamdeok, Jocheon, Jeju, open since 2016, where travelers and locals can stay and rest with books. Its first and second branches stand side by side, close to the sea, making it a good stop on a walk.

A wildflower garden in Hangyeong, Jeju, with about 3,000 live wildflower species displayed by theme, collected over 30 years from around the world. It also has indoor exhibits, outdoor gardens and a cave, with frog sculptures hidden around the grounds.

An independent bookshop in Jongdal-ri, a small village at the eastern tip of Jeju in Gujwa. It has a quiet, cozy atmosphere with travel, literature, art and philosophy books, and comfortable seating for reading and relaxing.

Jeju's largest immersive media art exhibition hall, with nine themed spaces where visitors experience light and video art. It is an indoor attraction about 20 minutes by car from Jeju Airport, good for rainy days.

A visitor center at the Eorimok trailhead on Mount Hallasan, with exhibits on the mountain's formation, history, geology, legends and ecology. Its video room shows the World Natural Heritage promotion video and live CCTV views of the trails. Nearby: Hallasan Trekking (한라산 트레킹, sight, about 60 m).

The only independent bookshop on Udo island, housed in a building with traditional Jeju stone walls. Its name comes from an endangered coral found in Jeju's waters, and it stocks independent publications, drawing books and vegetarian titles, with sea views from the window. Nearby: Hahahoho (하하호호, restaurant, about 20 m).
closed_days: none (open year-round); irregular closures possible, check website or call

description_en: A museum dedicated to the architecture and philosophy of Yu Dong-ryong, born to Korean parents in Japan and known there as Itami Jun. His Jeju works include Ark Church, the Supungseok Museum and Podo Hotel, and the museum was designed by his daughter.

A gallery in Jeju City run by child painter and children's book author Jeon I-su. Admission fees go to a Jeju shelter for unmarried mothers, Doctors Without Borders and African charities, and the entrance shop sells goods and books by Jeon and her brother.

An indoor water show in Gujwa, Jeju, featuring big fountains, high-diving, tightrope acts and high falls, performed by troupes from several countries. It is considered Korea's first sky water show and includes world-champion divers.

An information center on the Gosanri Site in Hallim, Jeju, the oldest Neolithic site in Korea. Exhibits and guided explanations cover the site's history and excavations, including Gosanri-style pottery, considered Korea's first pottery.

A hands-on science center in Jeju City with physics, math, life and earth science exhibits, plus drones, space, robots and energy on the third floor. It includes a 3D theater, a planetarium and a library, and admission is free.
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok holidays

description_en: A museum opened in 1995 in Jeju City that collects and displays textbooks, teaching tools and documents on education from prehistoric times to the present. It has four permanent halls and uses real objects, videos and diorama displays.
closed_days: Mon; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok; temporary public holidays

description_en: A cultural and art complex in Jocheon, Jeju, set among the nature of Geomunoreum, a UNESCO World Natural Heritage site, and green tea fields. Visitors can ride a zipline over the fields, soak their feet in a foot bath, and see art galleries and night light displays.

A literature museum in Jeju City, opened in October 2021 to record Jeju's literary history and support local writers. It has permanent exhibitions, seminar rooms, creative spaces for writers and a large auditorium that hosts literary events.

A multipurpose performing arts venue in Jeju City, opened in May 2010, with 1,184 seats and an orchestra pit. It hosts classical concerts, musicals, plays and dance, with modern sound, lighting and stage systems.

A tourist information center in Jeju City run by the Jeju Tourism Organization. It offers general travel information, currency exchange, a tourism souvenir exhibit, photo and video studios, and a 240-seat multipurpose hall.

The world's first museum to display wild animals, sea animals, flowers and birds all as plush toys, in Aewol. Visitors can touch and photograph life-size stuffed animals and teddy bears, and children can play in a play area on the second floor.
opening_hours: Spring/autumn (Mar-Jun, Sep-Nov) 09:00-19:00 (last entry 18:00); summer (Jul-Aug) 08:30-19:00 (last entry 18:30); winter (Dec-Feb) 09:00-18:30 (last entry 17:40)

description_en: A memorial hall in Jocheon, Jeju, opened on Liberation Day in 1997, showing Jeju's anti-Japanese independence movements in chronological order. It covers the Jocheon Independence Movement of March 1919, the Beopjeongsa resistance and the haenyeo (women divers) resistance.
closed_days: none; closed on Jan 1 and during Seollal and Chuseok holidays (3 days each)

description_en: A contemporary art museum in Jeoji village, Jeju, opened in September 2007, with special, permanent and temporary exhibition galleries, an outdoor sculpture park and an outdoor performance space for 1,000 viewers. Painter Kim Heung-soo donated his major works to it.
opening_hours: Main building 09:00-18:00; public storage 09:15-17:30; ticket sales end 30 minutes before closing
closed_days: Mon (if Monday is a holiday, the next non-holiday day); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: An interactive exhibition in Aewol, Jeju, housed in an upcycled nursing hospital built about 50 years ago. Its five themed spaces reinterpret Jeju through installations and hands-on experiences.

A public library in Jocheon, Jeju, opened in 1999 and managed by Udang Library. It has a reading room with 250 seats, a calligraphy room, an information room, a multipurpose hall and a children's room.
opening_hours: General materials room: weekdays 08:00-22:00; weekends and public holidays 09:00-18:00. Reading and digital seats 08:00-22:00. Children's room 09:00-18:00.
closed_days: Fri; Dec 31; Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok; substitute holidays

name_en: Jujeong Factory Detention Camp 4.3 History Hall
description_en: A history hall on the site of a former alcohol factory from the Japanese colonial era. Its warehouses were later used as a civilian detention camp during the 4.3 period, and the hall commemorates victims who went missing.
closed_days: Mon (2nd and 4th of each month); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A small unmanned bookstore on a quiet alley in front of an elementary school. Its shelves hold picture books, children's books and essays that visitors can browse freely.

An exhibition hall dedicated to HARIBO gummy candies, with media art and games covering the brand's history and production process. It has photo spots and an upstairs art shop selling gummies and goods from around the world. Nearby: Pickus Jeju (피커스 제주, cafe, about 10 m).

A museum on Jeju's haenyeo, the women divers, covering their daily life, customs, rituals and the wider history and culture of the island. Many exhibits were donated by haenyeo, and a real haenyeo house is on display. Nearby: [Jeju Olle Course 21] Hado-Jongdal Olle ([제주올레 21코스] 하도-종달 올레, sight, about 10 m).
closed_days: Mon (if Monday is a public holiday, the next first non-holiday day); Jan 1; Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A cultural arts complex on Udo island with architecture and artworks by Friedensreich Hundertwasser, designed to blend with nature. It includes a museum on his life and works, an Udo gallery and a goods shop.
A Jeju Olle walking course across Gapado, the lowest inhabited island in Korea. Even a slow walk takes about two hours, and the island is a good place to rest for a day.
A coastal Olle trail that starts at Hwasun Geummorae Beach and ends at Hamo in Daejeong-eup, passing Sanbangsan, Songak and views of Marado and Gapado. Walkers also see Hallasan and the oreum hills.
A coastal and inland Olle trail from Mureung 2-ri to Yongsu Port, passing open fields, Dowon Pond and views of Chagwido island. Walkers also pass Suwolbong peak and the Saengi Gijeong coastal path.

The first Jeju Olle course, linking oreum hills, fields and the coast from Siheung to Gwangchigi Beach. From the hills walkers can see Seongsan Ilchulbong and Udo island, and a patchwork of black stone-walled fields.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 성산읍 시흥상동로 113 시흥리 버스정류장~광치기해변

description_en: A trail from Gwangchigi Beach to the Onpyeong coast, with quiet forest paths and a summit view of Jeju's east coast from Daesusanbong. Walkers also pass Honinji, a site linked to the Samseong myth.
An inland Olle course with old stone walls, camellia paths and citrus groves. Walkers enjoy views from Tongoreum and Dokjabong oreum hills, and visit the Kim Young-gap Gallery Dumoak.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 성산읍 온평리 1001-6 온평포구~제주민속촌 주차장 입구

description_en: A coastal Olle trail from Onpyeong Port past the Hwanhaejangseong sea wall and the Sinpung Sea Ranch, where the A and B courses meet. Walkers see the sea, grassland and wildflowers along the shore.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 성산읍 온평리 1001-6 온평포구~제주민속촌 주차장 입구

description_en: A coastal and village Olle trail from Namwon Port to Soesokkak, where fresh water meets sea water. Walkers pass the Geunyeong coastal walk and village streets lined with camellia trees. Nearby: Namwon Lava Seawater Pool (남원용암해수풀장, sight, about 40 m); Original Namwon Port Restaurant (원조남원포구식당, restaurant, about 90 m).

name_en: [Jeju Olle Course 6] Soesokkak-Jeju Olle Traveler Center Olle
description_en: A trail from Soesokkak Bridge through central Seogwipo, passing Sogeummak coast and Lee Jung-seop Street. Walkers enjoy panoramic sea views from the Seogwipo KAL Hotel path and the Honeymoon House observation deck. Nearby: Jemini Noodles and Gimbap (제미니국수김밥, restaurant, about 70 m).

name_en: [Jeju Olle Course 7-1] Seogwipo Bus Terminal-Jeju Olle Traveler Center Olle
description_en: A Jeju Olle course from Seogwipo Bus Terminal through the inland hills to the Olle Traveler Center. Walkers see Hallasan and the south coast, and pass rice paddies, which are rare on Jeju. Nearby: Sisterfield (시스터필드, cafe, about 80 m).
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 일주동로 9217 (법환동) 서귀포 버스터미널~제주올레 여행자센터

name_en: [Jeju Olle Course 7] Jeju Olle Traveler Center-Wolpyeong Olle
description_en: A coastal Olle course from the Olle Traveler Center past Beophwan Port to Wolpyeong. It features the Oedolgae rock stack and the Subong Trail, a path first cut by hand with simple tools. Nearby: Jinju Restaurant (진주식당, restaurant, about 100 m); Sambo Restaurant (삼보식당, restaurant, about 50 m).

A coastal Olle course along the blue sea, passing columnar joint cliffs and the Yerae Ecological Park, which has flowers in every season. It ends in Daepyeong, a small village with a relaxed atmosphere.
A diving company in Seogwipo offering scuba diving, trial dives, open water courses and boat dives at sites such as Munseom island. It also runs night dives and a guesthouse for divers.
A shooting and ATV adventure park in Seogwipo, offering hunting, pistol, clay and rifle shooting, plus ATV and buggy rides in nature. Visitors must be at least 14 years old.

A forest trail in Hannam-ri, Seogwipo, combining wide pastures, grassland and virgin forest. Walkers pass a stone wall, an old farmhouse site, a cypress grove and the Seojungcheon observation deck, and guided tours are available.

A campground in Seongsan run by Seogwipo City, divided into several zones. Facilities include carts, parking, a playground, a fitness area, toilets, a kitchen, showers and a walking path, and each site has an electric hookup.

A diving school in Seogwipo with trial dives for beginners and open water and other scuba courses that follow PADI standards. It holds monthly events and offers consultation and services for foreign travelers.

A 6.5 km walking path along Beonyeong Road from Jeonguihyeon Crossroads toward Pyoseon Beach, with flowers and trees on both sides. Quiet hours with little traffic are a good time to find photo spots.

name_en: View Jeju Sky Horse Riding Park
description_en: A horse riding park in Seongsan where visitors ride up and down the Nasiri oreum hill to its summit. From the top, views include Udo island, Jiminbong peak, Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hallasan.
A cedar-lined forest trail in Pyoseon, one of Jeju's 31 hidden scenic spots. It runs from Bija Forest Road past Mulchat Oreum to Saryeoni Oreum, and many tree species grow along the way.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 표선면 가시리 붉은오름 입구
opening_hours: 09:00-17:00 (summer Apr-Sep: entry closes 14:00; winter Oct-Mar: entry closes 12:00)
closed_days: none (open year-round; access may be restricted in rain or heavy snow)

description_en: A caravan and camping site in Gangjeong village in Seogwipo, near Olle Course 7 and Beomseom island. Visitors can stay in fully equipped caravans or camp on the lawn.

An indoor swimming pool in Seogwipo that opened in 2020, with seawater pools kept above 30 degrees year-round. It offers adult, child and infant lessons across nine lanes, with views over Seogwipo from the first floor.
Jeju's first horse riding ground, set against a wide field, with trails for beginners and experienced riders alike. Riding gear is provided free of charge, and the parking area is spacious.

A leisure theme park beside the Seogwipo World Cup Stadium, with kart racing where visitors drive their own karts. It also has a maze park decorated with camellia-lined paths. Nearby: Angkeure Noodles Seogwipo Main Branch (앙끄레국수 서귀포본점, restaurant, about 80 m).
closed_days: none (open year-round; closed when raining, call ahead)

description_en: A licensed horse riding park in Seongsan next to Seongsan Ilchulbong and Gwangchigi Beach, suitable for beginners and experienced riders. Expert instructors teach safety and technique, and the park has been used as a TV and film location.
A campground in Seogwipo at about 600 m elevation on Hallasan, surrounded by clean nature. It has a swimming pool, an outdoor hot spring and campfires, and is good for families and friends.

A horse riding park in Andeok that offers rides across private oreum hills, regular lessons and a pony club. Visitors can feed the horses, and children can ride on oreum trails with staff who take photos.

A horse riding park in Seongeup, Pyoseon, offering pony riding and horse feeding for children. Parents can relax with coffee at the cafe, and the safe courses suit first-time riders. Nearby: Bokdwaeji Restaurant (복돼지식당, restaurant, about 100 m).

A camping and stay site in Seongsan that blends hotels and camping, with distinctive lodgings in the mid-mountain area of Jeju. Camping gear is available for one person or for families, and it suits first-time campers.
A caravan campground beside Taeheung Port in Namwon, with round Airstream caravans arranged around a large lawn. The sea is in front and the foothills of Hallasan are behind.

A horse riding park near Seongeup Folk Village that specializes in guided trail rides. It offers beginner lessons and horses for each skill level, with large meadows, small oreum hills and pampas grass fields.
closed_days: none; closed on Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A kart theme park in Topyeong, Seogwipo, with a family kart course that offers views of Hallasan. It also has Jeju's only indoor BB pellet survival zone.
opening_hours: 10:00-18:30 (prep time 11:30-12:30; ticket sales end 18:00; early close at sunset)

description_en: A yacht tour with a large panoramic glass floor for viewing marine life below the sea. The tour also points out Sanbangsan, Yongmeori Coast, Hyeongje island and Songak, and is good for photos.
A horse riding park on a wide meadow near Moguri Alo oreum in Seongsan, with views of Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hallasan. Trained horses and courses of varied difficulty suit beginners and families.

A camping site in Namwon, Seogwipo, with caravans and a pension by the sea, offering ocean views, a large parking lot and a palm-lined garden. Olle Market is a 20-minute drive away. Nearby: Okdom Village (옥돔마을, restaurant, about 60 m).
A football stadium in Seogwipo next to the bus terminal, built for the 2002 FIFA World Cup with 42,256 seats. Its stands and decks offer views of the sea, islands and Hallasan.

A marine leisure company in Jungmun Tourist Complex offering parasailing, with views of coastal cliffs, Hallasan and nearby islands from 30 to 200 meters above the sea. Staff hold lifeguard and rowing licenses. Nearby: Jungmun Haenyeo House (중문해녀의집, restaurant, about 100 m).

An 18-hole golf course in Jungmun Tourist Complex, built in 1981 along coastal cliffs and a valley with a stream. Non-members can play by advance reservation, and the course changes character with each season.

An off-road experience park in Seogwipo offering ATV, buggy and Wrangler jeep rides on unpaved roads. Adults with a driver's license can take part, passengers can ride along, and horse riding is also available.

A kart racing experience near Jungmun Tourist Complex, where people of all ages can ride single or double karts for about 10 to 15 minutes. Children may ride with an adult, and a short safety briefing comes first.
closed_days: none (open year-round; may not operate in bad weather)

description_en: A golf club in Andeok, Seogwipo, with views of Hallasan and the Hallim coast. Opened in 1995, it hosted the Samsung World Championship, an official LPGA Tour event, and its links-style course follows the shape of Jeju's oreum hills.

A new campground on Yeongcheon Oreum in Seogwipo, with trails over the oreum and views of Jeju's coast. It has modern caravans with four glass walls and glamping units, and the facilities are clean and ready to use.

A free campground at the entrance of Pyoseon Beach, with grass sites under a pine forest that serves as a windbreak. It has a sink and drinking fountain but no shower, and is popular with solo and family campers.
A 12 km coastal road linking Sehwa in Gujwa-eup to Pyoseon Beach on Jeju's east coast. Viewpoints along the way show Tokki island, Udo island and Seongsan, and a stone bridge crosses the sea.

The first course of Hayeong Olle, a walking route through Seogwipo's old downtown that starts and ends at Seogwipo City Hall. It follows the Cheonjiyeon Falls stream and passes Geolmae Ecological Park and Arangjoeul Food Street. Nearby: Hayeong Olle Course 3 (하영올레 3코스, sight, about 10 m); Hayeong Olle Course 2 (하영올레 2코스, sight, about 10 m).

name_en: Hallasan Trail Dol-oreum Course (Borim Farm Crossroads to Georinsaseum Oreum)
description_en: A 9-section forest trail circling Mount Hallasan through woods, grasslands, oreum hills and streams. This second section runs about 8 km from Borim Farm crossroads to the Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest entrance, passing Yong Rock.

An eco-friendly gravity racing theme park in Aewol, Jeju, with downhill races facing the sea and uphill races facing Hallasan. It has four courses and ten tracks, plus kart rides suitable for children. Nearby: Space Zero (스페이스제로, cafe, about 10 m).

Jeju Olle Course 14 winds through green forest paths, farmland roads and a dry streambed before reaching the coast. Walkers see the rocky shoreline and the island of Biyang along the way. Nearby: Jeju Olle Course 14-1: Jeoji-Seogwang Olle ([제주올레 14-1코스] 저지-서광 올레, sight, about 10 m).

name_en: Jeju Olle Course 17: Gwangnyeong-Jeju Old Downtown Olle
description_en: Jeju Olle Course 17 follows forest trails along Musucheon Stream to the sea, then continues past Ihotteu Beach and Dodobong Peak into Jeju City. Yongduam Rock and Yongyeon Bridge are also along the route.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 제주시 애월읍 광성로 242-1 호끌락키즈북카페~김만덕 기념관

description_en: Jeju Olle Course 19 links the sea, oreum hills, forests, villages and fields. Along the way, Jocheon Manse Hill recalls Jeju's anti-Japanese movement, and Neobeunsungi 4.3 Memorial Hall in Bukchon-ri commemorates the 4.3 tragedy.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 제주시 조천읍 조천북6길 44 조천만세동산 맞은편~김녕서포구

description_en: Jeju Olle Course 20 starts at Gimnyeong Seopo and follows the northeast coast past Gimnyeong, Woljeong and Sehwa with clear blue waters. Lucky visitors may see haenyeo (female divers) at work and hear their sumbisori breath sounds.

Golche Oreum Camping is a family campground with a central lawn where children can play safely. Free rentals of soccer balls, badminton sets and jump ropes are available, and the clean restrooms include accessible facilities.

Gwaneumsa Campground sits at about 620 m elevation on the Gwaneumsa trail of Hallasan, just north of Jeju City. The trail to the Baengnokdam crater lake is 8.7 km long and passes deep valleys and rugged peaks.
closed_days: none (open year-round); may be fully closed due to weather on Hallasan, check the website before visiting

description_en: Gwideok Sea Transparent Kayak lets visitors paddle clear-bottomed kayaks off the Gwideok breakwater in Hallim. Beginners practice inside the calm breakwater first, then head to open sea and watch fish swim beside the kayak. Nearby: Cafe Cola (카페콜라, cafe, about 70 m).

Gyulbit Camping Site in Daheul-ri, Jocheon-eup, has 35 crushed-stone sites with electricity, hot water, restrooms, showers and a cooking area. Without a tent, guests can book a 4-person tent, caravan, natural house or private pension.

Geumneung Beach Campground sits under a grove of palm trees 20 to 30 m tall, right next to Hyeopjae Beach. Campers can pitch tents freely within the area and enjoy the sea view in a relaxed, simple atmosphere.

Gimnyeong is a dolphin habitat, where visitors can watch dolphins swim alongside the eco-friendly aluminum sailing yacht BONA520. The tour also offers fine dining with local seafood such as abalone, octopus and raw fish.
closed_days: none (open year-round); sailing is suspended in bad weather, call before visiting

description_en: Dolhareubang Camping Ground in Hanggyeong-myeon has a wide lawn with a pool, a footvolley court and campfire facilities. The pool and footvolley court are free for campers, and reservations are by phone only.
Raon Golf Club is set in a natural warm-temperate forest in Hanggyeong-myeon, with Stone, Lake and Pine courses. Hallasan, seven surrounding oreum hills and the blue sea are visible from the course.

name_en: Horse Theme Park Golf Course (Let's Run Park Jeju)
description_en: This large park golf course by Jeju Racecourse blends golf and gateball and suits all ages. Its learning garden of wildflowers is shaped after Jeju's oreum hills and cliffs.
closed_days: Mon-Thu; Seollal and Chuseok; public holidays

description_en: Mugeo Caravan is a campground on the Hamdeok coastal road offering caravans and pensions, with fully equipped interiors. The Sinheung house is a private jacuzzi pension with an ocean view. Nearby: Mugeo Burger (무거버거, restaurant, about 30 m).

Munseupeu is the first surf shop in northwest Jeju, located in Gwakji-ri, Aewol-eup. It offers surfing lessons, gear rental and sales, a surf-themed cafe, and photo service with a professional photographer.

Baengdi Horse Riding Club is a riding ground with wide grasslands, offering a grassland route, a forest route, or both together. Riders can enjoy views of oreum hills and cypress forests around the club.
Byeolhaneun Bam Glamping sits at 200 m elevation in Yusuam-ri, Aewol-eup, with five glamping domes and two caravans. Nearby are Jeju Airport, Gwakji Beach, Hyeopjae Beach and Ihotteu Beach.

Black Stone Golf Club is set in the Gotjawal forest area of Jeju, with ancient trees transplanted to the course. Players see oreum hills on the south course, and Hallasan from holes 7 and 8 on the north course.

Samdasu Horse Riding Ranch sits on the eastern slope of Hallasan, with forests and grasslands. It offers basic, double, ranch and walking courses, and the longest walking course passes through the woods of Gyorae-ri.
Samdasu Forest Trail is a geological trail built on a forest road, where cedar trees planted in the 1970s now form dense woods. It is part of Jeju's geopark and has rare plant colonies.

Seuobong Trail is a coastal path east of Hamdeok Beach, part of Jeju Olle Course 19. Yellow rapeseed flowers bloom in spring along the emerald shore, and the summit is a popular spot for New Year sunrise viewing.
Songdang Horse Riding Ranch offers short routes, walking trails and one-hour free riding. It suits all ages, and beginners can learn riding from instructors.

This sea fishing experience park near Hamdeok Beach in Jocheon-eup operates in all seasons regardless of weather. Visitors catch fish from the sea, and the catch can be eaten fresh as raw fish on site.

Everis Golf Resort is a traditional golf course in Aewol-eup that uses Jeju's oreum hills, rocks, sea and wind in its design. Hallasan is visible to the east, while open grasslands and the sea spread to the west.

Eco Green Camping Ground in Aewol-eup is about 15 minutes from central Jeju City. It has wide 6x7 deck sites and a 12x8 gravel site, accepts caravans and campers, and is surrounded by traditional Jeju stone walls.
Eco Horse Riding Academy is near Saryeoni Forest in Jocheon-eup, offering riding for beginners and advanced riders. Its children's riding programs include forest, valley and grassland rides.
closed_days: none (open year-round); closed in rain, call before visiting

description_en: Eco Hill Glamping in Aewol-eup offers views of Hallasan and Jeju City in a quiet setting near the city. From May to September a swimming pool operates, and campfires are held in the evening.

Elysian Jeju Country Club in Aewol-eup offers rounds with views of Hallasan and the sea off Hallim. Its four courses showcase Jeju's nature, and the resort also hosts corporate seminars, events and hotel-class lodging.
opening_hours: 20 min before sunrise to 20 min after sunset (varies by season and club schedule)

description_en: Golfzone County Ora is one of Jeju's leading golf courses, with an international-standard 36-hole layout along the Yeonggu-chunhwa valley below Hallasan. It is open all year and offers a One Caddie One Bag service.

Ongpocheon Eoul Park Pool is a free summer-only pool in western Jeju, open each year from July to August. It uses cold natural spring water from the Ongpo stream and has a foot bath, showers and changing rooms.

Woljeong Transparent Kayak on the Woljeong-ri coast lets visitors paddle clear-bottom kayaks over calm water, and with luck they can see fish swimming below. Dogs can come along when booked with two people, but dog life vests are not provided.

Jayeonin Pension and Glamping is 5 minutes from central Jeju City, with a pension, outdoor stage, cafe, workshop and restaurant. Nearby sights include Ecoland, Yongduam Rock and the Saryeoni Forest Trail. Nearby: Jeonggane Bapsang Jeju Smart Farm (정가네밥상 제주스마트팜, restaurant, about 10 m).

Jerajin Adventure offers off-road tours through 429,752 m2 of grassland and forest in Jocheon-eup, where horses, roe deer and pheasants roam freely. Visitors can take off-road routes or RC car tours along paths horses once used.

Jeju Seopingdo is Jeju's first indoor surfing park, with a warm pool open 365 days and artificial waves for many surfers at once. Its trampoline floor makes falls soft, and certified instructors guide beginners.

Jeju Rail Bike lets riders cruise along a rail track on four-wheeled bikes, with views of oreum hills, Udo Island and Seongsan Ilchulbong. The bikes are electric-powered so no pedaling is needed, and a rain cover keeps riders dry.
opening_hours: Summer (Mar-Oct) 09:00-17:30; Winter (Nov-Feb) 09:00-17:00; call for details in bad weather

description_en: Jeju Leports Land is a leisure theme park offering European racing karts, survival games, zip line, mountain ATVs, all-season sledding and shooting. Its kart track includes drift-friendly curves, S-curves and hills.

Jeju Best Hill Glamping and Pension sits beneath Banong Oreum in the Gotjawal forest on Namjo-ro, about 20 to 30 minutes from Jeju Airport. Pension rooms are themed around camellia, herb, meditation, family and experience.

Jeju Belita Camping Ground, formerly Jeju Base Camp, is about 30 minutes from Jeju Airport and next to the coastal road. Its sites on crushed volcanic rock stay dry in rain, and each has its own parking and power.
Jeju Big Ball Land offers zorb rides in which people roll down a slope inside a large ball. The water-filled Big Ball course runs about 300 m, and the dry Zorb course about 170 m with two riders.
opening_hours: 10:00-17:00 (weather may affect operation; call before visiting)

description_en: Jeju Horse Riding Park in Aewol-eup offers horse shows, couple and children's riding camps, and corporate workshops, with the longest trekking route on the central mountain grasslands. Beginners can learn with top instructors and safety care.

Jeju Youth Training Center is a facility for the healthy growth of young people, with sports, cultural programs and camps in a wide natural setting. It offers chances for self-development and social experience.

Tap Horse Riding Club sits in Jeju's mid-mountain area, with clean air and oreum views. It offers programs for beginners and advanced riders, and it is near Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest and the 4.3 Peace Park.

Jeju Platinum Caravan sits right on the Aewol shore, 20 minutes from Jeju Airport, among palm trees. Guests can swim, snorkel, trap octopus and catch crabs or bomal (sea snails), and the walk connects to Jeju Olle Course 16.

Jeju Port Breakwater is a shore fishing spot that is busy year-round, with tetrapods to cast from. Anglers often catch black porgy, sea bass and red porgy, and national sea fishing contests are held here. Nearby: Haejin Raw Fish Restaurant (해진횟집, restaurant, about 20 m).

Jeju Holsta Horse Riding Ground sits at the foot of Eoseungsaengak on Hallasan, with programs for beginners, lessons and trail rides through the oreum hills. Children's courses are structured, and some rides pass through cypress forests.

Chagwido is a striking island about 10 minutes by boat from Jagu-naepo in Hanggyeong-myeon, with deep waters holding red sea bream, rock bream, black sea bream and other fish. Small boats with fishing gear can be rented.

A water sports center on Jeju's western sea, offering sailing yachts and power fishing boats with a rescue boat and lifeguards on standby. Trips pass close to Dangsan Cliffs and Chagwido Island, with fishing, snorkeling, and sailing alongside southern bottlenose dolphins. Nearby: Jeju Olle Trail Course 13 (Yongsu-Jeoji Olle) ([제주올레 13코스] 용수-저지 올레, sight, about 20 m).

Section 1 of the Hallasan Circular Trail, an 8.7 km route from Cheona Reservoir to the Borim Farm crossroads. It passes several oreum (volcanic cones) and the hidden marsh Sumeunmulbaedi at about 1,000 m elevation on Hallasan's slopes.
address_ko: 제주특별자치도 제주시 애월읍 광령리 천아숲길입구(천아계곡)~보림농장 삼거리

description_en: A golf course opened in 1998 at the lowest elevation of any golf course in Jeju, about 25 minutes from the airport. It has a 31-room golf village and a renovated clubhouse and course, and it is open for rounds year-round.

A horse riding ground opened in 1983, with about 80 trained Halla horses and ponies, suitable for first-time riders. Visitors wear a riding helmet before mounting and must follow instructor guidance throughout the ride.

A golf course on the slopes of Hallasan at about 400 m elevation, with mountain views behind it and the southern sea spread out in front. It was built with the aim of offering a course that stays mild even in winter.

A leisure complex on the outskirts of Jeju City combining horse riding with ranch experiences, set in a western-themed space with a large grassland. Beginners can move from walk to gallop with instructor help, and clear days offer views of the sea and Hallasan.
opening_hours: summer (Mar-Oct) 09:00-19:00, prep 13:00-14:00, last departure 18:30; winter (Nov-Feb) 09:00-17:00, prep 13:00-14:00, last departure 16:30

description_en: A fairly large five-day market in Goseong-ri, near Seongsan Ilchulbong and beside National Route 12. It sells fresh produce, seafood, meat, housewares, clothing, farm tools, and general goods, with a rural market atmosphere. Nearby: Jieunine Bapsang (지은이네밥상, restaurant, about 60 m).

Opened during the Korean War, this is the largest oil market in western Jeju, located in Hamo-ri, Daejeong-eup, and also called Mosulpo Market. It sells a wide range of goods, including items for fishermen, and has many food options for a quick meal. Nearby: Nabi Garden (나비정원, cafe, about 90 m).

A small, neat traditional market in Daejeong-eup, popular with local residents and known for appearing on a Jeju TV program. It sells fresh seafood and daily goods, and nearby restaurants are known for mung bean pancakes and sea urchin gimbap.

A five-day market opened in 1995 that is one of the largest traditional markets in Seogwipo, held on the 4th and 9th of each month. It sells seasonal fruit, fresh seafood, vegetables, small goods, and clothing, with ample parking and nearby bus stops.

The largest and oldest permanent market in central Seogwipo, busy with locals and travelers all year. Known for citrus fruit such as hallabong, fish, and black pork, with specialty shops selling Jeju silver hairtail, fresh mackerel, and golden threadfish. Nearby: Ppolsaljip Main Branch (뽈살집 본점, restaurant, about 80 m); Nammaenae Wanggalchi (남매네왕갈치, restaurant, about 80 m); Captain Clubhouse Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market Branch (캡틴클럽하우스 서귀포매일올레시장점, restaurant, about 60 m).

A traditional market in the Jungmun Tourist Complex, formed in the 1950s and officially opened in 1965. It mainly sells home-grown produce and seafood, with an old-style country market feel and many things to see and buy. Nearby: Bullanji Night Market (불란지야시장, market, about 30 m); Mano Coffee House (마노커피하우스, cafe, about 90 m); Jeju Halla Noodles (제주한라국수, restaurant, about 50 m).

A small traditional market in central Pyoseon, held on the 2nd and 7th of each month. It has three buildings: general goods and produce, a fish market beside Pyoseon Port, and small restaurants serving pork sausage soup and meat noodles.

A traditional market connected to the Dongmun Market in Jeju City, known for Jeju specialties such as tangerines, golden threadfish, black pork, meat noodles, and omegi rice cakes. It is convenient for buying gifts on the way to the airport. Nearby: Abebebe Bakery (아베베베이커리, cafe, about 60 m).

A cooperative fish market about 15 minutes by car from Jeju International Airport, where fresh fish is brought in each morning and auctioned. Visit early to see the auction; it sells silver hairtail, filefish, golden threadfish, and hanchi squid, and nearby raw fish centers will prepare your catch.

A traditional folk market next to the main crossroads in central Sehwa, where residents and merchants trade side by side. Held every five days, it offers a wide variety of goods at fairly low prices. Nearby: Hangari Jorim (항아리조림, restaurant, about 90 m).

A permanent market in Hallim that is open every day, alongside the five-day Hallim market. It is smaller than other daily markets but sells farm, livestock, and seafood items plus clothing and side dishes, and is mostly used by locals. Nearby: Boyeong Banjeom (보영반점, restaurant, about 50 m).

A traditional five-day market in western Hallim, also called Hallim Jokkeutre Market, a Jeju dialect name meaning close by. It sells household goods, farm tools, clothing, and fresh seafood, with a blacksmith and the port nearby.

A traditional five-day market in Hamdeok-ri, Jeju City, facing Hamdeok Beach, with market days on the 1st and 6th. It sells clothing, produce, hardware, dried fish, and side dishes, with good fish and traditional street food.

A large ocean-view brunch cafe in a three-story building by the sea near Seogwipo Girls' High School. The rooftop has wide views of Hallasan and the blue sea, and the grounds have photo spots, with pink sunsets over the water.

A puffer fish restaurant in Seogwipo, opened in 1966 and run by the same family for generations. It cooks only blowfish landed at Hallim Port each day, serving puffer soup, grilled puffer, and fried puffer, with raw puffer as the signature dish.

A cafe near Seogwipo Port named after 'an open space between trees', with an indoor courtyard and plants inside and out. It makes its own syrups, yogurt, and citrus cordial, and on days without desserts visitors may bring outside food.

A stone pot rice restaurant on Jungmun Tourist Road, opened in 2003 by a family whose mother was a haenyeo diver. Abalone or fresh raw fish comes with every meal, and the sea urchin seaweed soup and mixed seafood stone pot rice are popular.

A garden cafe on the road to Ettoo Waterfall near Seogwipo, run by a couple who have farmed citrus for three generations. Pets can join you in the outdoor garden, and couples book snap photo shoots; tangerine picking is offered from October.

A restaurant in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, serving noodle dishes and boiled pork in a vintage-style space. Its handmade meat skewers are grilled and served on a long wooden board, and the Noru Hanpan platter is designed for sharing.

A noodle restaurant in Seogwipo known for handmade noodles and a broth simmered for 12 hours, serving meat noodle soup. Sea urchin and abalone are added generously, and the restaurant has 88 seats and a private parking lot.

A cafe in a converted old warehouse along the Hyeongje Coastal Road in Sagye, Seogwipo, with a mascot cat named Boreum. Coffee is made with beans from a well-known roastery, and you can choose between a smooth nutty bean and a bean with a sweet fruity aroma. Nearby: Jeju Seonchaehyang (제주선채향, restaurant, about 90 m).

A raw fish restaurant at the entrance to Seongsanpo Ferry Terminal, recommended by local taxi drivers. It serves fresh mackerel sashimi, hairtail sashimi, and grilled mackerel, plus abalone and sea urchin seaweed soup and spicy noodles.

A grilled freshwater eel restaurant in Seogwipo, serving eel with herbal sauce, chili sauce, and salt, plus eel rice bowl and eel soup. Side dishes include mussel soup and raw beef, and private rooms can be booked for group meals.

A raw fish restaurant at Moseulpo Port in Daejeong-eup that also sells raw fish to take away. Signature items include the Kim Seonjang Box, a boxed selection of raw fish and seafood, along with horned turban shell, sweet shrimp, and wild sea bream.

A restaurant in Daepyeong-ri, Seogwipo, serving Jeju black pork grilled with an ocean view, although no major attractions are nearby. A two-person portion comes with shrimp doenjang stew, and the meat is dipped in fermented damselfish sauce.

A Jeju home-cooking restaurant near Hoesu village hall on the Jungsan-gan Seo-ro road in Seogwipo. It is known for abalone stone pot rice with abalone liver sauce, along with hairtail stew and a bone soup made with buckwheat flour and radish.

A traditional tea house in Jeju that makes all of its menu items in-house, including cooked Ssanghwa tea, jujube tea, and grilled rice cakes. Desserts include red bean and rice cake bingsu, and traditional tea sets come with rice cake and yanggeng.

A quiet, simple restaurant in a remodeled tangerine warehouse in Changcheon-ri, Andeok-myeon. It serves a single set meal of homemade soybean paste stew and grilled bulgogi with barley rice on round trays, and is closed when ingredients run out.

A pork cutlet restaurant near Haebichi Beach in Pyoseon, with ocean views from the window and outdoor seating when the weather allows. Its cutlets are paired with local Jeju ingredients, and the garden has swings and a pavilion for children. Nearby: Dangke Olle Noodles (당케올레국수, restaurant, about 70 m).

A former racehorse ranch that was closed to outsiders for about 70 years and is now open to visitors, with a large grassland and bamboo forest. The cafe is in a converted stone warehouse, and horses can be seen on the outdoor farm.

A specialty coffee cafe across from Andeok Middle School in Andeok-myeon, where a real golden retriever lives. Pets are welcome, coffee is hand-brewed from freshly roasted beans, and the cafe serves only coffee and drinks, with no snacks or bakery.

A hangover soup restaurant in Jungmun that opens at 7 a.m., popular for a Jeju breakfast while traveling. Its beef neck bone broth is simmered for over 12 hours for a clear, deep taste, and signature dishes include beef neck bone hangover soup and mountain-style hangover soup.

A cafe in a citrus orchard in Samdal-ri, Seongsan-eup, in a white building styled after Santorini. Large windows look out over the orchard, with natural lighting and plants inside, and signature items include the green tangerine latte and cookie choux.

A grilled Jeju black pork restaurant in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo, cooked over coal briquettes. Staff grill the meat for you, and side dishes such as bracken fern can be refilled at the self-service bar.

An outdoor grill restaurant near the carbonated hot spring at Sanbangsan in Sagye-ri, Andeok-myeon. Guests grill pork belly on a pot lid over firewood, camping-style, and staff explain the grilling method; outdoor seating is by reservation only.

A jjamppong restaurant in Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, that uses buckwheat grown on Jeju instead of wheat flour, giving the noodles a distinct texture that is easy to digest. Served spicy, white, or seafood style, and the sweet and sour pork comes in a fried chip bowl.

A restaurant in Seogwipo that has served the same single set meal for over 15 years. Braised mackerel, grilled golden threadfish, and seafood stew come with every meal, plus homemade seasonal namul and kimchi that change with the season.

A traditional noodle restaurant at the Wimi entrance crossroads in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, serving noodles in a neat, stylish set-meal style. Its molmang noodles, made with Jeju beef bones and sea mustard, are the signature, and set options include boiled pork slices and dumplings.

A cafe about 2 minutes by car from Gwangchigi Beach in Seongsan, with a lawn plaza, a stone-walled castle, and a carousel. Its studio-like interior is good for photos, and themed caravans can be booked for private parties with views of Seongsan Ilchulbong.

A dessert cafe near Kal Hotel in Seogwipo, decorated with plants and small props, with a lawn and small walking path that overlooks Seopseom Island. Signature drinks are lime coffee, orange coffee, and hagyul coffee, made with homemade citrus syrup and espresso.

A coffee shop beside Sinyang Seopji Beach in Seongsan-eup, with large windows and ocean views and a narrow white interior. The signature Island Tea and photogenic cafe mocha and mousse cake are popular, and the second floor is restricted to adults only.

A lemon-themed cultural complex in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, combining a lemon farm, a cafe, and a gallery. Drinks and desserts are made from pesticide-free lemons grown on site, and visitors can tour the farm or join harvesting and lemon syrup making programs.

A restaurant in Namwon-eup, Seogwipo, near the Keunong Coastal Scenic Area and surrounded by pine and palm trees. The name means dull ice flower, and the first floor has a lively pub-style feel, while the second floor has a quiet terrace with hammocks.
A garden cafe in front of Mt. Sanbang with European hydrangeas, roses and camellias and views of the sea. Its pink muhly grass garden, which blooms from August, is a popular photo spot.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:30 (last order 18:00); may vary by season, call to confirm

description_en: A restaurant in a quiet residential area of Jungmun known for cutlassfish dishes. Its signature is boneless braised Jeju cutlassfish, and whole grilled cutlassfish is also popular.
A bakery cafe in Wimi-ri, Namwon, with a large lawn and patio tables where children can play. Dogs are allowed, and the red-brick warehouse-style building has a modern interior and desserts.
A gallery cafe near Ttarabi Oreum in Gasi-ri, Pyoseon, serving coffee from several countries and freshly roasted beans for sale. The vintage interior is cozy, and pasta and bagels are also served.
A cafe in Daejeong with a rough rock-textured exterior and an angled rooftop. A sloped walkway on the roof offers panoramic views of western Jeju, and the courtyard has a pond.
A cafe near Deokdol Port on Olle Trail Course 4, with a bright yellow exterior and retro decor such as vintage typewriters and CRT televisions. It serves specialty coffee and homemade bread.

A ranch cafe that also runs a working farm, with a cozy interior and windows overlooking the pasture. Visitors can try horse riding, bicycles and feeding animals, and walk a trail covered in volcanic cinder.

A ranch cafe in Pyoseon with an indoor space facing the open fields. Activities include horse riding, cart rides and feeding animals, and the outdoor grassland has many photo spots and special bicycles.

A rest stop on the coast of Olle Trail Course 1 near Seongsan, popular for grilled semi-dried squid that visitors eat outdoors by the sea. Convenience store drinks, instant noodles and alcohol are also sold.
A cafe in Seogwipo with a black-toned exterior that feels like an art museum. Every seat faces a window onto a green garden, and traditional clay jars decorate the interior.

A grilled meat restaurant in an apartment complex in Gangjeong, near Seogwipo Bus Terminal. The pork is grilled over charcoal and dipped in a Jeju fermented anchovy sauce with salt and wasabi. Nearby: Hwago Sinsigaji Branch (화고 신시가지점, restaurant, about 60 m).

A hanok bakery cafe near Sindo Port in Seogwipo, named after a Korean word meaning trustworthy. Behind the building is a garden with a pond, fountain, pavilion, swings and seesaws. Known for salt bread and red bean bread.
A cafe in Daepo near Jungmun Tourist Complex with views of the sea. Guests can enjoy non-alcoholic ades, coffee and draft beer while sitting toward the water.
A sheep ranch-themed cafe in Donggwang that is good for families with children. Guests can see sheep from the window and buy feed for a feeding experience. Drinks use Jeju ingredients.

A seafood restaurant in front of Pyoseon Beach run by an experienced chef, known for wild Jeju shrimp. The signature Batata raw fish set includes raw shrimp and a choice of sushi, boneless cutlassfish or noodles.

A Thai restaurant in Daejeong-eup with a spacious interior of red brick walls, plants, tile decor and rattan chairs. A cart-style self-service bar and Thai seasonings on each table add to the atmosphere.

A seafood restaurant run by the village fishing cooperative, where haenyeo (female divers) take turns working. It overlooks Gwangchigi Beach and Seongsan Ilchulbong, and the seafood platter includes abalone, whelk and sea squirt caught that day. Nearby: Horang Horang Seongsan Cafe (호랑호랑 성산카페, cafe, about 70 m).

A Mexican restaurant in an apartment complex in Seogwipo's English Education City. Known for palm-sized tacos and quesadillas, with burritos, nachos and chips, in a casual setting popular with locals.

A cafe on the coast at Beopwhan Port near Beomseom, with a semicircular bunker-shaped building and large glass windows facing the sea. Popular drinks include the bunker cream peanut latte and vanilla latte.

A cafe at the foot of Wolla Oreum in Hyodon-dong, with a gray exposed-concrete building and a green garden seen through floor-to-ceiling windows. There is a large parking lot, and Soesokkak is nearby.
A bakery cafe in Seogwipo with a wide ocean view of Seogwi Port and Munseom. It operates alongside Hotel Seogwipian, bakes goods fresh each day, and roasts its own beans.

A restaurant with sea views serving Jeju black pork neck and belly, about 600g, grilled over charcoal briquettes by staff. A free cafe on the second floor is for customers waiting for a table or relaxing after the meal.

A Chinese restaurant run by a chef with 20 years of experience, known for jjamppong made with spinach noodles pulled in-house. The broth mixes beef and seafood stock, the spice level can be adjusted, and there are private rooms.
opening_hours: Weekdays: 11:00-20:50; prep time 14:50-17:30; last order 19:50. Weekends: 11:00-20:50; last order 19:50

description_en: A cafe in Jungmun-dong near Jungmun High School, in a converted former tangerine warehouse with a vintage exterior and tall ceilings lit by natural light. Plants and decor fill the interior, and it is good for photos.
A black pork restaurant in Daejeong-eup with open outdoor tables among tangerine trees. Known for friendly service and a good stew, and waits can be long, so reservations are recommended.

A French-style bakery in a residential area near Jeju World Cup Stadium, using organic flour, cream and butter. Signature items include mille-feuille with butter, pretzels, Swiss bread and Portuguese egg tarts, plus coffee drinks.

A local seafood restaurant at Moseulpo Port, run by the owner who catches the fish on their own boat. Its 45-year-old tradition is known for daebang (greater amberjack) sashimi, and it also serves stews, tempura and set menus. Nearby: Geulla Geulla Hawaii (글라글라하와이, restaurant, about 90 m).

A small old-style eatery in Goseong-ri near Seongsan Ilchulbong, known for braised cutlassfish served with a free grilled cutlassfish. The homestyle meal includes side dishes, and it opens early for travelers.
opening_hours: 08:00-20:00; for morning visits, call ahead to confirm

description_en: A Japanese restaurant on World Cup Road in Seogwipo run by a husband-and-wife chef couple who trained at a Lotte Hotel restaurant. It serves Japanese home-style cooking such as three-tier set meals and eel rice bowls, and reservations are required.

An ocean-view cafe in front of Sagye Beach on the Hyeongje Coastal Road, known for its framed sea window and views of the Hyeongje Islands. Its signature volcanic cinder latte is made with homemade strawberry syrup and cream.

A black pork restaurant in Jungmun Tourist Complex where Jeju black pork is grilled over charcoal. Set meals mix pork belly and neck, served with a dipping sauce of Jeju fermented anchovies, and abalone-innards fried rice is a popular side. Nearby: Jungmun Doldam Heukdwaeji (중문 돌담흑돼지, restaurant, about 100 m).

An abalone restaurant in Hwasun-ri, just before Sanbangsan, run in a family with generations of haenyeo tradition. It serves abalone porridge and abalone stone-pot rice, using only abalone collected in Jeju.

A restaurant in Seogwipo known for Jeju cutlassfish dishes, including spicy braised cutlassfish with large chunks of radish and raw cutlassfish. Its two floors seat about 150 people, and reservations are essential in peak season. Nearby: Donghaemirak (동해미락, restaurant, about 90 m).

A cafe in a converted 45-year-old house in Seogwipo, where a pastry chef trained in Nakamura makes seasonal cakes and desserts with 100% animal cream. The terrace is shaded by trees and overlooks the forest.

A dessert cafe in Seongsan-eup with a wide view of the Jeju sea, known for kaymak, a Turkish dessert learned locally. Drinks are made with Jeju ingredients, and it is a good place to rest while traveling.

A wild-caught raw fish restaurant near Seongsan High School that also supplies fish to markets across the country, including Noryangjin in Seoul. It serves affordable raw fish such as isigari, rock bream and mackerel, cut fresh to order.

A local restaurant in Seongsan serving duruchigi (stir-fried pork) made only with Jeju black pork. The signature samhap duruchigi uses a special sauce and a rich broth of black pork bones simmered in a cauldron.
An Italian restaurant near the Lee Jung-seob Art Museum in Seogwipo where every dish is made in-house. Known for potato gnocchi, lasagna and bisque cream pasta, with reservations given priority.
opening_hours: 09:00-20:00 (last order 19:00); closes early when ingredients run out; reservations required 9-10 and 15-17

description_en: A Korean restaurant on Soesokkak Road in Seogwipo, in a friendly setting near the Soesokkak coast. Known for seafood stew with generous fresh seafood, and it also serves grilled okdom (tilefish) and sea urchin seaweed soup.
An organic tea farm and cafe near the Sumang intersection in Namwon-eup, with views over green tea fields. It serves organic green tea, black tea and matcha latte, and visitors can buy tea leaves.

A large round cafe in Daejeong-eup with a window overlooking the sea. It is named after the dolphins, called suaegi, that can be seen near Moseulpo Port, and is known for almond cream latte and freshly baked salt bread.

A bakery in an old house in a residential area near Wimi Elementary School in Namwon-eup. It sells only bread and bottled drinks, takeout only, and its salt bread uses French butter and organic flour.
A simple, clean Seogwipo local restaurant known for abalone hotpot and braised cutlassfish. The seasonal sea urchin water-stew and grilled Jeju golden thread fish are also popular.

An American-style pub and restaurant at the Ingu-eok crossroads in Daejeong-eup, housed in a converted garlic warehouse with a graffiti exterior. It serves handmade burgers, sandwiches and Southern-style pulled pork, and pets are allowed.
opening_hours: 12:00-21:00 (last order 20:00); closes early when ingredients run out

description_en: A Chinese restaurant at the entrance to Seopjikoji in Seongsan-eup, serving traditional Chinese dishes. Signature items include seafood jjamppong topped with a whole abalone and seafood jjajang; there is no parking lot, but roadside parking is available. Nearby: Jejuroun Cheonghaewon (제주로운청해원, restaurant, about 90 m).

A popular Japanese restaurant near Seogwipo Bukcho Elementary School, known for tendon (tempura rice bowl) with shrimp, vegetable tempura and an onsen egg. It moved from Gangjeong to a modern, cozy space with figurines.

A milmyeon (cold wheat noodle) restaurant in Seohong-dong beside Geolmae Ecological Park in Seogwipo. It uses fresh noodles and topping of Korean beef brisket, and sliced Hindon pork is a popular side.

An apple mango cafe in Shinpyeong-ri near the village hall, run by a farmer who grows the apple mangoes. Its signature is apple mango bingsu topped with generous fruit, and it also serves mango juice, yogurt smoothies and Daejeong garlic bread.

A beef gukbap restaurant near the Donggwang rural experience village, with a large cauldron out front where Hanwoo bones are simmered for broth. It opens early for breakfast, and in summer it also serves naengmyeon and makguksu.

A cafe in a third-generation tangerine orchard in Daejeong-eup, facing Mt. Sanbang and Mt. Dan. The interior is decorated with tangerines, and outside there are palm trees, hammock chairs and tractor rides for children.
Yeondon is a pork cutlet restaurant in Seogwipo known for its crispy, juicy tonkatsu and cheese cutlet. It serves only these two signature dishes and now takes reservations.

Yeongyukilsam is a pork cutlet restaurant across from Kensington Resort Seogwipo. Dishes are cooked as orders come in, and the menu includes cold udon and soba with homemade tsuyu sauce, plus set meals.
opening_hours: 11:30-19:30 (prep time 15:00-17:30; lunch last order 14:30 / dinner last order 19:00)

description_en: Yewonine is a hairtail stew restaurant in Seogwipo that uses fresh silver hairtail caught off Jeju. Its signature set pairs spicy hairtail stew with pot-cooked rice, and the menu also includes grilled hairtail, mackerel stew, abalone hotpot and grilled red tilefish. Nearby: Dalpeiji (달페이지, restaurant, about 60 m).

Ottugi Bakery is a nostalgic bakery across from the Wimi Nonghyup in Seogwipo, popular with travelers on bakery tours. Its signature salad burger has cabbage and a ketchup-mayo sauce, and it sells old-style breads such as mammoth bread, okushi and chapssal bread.

Orangutan Myeonsamuso is a tantanmen restaurant near the Sagye-ri Office in Seogwipo that sells one noodle dish with adjustable spiciness. Diners can add noodles, hot-spring egg or coriander, and the interior is decorated with orangutan figures and goods.

Oreun is a large modern cafe on the coastal road near Seongsan High School. Its garden has seasonal flowers, and the windows look out over the sea and Udo island. It serves signature drinks, brunch, desserts and a kids menu.

Ojeon Yeolhansi is a fusion Korean restaurant in Jungmun, Seogwipo, with a small menu of cold dongchimi noodles, boiled pork, abalone fried rice and soy-marinated shrimp rice. The garden of palm trees and flowers makes the wait pleasant.

Oldi Beotgudi is a cafe in a remodeled old house near the Doseun Village welfare center in Seogwipo, with a simple vintage interior. Popular items include oldi coffee topped with thick cream, a croffle with brown cheese, and cookies.

Wangilbeonji Restaurant is a black pork bulgogi restaurant near Seongeup Folk Village in Seogwipo. It serves Jeju black pork with Jeju ferns and shiitake mushrooms in a spacious modern building with parking, popular with large groups. Nearby: Gumburi Restaurant (굼부리식당, restaurant, about 70 m).

Yudong Coffee is a local roastery cafe near Olle Market and Lee Jung-seop Street in Seogwipo. It serves coffee made from its own roasted beans, along with specialty drinks and desserts, in a warm modern interior suited to quiet time. Nearby: Angeori Bakkeori (안거리 밖거리, restaurant, about 40 m).

Inseumil is a seaside cafe in Ilgwari, Seogwipo, where dolphins can sometimes be seen. Set in a garden of palm trees and cycads, its granary-style building gives it a tropical resort feel. Its signature menu features healthy barley-flour drinks.

Jaridom Raw Fish Restaurant in central Seogwipo is known for raw mackerel, cut thick and tender. In summer it serves chilled raw fish soups such as jaridom and hanchi mulhoe, and in winter it offers fatty yellowtail sashimi.

Natural Restaurant is a Mediterranean restaurant behind Seogwipo Girls' High School, run by a single chef and reservation-based. Its menu uses Jeju ingredients for souvlaki, tzatziki and a Greek octopus salad with hallabong and canola honey.

Jangsuaeseom Restaurant is a seafood restaurant known for its fish stew and grilled fish, made with fresh seasonal catches delivered daily. Meals come with a variety of side dishes in a clean, cozy dining room.

Jeju Goro is a small fusion Japanese restaurant in Mureung-ri, Daejeong-eup, near Mureung Elementary School. Its menu includes donburi rice bowls and cream udon with ingredients like avocado, and its quiet interior suits couples and families.

Jeju Gomjip is a barbecue restaurant serving Jeju black pork with seafood such as grilled prawns, butter abalone and pen shell clams. The meat comes pre-grilled and is finished over charcoal briquettes, with Jeju side dishes like fern namul and anchovy sauce.

Jeju Ttukbaegi is a restaurant at the start of the one-way road to Seongsan Ilchulbong, known as one of the first eateries in the Seongsan-ri area. It is famous for seafood hotpots and also serves fish stews and abalone porridge, suited to family and group meals.

Jeju Yaksuteo is a local craft beer pub and takeaway shop with 16 beers, including brews from three Jeju breweries and its own recipes. Free tastings let visitors find a beer they like. Nearby: Cheonjitgol Restaurant (천짓골식당, restaurant, about 70 m).

Jeju Ein is a tangerine orchard cafe in Seogwipo where visitors can walk into the orchard after ordering a drink. Photo zones, year-round decorative tangerines and signature drinks such as Hallabong ade make it a fun stop, and citrus goods are sold.

Jeju Oseong is a hairtail restaurant at the entrance to Jungmun Tourist Complex, in a new building with parking, a cafe and a gift shop. It serves hairtail stew and whole grilled hairtail set meals, including a boneless hairtail stew for all ages.
Jeju Halmang Bapsang is a budget-friendly restaurant near Sanbangsan serving grilled fish and spicy pork stir-fry. Each meal comes with rice, soup and ten side dishes that change daily.

Jungmun Mackerel Ssambap is a Korean restaurant near Jungmun Tourist Complex, known for boneless flower mackerel braised with aged kimchi in limited daily portions. In rose season, the entrance and garden are lined with roses.

name_en: Jungmun Saekdal Whole Hairtail Stew and Grill
description_en: Jungmun Saekdal is a restaurant west of Jungmun Tourist Complex specializing in whole hairtail dishes. Its boneless hairtail stew set comes with seasonal side dishes, and grilled whole hairtail is picked off the bone by staff for easy eating.

Jungmun Sudu-ri Bomal Kalguksu is a noodle restaurant in Jungmun, open since 2013, known for kalguksu with hand-kneaded hijiki noodles and a broth made from fresh bomal (top shell). Side dishes are homemade, and the menu has four dishes.

Jungmun Childonga is a barbecue restaurant near Jungmun Tourist Complex serving thick cuts of Jeju black pork and white pork. It has a spacious parking lot and self-refill side dishes, and staff grill and cut the meat for guests. Nearby: Duridumbi (두리둠비, restaurant, about 90 m).

name_en: Jungmun Haemul Ramyeon Oppane Main Branch
description_en: Jungmun Haemul Ramyeon Oppane is a seafood ramen restaurant near Jungmun Tourist Complex. Its octopus seafood ramen uses a homemade sauce, with no standard ramen seasoning or capsaicin, and its abalone cheese rice is a creamy, risotto-style side.

name_en: Jungmun Hoe Pojang Center Dawn Night Market
description_en: Jungmun Hoe Pojang Center Dawn Night Market is a seafood shop near ICC Jeju, selling takeout platters of raw fish such as mackerel, sweet shrimp and hairtail. It is open until 11 p.m., takes online reservations and offers delivery.

Jinmi Myeongga is a seafood restaurant near the Sagye coast on Jeju Olle Trail Route 10, famous for dagumbari raw fish. It has been run by one family for three generations and serves many side dishes and a clear fish-bone soup.

Jjanggu Bunsik is a casual snack restaurant in Seogwipo specializing in modakchigi, a Jeju dish where tteokbokki, gimbap, fried foods and jeon are served together on one plate. The tteokbokki is generous and mild, and the gimbap is known for its sesame flavor.

Cheondonga Jungmun Main Branch is a Jeju barbecue restaurant at the entrance to Jungmun Tourist Complex. It serves Jeju flower pork collar, pork belly, black pork kimchi stew and steamed eggs, with round tables suited to group meals. Nearby: Gojipdol Ureok Jungmun Branch (고집돌우럭 중문점, restaurant, about 70 m).

Cheongchun Bubu is a cafe in a former tangerine warehouse, renovated in 2018, in southwestern Jeju. It bakes its own desserts and roasts its own beans, serving egg tarts, salt bread, bagels, cinnamon rolls and citrus cheesecake in a cozy, photogenic space.

Chunmihyang is a family-run restaurant in Seogwipo known for its Chunmihyang set meal, which includes pork neck, bomal seaweed soup, red tilefish and sweet shrimp with side dishes. It uses fresh, seasonal local ingredients.

Chwihyang-ui Seom is a kitchen in Wimi-ri, Seogwipo, set in a 1970s house remodeled by a carpenter and painter couple. It serves Korean-inspired international dishes, such as fern pasta with salted anchovy sauce, grilled mackerel oil pasta and black sesame cream pasta.
opening_hours: 11:00-16:00 (last order 15:00); may close early when ingredients run out, so call ahead

description_en: Chinbong Sanjang is a log-cabin cafe at the end of Route 516 near Donnaecko Recreation Area in Seogwipo. Decorated in an American Old West style, it has a stone fireplace and serves Irish coffee, a peanut injeolmi latte and beef stew in bread.

Cafe Gyulkkotdarak is a tangerine-themed cafe converted from a stone storehouse built in 1978. Its cakes, jelly and drinks are handmade, with signature items like citrus mousse cake and Jeju green tea custard latte, plus a tangerine grove photo zone.

Cafe The Light is a cafe between Seongsan Ilchulbong and the Seongsan Port passenger terminal, with large windows looking out over Seongsan Ilchulbong and Udo island. Its desserts and drinks are all handmade, and the rooftop swing is a popular photo spot.

Cafe Lucia Main Branch is a seaside cafe at Daepyeong Port near Olle Trail Course 8 in Seogwipo. From its seating and rooftop you can see Baksugijeong cliff, Songak Mountain and Hyeongje Islands, and on clear days Gapado and Marado. Pets are welcome.

Cafe Seoyeonui Jip is a cafe on Olle Trail Course 5 that was built as a film location and opened as a cafe in 2013. Film fans and tourists visit to see movie memorabilia, and the cafe serves cakes and a muffin named after a character from the film.

Cafe Syong is a simple cafe by the sea at Gongcheonpo in Seogwipo, overlooking the quiet southern coast. Popular items include cafe latte, chocolate drinks with four strength levels, and syongpeul, a dessert with banana, walnut, maple syrup and cream. Nearby: Gongcheonpo Restaurant (공천포식당, restaurant, about 20 m).

Cafe Onol is a dessert cafe at Daepo Port in Seogwipo, serving milk drinks made from same-day milk of cows grazing on Hallasan pastures. Desserts use seasonal Jeju fruits such as citrus and blueberries, and the cafe overlooks Daepo harbor.

Koba Ramen is a ramen restaurant inside Play Sagye, a cultural complex with views of Sanbangsan. It uses a broth made from Jeju red tilefish, and its signature Midori Shio ramen is flavored with an oil made from Jeju winter greens.

Coco Mama is a Hawaiian-style seafood restaurant near Seongsan Ilchulbong. Its jumbo seafood platter includes pineapple fried rice, scallops, mussels, skewers, squid and shrimp tempura, and lobster can be added. It also serves seasonal fruit juices. Nearby: Gyeongmine Jip / Gyeongmi Rest Area (경미네집 / 경미휴게소, restaurant, about 80 m).

Crackers Daejeong Branch is a warehouse-style cafe in a converted basalt tangerine storehouse, known for coffee roasted in-house. You can choose the beans for your drink, and the cafe also serves bakery items, desserts, tea, lemonade and hot chocolate.

Takuma Sushi is a container sushi restaurant near Seopjikoji in Jeju. Its assorted sushi and sashimi change daily, and the menu also includes poke, pasta and udon. Its red udon has a rich fish-bone broth with crab, abalone and sweet shrimp.

Tropical Hideaway Cafe is a brunch and bakery cafe near Songak Mountain on the Sagye coast. It serves Mediterranean dishes such as Turkish-style pide pizza, hummus salad and falafel platter, with views of Hyeongje Islands. It turns into a draft beer pub in the evening.

Perlo is an Italian restaurant in Deoksu-ri, Daejeong-eup, serving southern Italian-style dishes with local Jeju ingredients. Its menu includes sea urchin roe pasta, octopus pasta, Jeju black pork steak and wood-fired pizza with buckwheat.

Pulbegae is a vintage cafe in a renovated old Jeju house in Seogwang-ri, Seogwipo, with a tangerine tree in the yard. Its decor includes school desks, tables made from iron doors and beer-crate chairs, and the glass ceiling makes it a photo favorite.

Pins is a dolphin-view cafe on the coast of Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, where wild bottlenose dolphins can sometimes be seen through large windows. Its stone-and-wood building has dolphin photos and books, and the owner alerts guests when dolphins appear.

Harakeke is a tropical-style cafe inside Sogol Farm Village Pension in Seogwipo, with hundreds of palm trees, Bali-imported statues, a swing and a pool. Balinese crafts and rattan furniture add warmth, and the menu includes coffee, pizza, desserts and cocktails.

Harubang Milmyeon is a restaurant in Daejeong-eup, Seogwipo, specializing in Busan-style cold milmyeon noodles. The noodles contain hijiki seaweed and domestic wheat, and the broth is a bone stock simmered for 24 hours with herbs. Nearby: Watto Coffee (와토커피, cafe, about 80 m).

A buckwheat restaurant run by a farming cooperative in Gwangpyeong-ri, Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, serving handmade noodles made from Jeju-grown buckwheat. Signature dishes include nutty perilla-oil noodles, cold noodles, and the Jeju traditional dish jobegi.

The main branch in Mosulpo, Daejeong, serves fresh Jeju abalone in several dishes. Its signature abalone stone-pot rice is mixed with butter and chive soy sauce, then finished with hot water as a savory rice drink.

A seafood restaurant in Seongsan-eup known for its cutlassfish special, which includes grilled and braised cutlassfish plus cutlassfish sashimi and soup. The fish is brought in from Seongsan Port that same day. Nearby: Cheongun Restaurant (청운식당, restaurant, about 20 m); Deunggyeongdol Restaurant (등경돌식당, restaurant, about 70 m).
closed_days: none; closed on Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: Ham Chef Kitchen, near the Daepo Jusang Jeolli cliffs in Seogwipo, is known for its jjamppong noodles and Jeju black pork cutlet. Portions are generous, and dishes are served on wave-shaped plates and shell-like dishware.

Honeymoon House is a cafe in Seogwipo that opened in 2018 in part of a former Paradise Hotel. The approach is lined with sea and forest, and from the terrace guests can see Seopseom and Beomseom islands while enjoying homemade desserts and light meals.

Hongseongbang, at the entrance of Mosulpo Port in Daejeong, is known for seafood jjamppong with a whole flower crab. Its tangsuyuk is piled like a tower and topped with sweet-and-sour sauce and sliced onion.

Hoesoodaok is a tea house in Hoesu-dong, Seogwipo, opened in 2024 in a remodeled house more than 30 years old. Guests sit among Jeju clay pottery and basalt stone-wall tables while the host brews Jeju teas.

Hayeong Black Pork Grill House sits at the entrance to the Jungmun Tourist Complex, on a slight rise with views of the coast. It is spacious and suits groups, families, and solo travelers. Nearby: Jungmun Braised Cutlassfish Ijoeun Restaurant (중문갈치조림 이조은식당, restaurant, about 40 m); Jeju Mihyang (제주미향, restaurant, about 20 m).

513 Tendon is a fusion tendon (tempura rice bowl) restaurant in Jeju City where diners can choose their own combinations. Its signature 513 Tendon features plump shrimp tempura, seasonal vegetable tempura, oyster mushroom, chili, seaweed, and a poached egg.

5L2F is a roastery cafe in Wahul-ri, Jocheon-eup, in the calm mid-mountain area of eastern Jeju. Its signature drinks include Cream Crema, a smooth cream latte, and 153 Coffee, a rich latte, and it also sells homemade cakes.

88 Roasters is a roastery cafe near Hwabuk Port on the Hwabuk coastal road in Jeju City. Inside, mint tones, tiles, and brick create a stylish space, and the coffee is made from beans roasted in-house.
opening_hours: 12:00-19:00 (may change; please call ahead before visiting)

description_en: AND YOU CAFE is a vegan cafe in Ongpo-ri, Hallim-eup, that uses no animal products. It serves homemade vegan burgers, sandwiches, fair-trade coffee and chocolate, and organic tea, and avoids disposable items.

Ganeungot Sehwa is a bakery in Sehwa-ri, Gujwa-eup, Jeju City, that makes bread with local farm produce such as Jeju native black barley, cherry tomatoes, and green soybeans. Signature breads include Emmental sun-dried tomato bread and roasted Jeju potato bread.

Gasieomeong Gimbap is a snack restaurant in central Nohyeong-dong, Jeju City, about 10 minutes from Jeju Airport. It is the main branch of a nationwide chain known for gimbap with tot (sea tangle), and it opens at 7 a.m.

Gyeongseong Seafood, near Hallim General Sports Complex, sells and cuts fresh seafood, including wild and farm-raised fish. Staff clean and fillet fish such as amberjack, mackerel, and red sea bream for takeout, and a few tables let visitors try a bite on site.

Goguksu is a Jeju pork noodle restaurant about seven minutes from Jeju Airport, with broth simmered for 48 hours and chewy fresh noodles. It also serves Jeju black pork gukbap, and its large pond interior suits families with children.
opening_hours: 09:00-20:30 (prep time 15:30-17:00; last lunch order 15:00 / last dinner order 20:00)

description_en: Aewol Gobullak is a home-style set meal restaurant in a 100-year-old traditional house in Aewol-eup, Jeju. It is the only place in Korea where you can eat lettuce enzyme rice, served in a set with Jeju black pork stir-fry. Nearby: Sanchaek Unmanned Cafe (무인카페 산책, cafe, about 30 m).

Gosari Coffee in Gujwa-eup, Jeju City, has a large side window that looks onto a forest. Its signature drinks are Gosari Coffee, a blend of kettle-roasted tangerine peel tea and specialty espresso, and Green Citron Coffee made with handmade Jeju citron syrup.
Goto Coffee Bar is a quiet cafe down an alley near Guem Port in Aewol-eup, converted from a house. It has a stained-glass window, two other rooms to sit in, and many photo spots.

Alley Cafe Oksu is a cafe in an alley near Sogil Community Welfare Center in Aewol-eup, set in a grandmother's old house. Vintage items such as an old carpet and a table made from a mother-of-pearl door fill the space, and its same-day egg tart is famous.

Gommak Restaurant in Gujwa-eup, Jeju, is known for abalone porridge with plenty of sesame and fresh raw fish from water drawn 80 m underground. Its sea urchin noodles and raw noodle dishes are also popular, and drinks and extra side dishes are self-service.

Gwangyang Haejangguk is a long-running hangover soup restaurant in Jeju City, open since 1987. Its most popular haejangguk uses aronsatae instead of brisket, and the spacious interior fits large groups. Nearby: Halla Restaurant (한라식당, restaurant, about 100 m).

Original Gyorae Son Kalguksu in Jocheon-eup, Jeju, is known for hand-kneaded green noodles and a rich chicken broth. It sits in front of a bus stop and has a large parking lot, but it is often crowded, so arrive before 3 p.m. or reserve. Nearby: Sambok Garden (삼복가든, restaurant, about 80 m).

Gussi Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee shop in Sehwa-ri, eastern Jeju, opened in 2019. It selects and roasts its own beans and presents each bean's flavor through different brewing methods in a calm space.

Guisai is a budget-friendly Korean set-meal restaurant near Aewol, designated a Jeju good-price restaurant. The standard set includes bulgogi, grilled fish, and soybean paste stew, and for a small extra charge you can order dishes such as boiled pork (domberye-gogi), egg roll, and braised fish.

Gujwa Store is a quiet cafe on Woljeong-ri beach, made from two remodeled Jeju stone-wall houses with large windows. Its signature carrot cake is moist, and the front yard with tables and plants is a photo spot.

Gwonga Kalguksu is a knife-cut noodle restaurant in Jeju City that makes its noodles fresh every day. Its chicken and clam kalguksu are popular, and it also serves chicken gomtang and seafood pajeon at reasonable prices with generous portions.

Geugyejeol is a plant-filled cafe in Pyeongdae-ri, Gujwa-eup, down an alley near the beach. Green plants and natural wood furniture fill the indoor and outdoor spaces, and its sunlit entrance door is a popular photo spot.

Geureomeuro Part2 is a dessert and roastery cafe near Hallasan Arboretum in Jeju City, in a modern single-story building. Its garden has seasonal flowers and a small forest, and the signature Merihaha latte is made with cold milk instead of ice.

Green Pebble is a rural cafe on Olle Trail Course 14 in Hallim-eup, Jeju, that serves tea made from seokchangpo grown at a local farm. Its signature vegan drink, Seokchangpo Milkong Tea, combines black tea, seokchangpo, and soy milk.

Geuchorok is a cafe on the Woljeong-ri coastal road in eastern Jeju, filled with green plants and vintage wooden furniture. Its signature avocado coffee pairs bitter coffee with creamy avocado, and a small garden overlooks the sea.

Geumdonga Jeju Main Branch is a black pork restaurant near Gamundong Harbor on the Aewol coastal road. It grills aged Jeju black pork on a special griddle using oak pellets, and staff grill the meat for guests for a lighter, juicier taste than charcoal.

Geumak Ttot-ttot Ramyeon is a noodle restaurant near Geumoreum in Hallim-eup, known for a spicy ramyeon with plenty of garlic, scallion, and minced beef. Its Ttot-ttot Ramyeon was developed with Baek Jong-won for a TV cooking show, and there is often a waiting line.

Gimnyeong-e Saneun Kim Yeonghun is a cafe run by a couple who love coffee and desserts, in Gimnyeong, Gujwa-eup. It serves aeropress coffee made from its own roasted single-origin beans, and its cakes use almond and coconut flour instead of wheat flour.

Kim Mari is a snack shop in a corner alley across from Jeju City Hall, known for yubu gimbap made with homemade lemon syrup and Jeju tangerine. Its Mari Special mixed tteokbokki comes with fried snacks, dumplings, boiled egg, and ramen noodles.

Kkongsunine, at the junction of Jungsan-seo-ro and Sangga-ro in Aewol-eup, Jeju, is known for its pork noodle soup with a rich yet clean broth and tender boiled pork. It also serves anchovy noodles, bibim noodles, and momguk, a traditional Jeju dish.

Kkotbap is a Korean restaurant in Aewol-eup, Jeju, serving full table spreads of home-style side dishes. Its signature set pairs spicy Jeju black pork stir-fry with grilled mackerel, and solo diners can order the full set, unlike at most Korean set-meal restaurants.

Kkumnang Rice House is a neat Korean restaurant in Aewol-eup, Jeju, known for its boriguri rice-pot set. The mackerel is not overly salty, and its fermented soybean stew (cheonggukjang) is also popular.
