Nara Donkatsu is an old-style pork cutlet restaurant near Woldae Stream in Oedo-dong, a short distance from Jeju Airport. Its retro interior and thick cutlets with homemade sauce are popular, and it now offers cheese, sweet potato, and curry versions.

Namchun Restaurant in Idong-dong, Jeju City, sits down a quiet residential alley and offers floor seating. Its signature Jeju-style meat noodle soup uses boiled pork and carrots in a milky broth, and its gimbap is packed with carrot, spinach, and beef.

Nora Ba is a seafood ramyeon restaurant on a back road in Guem-ri, Aewol-eup, in a small remodeled Jeju stone house with indoor and outdoor tables. Its octopus ramyeon contains a whole crab and abalone, and since ingredients are limited, it may close early when they run out.

Noeulli is a brunch and dessert cafe in Guem-ri, Aewol-eup, with a bus-stop-style entrance and a glasshouse interior of tropical plants and sea views. Floors above the ground floor are no-kids zones, and its pizza, pasta, and signature Noeulli Ade are popular.

Danso, near Aewol Elementary School in Jeju City, serves a home-style set meal with ten side dishes, including Jeju black pork duruchigi as a key side. Ingredients are domestic, the side dishes change with the seasons, and only 50 servings are sold each day.

Dambaek, on the coastal road from Woljeong-ri toward Sehwa, makes pot rice with Jeju cutlassfish, abalone, and black pork. Its abalone pot rice uses a special sauce made from abalone innards, and its cutlassfish pot rice is fully deboned.
opening_hours: 09:00-16:00 (may close early if ingredients run out; call ahead)

description_en: The Healing Time is a foot-soak cafe on the Yongduam coastal road in Jeju City, near the airport. Guests soak their feet in aroma-oil baths for 30 minutes in group sessions, so they must arrive at their booked time. Nearby: Badapunggyeong Jeongyuk Restaurant (바다풍경 정육식당, restaurant, about 40 m).

Do Galbi, near Hanra University in Noheong-dong, Jeju City, is a black pork grill restaurant known for scored pork that stays tender and juicy. Its signature set, Do Daepyo Hanpan, features selected Jeju black pork cuts, and the mel-jeot (anchovy sauce) fried rice is popular.
opening_hours: 12:00-23:00 (prep time 15:00-16:30; last lunch order 14:10 / last dinner order 22:10)

description_en: Dodu Fresh is a handmade burger takeout and dine-in shop near Jeju Airport, Iho Tewoo Beach, and the rainbow coastal road. Patties are made fresh every day without freezing, and signature burgers include shrimp tempura and bacon egg.

Dori Tourist Farm, at Gyorae crossroads in Jocheon-eup, Jeju, combines a cafe with farm and animal experiences. Its coffee uses beans from Seogwipo's Yudong Coffee, and it sells sandwiches, cookies, and crafts by local Jeju artists.

Doeul is a dessert cafe near Jeju Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest in Jocheon-eup, set in a small stone-wall house with a yard. Its cube pound cakes come with toppings such as mugwort, pumpkin, lemon, and cheese, and the Udo peanut cream coffee is also popular. Nearby: Nangtteul-e Swimpang (낭뜰에쉼팡, restaurant, about 10 m).

Dochidol Hanwoo Charcoal Grill, in Nabeup-ri in Jeju's mid-mountain area, uses only Hanwoo slaughtered that day. Menu items include galbi-tang (beef short rib soup), sirloin, and yukhoe, served in a spacious, clean interior suited to families and groups.

Dongbok Ttukbaegi is a Jeju home-style restaurant in Dongbuk-ri, Gujwa-eup, known for fish dishes. Its signature whole grilled hairtail set uses fish bought fresh at the fish market. Nearby: Dongbok Haenyeochon (동복해녀촌, restaurant, about 70 m).
Dumori Isusa is a Japanese restaurant in Dumori, Hangyeong-myeon, known for good value. It is popular for sushi set menus with udon, cold noodles or pork cutlet, and also serves raw fish dishes.

Dilettante is a brunch cafe in Jocheon-ri near the Daeseom entrance bus stop, known for French-style quiche made with Jeju ingredients. The interior looks like a photo studio, there is a terrace, and pets are welcome.

Ttungdanji Aewol Main Branch is a restaurant in Aewol-eup known for Jeju black pork aged for seven days. It also serves a seafood table set and thick-cut pork, and diners can watch the sunset over Goneae-ri port.
Lara Cafe is a cafe in Gwangryeong-ri, Aewol-eup, with a large garden and sea views. It has a rapeseed field that turns yellow in spring, along with plenty of seating and photo spots.

Raeyong is a conveyor-belt sushi restaurant in Oedoil-dong, Jeju City, close to Jeju Airport. It serves sushi made with fresh fish daily, plus soba, tempura and rice dishes, and has a children's menu.

name_en: Romantic Shrimp Aewol Gwakji Main Branch
description_en: Romantic Shrimp Aewol Gwakji Main Branch is a shrimp specialty restaurant near Gwakji Beach, where nearly every dish except drinks contains shrimp. Signature dishes include Red Big Bang shrimp and romantic barbecue shrimp over omelette rice.

Longroad is a small Western-style restaurant on the coast of Gwideok-ri in western Jeju. Its signature is handmade beef hamburger steak cooked to order, and it also serves avocado hamburger steak, Japanese karaage chicken and taco rice.

Maru Kitchen is a restaurant in a renovated old Jeju house in Hangyeong-myeon, with a stylish interior. Its seafood platter is limited to 30 servings a day, and its crab pasta and Maru pork cutlet are also popular.

Mamarong is a handmade cake and dessert shop beside Jeju Tourism University on Pyeonghwa Road. It sells eclairs, macarons and cakes made with animal cream, in only the day's quantity, in a vintage-style interior.

Matilda is an LP record cafe in Goneae-ri, Aewol-eup, near the sea side of Aewol Library. Guests can listen to vintage records of old music and film soundtracks, and request songs. It turns into a cocktail bar at night.

Manbok Banh Mi is a Vietnamese-style sandwich shop in a residential alley near Nohyeong Catholic church in Jeju City. It bakes baguettes each morning and fills them with Vietnamese sauces, offering meatball, kebab and bulgogi sandwiches.

Meokdol Jeju Main Branch is a meat noodle restaurant in Yongdam-dong, right by Jeju Airport, that became famous through TV food shows. Its menu includes herbal pork soup, boiled Jeju pork and pan-fried black pork.

Mekong Sky is a Vietnamese restaurant near the Jeju Provincial Government office. Its pho broth is simmered for over 15 hours with beef bones and old hen, without concentrates, spice mixes or MSG, and its rice noodles contain no wheat flour.

Myeonppopneun Seonsaeng Mandubitneun Anae is a dumpling hotpot restaurant in Hallim-eup. Its signature is a Jeju hanwoo boiled-meat and mushroom dumpling hotpot, and fresh handmade noodles are added at the end.

Myeongrang Snack is a Korean snack-bar restaurant near Hallim Port, with views of Biyangdo island across the water. Its signature is chewy tteokbokki made with wheat rice cakes, and it also serves Jeju squid and black pork tempura. Pets are allowed.

Myeongjin Abalone is a restaurant in Gujwa-eup known for abalone dishes, with sea views from the window seats. Its signature abalone stone-pot rice comes with grilled mackerel and salted octopus, and the scorched rice is a favorite.

Monuet is a music-themed cafe in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, with records, CDs and cassette tapes on display. Its signature Hallasan canele uses Hallasan soju instead of rum. It works by table reservation and may close early when sold out.

Moraebi Cafe Lounge is an ocean-view cafe near Woljeong Beach in Gujwa-eup, known for hand-drip coffee and fresh bakery. Its name means sand blowing like rain in the strong Woljeong wind. Ades, juices and smoothies are also served. Nearby: Woljeongri Galbi-bap (월정리갈비밥, restaurant, about 90 m); Meomun (머문, cafe, about 40 m).

Mongrab is a 7,500-pyeong farm cafe about 15 minutes by car from Jeju International Airport. It grows GAP-certified figs and tangerines, offers seasonal picking experiences, and is known for fresh fig soft-serve ice cream.

Miseuchil is a Jeju restaurant on Iljuseo-ro known for dombe pork and abalone dishes, including stews, rice pot dishes and grilled dishes. Its full Jeju table set and dombe set meal feature local classics, and it is close to the airport.

Mystic Samdo is a gardening cafe in Nohyeong-dong, Jeju City, beside the Mysterious Road with a view of Hallasan. Flowers change with the seasons, from winter camellias to spring cherry blossoms and autumn pink muhly. Animals in the garden allow carrot feeding.

Miel de Sehwa is a dessert cafe in Sehwa-ri, Gujwa-eup, right by Sehwa Port and Sehwa Beach. Its signature is honey coffee topped with fresh cream, and carrot juice and carrot cake are also popular. Seasonal fruit desserts rotate.

Badaneun Anboyeoyo is a small cafe at the entrance of Jongdal-ri village, with a blue roof and cozy interior. It serves carrot juice made from Gujwa carrots. Books are available to read, but each group is limited to three hours.

Badareul Bon Dwaeji is a restaurant near Panpo Port in Hangyeong-myeon, with views of Biyangdo island through folding glass doors. Its signature is Jeju black pork grilled and wrapped in bracken, dipped in salted anchovy sauce. Nearby: Panpo Miin (판포미인, restaurant, about 60 m).

Badasok Godeungeo Ssambap is a mackerel ssambap restaurant in Aewol-eup with a large parking lot, open from early morning to late night. Mackerel with aged kimchi is wrapped in fresh vegetables, and local makgeolli and soy-marinated crab are sold.

Badang Han-geureut is a seafood restaurant on the Aewol coastal road near the Aewol Dolphin Observatory, with sea views. Its live tanks hold fish, abalone and seafood. Its signature is a special mulhoe, a cold raw fish dish with abalone, stone octopus and shrimp.

Barambyeoge Huin Dangnagwi is an artistic cafe in Gujwa-eup, where a white donkey sculpture is set along a windbreak wall. Warm lighting and small decorations make it cozy, and the surrounding nature suits walks and photos.

Bae Chef is a Chinese restaurant in Aradil-dong, Jeju City, serving traditional Chinese cuisine rather than tourist-style jjamppong. Its signature dishes are Kkanpung shrimp in garlic sauce and yusanseul, a sea cucumber and vegetable dish in oyster sauce.
Baengnihyang is a value Korean home-style set meal restaurant near Hamdeok Beach in Jocheon-eup. Its set meals come with doenjang stew, spicy pork stir-fry and grilled fish, and many locals visit.

Bomal Kalguksu Haewoljeong is a local food spot on the Jongdal coastal road, on Jeju Olle Trail Course 21. It serves noodles made with sea snails gathered by haenyeo divers, and sea urchin versions, with views of the sea.

Bon Cafe is a two-story cafe on the Aewol coastal road near Aewol Port, with sea views from its seats. Pets are welcome, and there is a photo zone with the sea as backdrop. It also sells snacks, souvenirs and toys.

Blue Saigon is a Vietnamese restaurant in Aewol-eup serving fusion dishes inspired by Vietnamese street food, in an exotic seaside setting. Its signature is banh mi with crispy baguette and fresh fillings, in pork, grilled vegetable and chicken versions.

Be My Guest is a cafe and brunch restaurant near the Hyeopjae post office in Hallim-eup, popular with travelers. Summer favorites include mango bingsu with Jeju apple mango and crispy croffles, and brunch options include panini and soufflé pancakes.

Biyangnol is an ocean-view cafe at Pyeongsu Port on the Hallim coastal road, known as a sunset spot where the sun sets behind Biyangdo island. Modern tables mix with antique furniture, and an open courtyard brings in light.

Bieoraundeu is a cafe in Hado-ri, a quiet village on Jeju's east side, with vintage speakers and wooden furniture. Its signature is carrot juice made with Gujwa carrots, and carrot cookies and carrot tiramisu are also popular.

Ppanggeut is a bakery in a residential area near Ido Elementary School in Jeju City, known among travelers for its salt bread. The salt bread is crispy outside, soft inside, and buttery. It also sells baguettes, brioche and sandwiches.

Samdado Hoejip is a raw fish restaurant near Jeju Airport on the Yongdu-am coastal road, serving wild live fish. Its tanks are continuously fed clean seawater, and visitors can enjoy fresh raw fish and other seafood dishes.

Samdae Guksu Hoegwan is a noodle restaurant in Samseong-ro, Jeju City, known for Jeju meat noodles, soybean noodles and young radish noodles. Noodles are made daily from fresh dough, and its dombe-gogi boiled pork shows the tender taste of Jeju pork.
opening_hours: 07:30-02:00 (last order 01:20; shortened hours only on traditional holidays)

description_en: Samu Guksu is a noodle restaurant on Samumu-ro near Jeju Airport, known for its meat noodles in clear pork broth topped with sliced pork. Its fish tray noodles, mixed with seasonal raw fish and vegetables, are also popular.

Seonheul Bangju Grandma's Restaurant is in Seonheul-ri, Jocheon-eup, near Jeju Raf. It is known for healthy meals using soybeans grown by the owner's son. Signature dishes include samchae gomchwi dumplings and bracken bibimbap.

Seopseopi-ne is a rustic restaurant at Songdang Crossroads in Gujwa-eup, serving meat noodles and fusion Indian curry. Its signature is black pork curry, with crispy fried black pork on a creamy tomato and butter curry. Nearby: Ppuriwa Yeolmae (뿌리와열매, restaurant, about 60 m).

Sogeumbachi Suni-ne is a seafood restaurant on the Jongdal coastal road. Its signature is stir-fried stone octopus with sweet and spicy seasoning, along with abalone porridge, sea urchin soup and hairtail stew.
opening_hours: 09:30-19:30 (prep time 15:00-16:30; last order 19:00; may open early if ingredients run out, so call before visiting)

description_en: Soseom Abalone is an abalone restaurant on Udo island, a short walk up the Udo coastal road from Geommulle Beach. It serves abalone rice, stew, porridge and mulhoe made with domestic abalone, and large windows overlook the sea.

Sonmatchon is a Korean restaurant in Jocheon-eup specializing in bracken hairtail stew and whole grilled hairtail. All seafood and ingredients are domestic. It is about 5 minutes by car from attractions such as Sangumburi Crater. Nearby: Seongmi Garden (성미가든, restaurant, about 50 m); Oreum Garden (오름가든, restaurant, about 80 m).

Songdang Jeju Salon is a quiet book cafe in Songdang village, Gujwa-eup, where visitors can read with simple drinks. It also runs a women-only book stay called Saenggakui Oreum, with books from the shelves available to borrow. Nearby: Hwanyeong Kitchen (환영키친, restaurant, about 90 m).

Songdang Namu is a gardening cafe in Songdang-ri, Gujwa-eup, with a wide garden of flowers. Herbs, palms and cacti grow in its greenhouse and outdoor garden, where visitors can enjoy ades and coffee. Pets are allowed.

Suldoga Jeju Badang is a rice wine brewery in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, making wine with Jeju lava seawater. Visitors can try free tastings and a rice wine-making experience. The brewery makes eight kinds of drinks, including buckwheat soju and kiwi wine.
Sushi Aewol is an omakase sushi restaurant near Aewol Port with ocean views. All courses are by reservation only, booked by phone, and it is a no-kids zone.

Stay With Coffee is a hand-drip coffee shop near Haean Elementary School on the mid-mountain Pyeonghwa Road in Jeju City. It offers over 20 specialty coffee beans from around the world, and the first floor lets visitors smell roasting beans and chat with baristas.
A small restaurant in Jeju City known for stir-fried octopus (nakji bokkeum) in a sweet and spicy sauce, served with thin noodles. The short menu also includes cheonggukjang soybean stew.
A Western-style restaurant in Jeju City with an open kitchen and a bar counter that suits solo diners. Signature dishes include sirloin and tenderloin pork cutlets and mayonnaise pilaf.

A Japanese-style curry restaurant near Geumseong Port in Aewol-eup, Jeju, serving mild curry with thick, crispy pork cutlets. Its signature is pork cutlet curry, and it is popular with both tourists and locals.

A Vietnamese restaurant in Aewol, Jeju, that follows traditional Vietnamese recipes. Signature dishes include beef pho, pho with raw beef, and stir-fried rice noodles, served with fresh vegetables and meat. Nearby: Jelkoba Bakery Cafe (젤코바 베이커리 카페, cafe, about 30 m).

A roastery cafe near Dongmun Market in Jeju City, serving hand-drip coffee in an old building with a vintage feel. It has seating on the first and third floors, and a clothing shop on the second floor.

A cultural cafe in Bonggae-dong, Jeju City, run by painter Kang Bueon, with a large lawn and forest walks where pets are welcome. Visitors can enjoy live performances and paintings, and it is popular for small weddings.
A spacious restaurant in Jeju City serving fusion abalone dishes made only with live abalone. Popular items include abalone porridge, avocado abalone rice and abalone mulhoe, a cold fish soup.

A bibimbap restaurant near Hyeopjae Beach with a bright interior and a second floor that has sea views. Signature dishes include red shrimp bibimbap and rock octopus bibimbap, and set menus offer good value for groups. Nearby: Honjeo (혼저, restaurant, about 100 m).

A cafe near Songdang bus stop in Gujwa-eup, Jeju, popular for photo spots, including a gap between trees that frames fields, oreum hills and sky. Signature items include carrot cake and the Dolttang latte.

A black pork restaurant in Jeoji-ri, Hangyeong-eup, Jeju, serving grilled black pork trimmings and briquette-grilled black pork belly. The trimmings come from different cuts, so the taste changes each visit, and stone-pot rice with stew is a popular set.
opening_hours: 11:00-21:30 (last order 20:00; may close early if ingredients run out)

description_en: A sea urchin seaweed soup restaurant near Goae Port in Aewol, Jeju, with large windows overlooking the sea and sunset views in the evening. The signature is sea urchin rice bowl, and food is cooked after ordering, so allow extra time.

A brunch cafe in Aewol, Jeju, on the road above the Hangdam Coastal Walkway, with sea views from indoors, the terrace and the rooftop. Signature items include Coco Sunset and the Aewol The Sunset parfait.

A buckwheat cold noodle restaurant near Aewol Port, Jeju, making noodles in-house from pure buckwheat with no additives. The mild, nutty noodles suit all ages, and the spacious hall works well for groups.

A cafe in Aewol-eup, Jeju, that sells film and rents film cameras, with a range of films on display. On regular closing days, cameras can be rented unmanned, and drinks include a barley drink and hand-drip coffee. Nearby: Aewol Twigimgan (애월튀김간, restaurant, about 40 m).

An American-style handmade burger restaurant in Cheongsu-ri, Hangyeong-eup, Jeju, housed in a renovated former village hall. Buns and patties are made in-house daily, and it serves craft beer and milkshakes.

A seafood restaurant right on the coastal road in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, Jeju, with a sea view from the front. Popular in summer are cold mulhoe with abalone, sea cucumber and fish, and raw fish rice bowl.
A restaurant in Yeondong, Jeju City, designated for traditional Jeju food. It serves Jeju pork platter sets and seafood sets in generous portions, and is about five minutes from Jeju Airport.
closed_days: none; closed on Seollal and Chuseok holidays

description_en: A grilled meat restaurant in Yeondong, Jeju City, known for pork collar. Pickled perilla leaves, salted anchovy and cheonggukjang are served alongside, and many diners mix cheonggukjang and anchovy sauce into rice.

A casual restaurant in Sangga-ri, Jeju, decorated with block sculptures and toy figures, with a dog in the yard. Its signature is squid cheese tteokbokki, cooked at your table with a whole squid stuffed with cheese, and parking is ample.

A noodle restaurant near Hagwi Elementary School in Jeju City, offering simple dishes such as noodle soup, cold mixed noodles and Jeju soybean noodles. Prices are low, portions generous, and an extra-large portion is available.

A Korean set-meal restaurant in Jeju City blending local Jeju and mainland dishes, known for its Maehwa set. Popular menu items include grilled black pork patties and grilled tilefish, and it is 5-7 minutes by car from Jeju Airport.

A Korean restaurant on the Iljuseoro road in Hyeopjae, Jeju, known for braised hairtail with bracken. Its seafood hotpot includes octopus, shrimp, abalone and crab; all dishes can be taken out, and children's drinks are offered.

A Chinese restaurant in Oedo-dong near Jeju International Airport, known for spicy seafood jjamppong. The spacious dining room and private rooms suit family dinners and group meals, and Iho Tewoo Beach is nearby. Nearby: Sundubu-en Jjamppong (순두부엔짬뽕, restaurant, about 80 m).

A naengmyeon restaurant in Jocheon-eup, Jeju, serving Hwanghae-style buckwheat cold noodles made with 100% Jeju buckwheat flour. Its water naengmyeon uses beef bone broth simmered for 24 hours with Jeju radish dongchimi.

A Jeju pork noodle restaurant in Yeondong, Jeju City, serving only one dish: pork noodles with thick pork and medium noodles in a rich bone broth. It often has a line before opening, and noodles arrive quickly after you sit down. Nearby: Samseonghyeol Seafood Stew (삼성혈해물탕, restaurant, about 60 m).
closed_days: Sun; closed on Seollal and Chuseok holidays

description_en: An organic-certified tea farm in the mid-mountain area of Jeju, inside the Geomun Oreum area, growing and processing green, black, hojicha and matcha teas. Tea sessions are by reservation, including the one-day Tea Mind tasting class.

A cafe in Oedo-dong, Jeju City, with a unique interior and a terrace overlooking the blue sea. Known for drinks and bakery items, it is a good place for sunset photos and relaxing by the sea. Nearby: Nimome Vintage Lounge (니모메빈티지라운지, cafe, about 70 m).

A Japanese udon restaurant in Jocheon-eup, Jeju, run by a celebrity chef. Its signature is chilled yamakake udon topped with grated mountain yam and egg yolk, and tempura udon is also on the menu. Nearby: Jeju Matjip Kalguksu (제주맛집칼국수, restaurant, about 60 m).

A Korean snack restaurant near Jeju Airport on Mugeunseong-gil, with a warm English-style home interior. Its signature is a whole fried rockfish with a special sauce and no fishy taste; rice cake stir-fry and swirl omurice are also served.

The main shop of Umu near the Hallim Harbor breakwater in Jeju, making handmade pudding from agar seaweed gathered by haenyeo divers. The pudding is softer than usual and sold for takeout, and the shop has goods on display. Nearby: Cafe Yuju (카페유주, cafe, about 90 m); Munsso Jeju Hyeopjae Branch (문쏘 제주협재점, restaurant, about 50 m).

A cafe at Seongisidol Ranch in Geumak-dong, Jeju, run by a social enterprise, known for organic milk ice cream and milk tea. Picnic mats can be borrowed for eating outside, and the ranch scenery changes with the seasons.

A gallery-style cafe next to the Kim Changyeol Art Museum in the Jeoji Artists Village, Hangyeong-eup, Jeju. It has concrete walls and glass windows overlooking the garden, and popular items include an egg sandwich and fresh carrot juice.

A stone-house-style cafe in Aewol-eup, Jeju, with a small garden and a bookshop selling independent publications and magazines. Coffee is brewed with fresh beans, and the cafe is close to the airport.
A wood-fired pizza restaurant in Gujwa-eup, Jeju, run by a comedian. Pizzas bake quickly in a hot oven, giving a crispy outside and chewy inside, made with natural cheese and fresh vegetables.
A large cafe in Aewol-eup, Jeju, serving signature coffee, seasonal menus and homemade cookies and desserts. Its signature ade mixes lemonade with matcha, and the wide parking lot suits families.
A Western-style restaurant in Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup, on Jeju's east coast, known for pasta. All sauces are made in-house, and the second floor is a cafe with views of a nearby oreum.
A restaurant in Aewol-eup, Jeju, known for mackerel steamed with aged kimchi, located on Olle Trail course 17 along the coast, with ocean views from terrace seats.
opening_hours: 10:00-20:30 (prep time 16:00-17:00; lunch last order 15:00, dinner last order 19:30)

description_en: A beachfront cafe between Woljeong-ri and Pyeongdae beaches in Gujwa-eup, Jeju, with ocean views. Visitors can try sunset fire-gazing and barbecue experiences, and rent tubes and snorkeling gear, with cakes and croffles on the menu.

A Jeju seafood restaurant in Samdo-i-dong, Jeju City, serving seafood caught by a local male diver, including wild sea squirt and red sea cucumber. The signature is fresh sea urchin eaten wrapped in laver with sesame oil.
A small Chinese restaurant in a Yongdam-dong alley near Jeju Airport, popular with locals. Its signature is spicy jjamppong with chewy noodles, seafood and mushrooms in a clear vegetable broth.

A Japanese home-style restaurant in Aewol-eup, Jeju, serving nine-side-dish Japanese set meals with a hearty Korean-style spread. Popular sets include tempura rice bowl, chirashi sushi, and rice bowl with grilled Patagonian toothfish.

A forest cafe in Jocheon-eup, Jeju, near Dongbaek Forest, with a European-style building and a greenhouse-style space. Large windows look out over a green garden, and the cafe has many photo spots for desserts and drinks.

A cafe near Geumneung Beach and Geumneung Harbor, in a renovated old Jeju stone house decorated with clay pots and plants. It serves hand-drip coffee and homemade bread, and the outdoor garden tables are a popular spot.

A stone-pot rice restaurant in Ido-i-dong, Jeju City, near Hanmaeum Hospital, serving home-style set meals. The Jangmo set includes abalone stone-pot rice, soy-marinated crab, spicy pork and many side dishes, at reasonable prices.

A handmade dumpling restaurant near Aewol Breakwater in Aewol-eup, Jeju, run by a family carrying on a grandmother's recipes. Dumplings are made in-house from scratch with Jeju ingredients, and the signature is a four-color dumpling hotpot.

A black pork restaurant in Aewol-eup, Jeju, near Goeni Port, where staff grill aged black pork over charcoal. The menu includes raw red shrimp, and the walls are covered with signs of celebrity visits.

A small cafe in a quiet alley in Aewol-ri, Jeju, with a stained-glass exterior, known for hand-drip coffee. Its signature Jeremy Coffee is cold milk with a double espresso shot, rich without ice, and thick toast is also popular.
A restaurant in Aewol-eup, Jeju, where every seat has a sea view. Popular dishes include braised hairtail with radish and the large hairtail stew with a whole octopus, served with a seafood platter.
opening_hours: 10:00-20:00 (last order 19:00; closes early when ingredients run out)

description_en: A Jeju pork restaurant in central Noheong-dong, Jeju City, near Jeju Airport. It serves dombe-gogi, sliced boiled pork on a cutting board, made only with Jeju female pigs, and its kimchi is made in-house with fresh fruit.
A takeout and reservation-only kimbap and stuffed tofu pouch shop on Yeonbuk-ro in Hwabuk-dong, Jeju City. Its signature Doldam kimbap is filled with black pork and served with wasabi mayo sauce.

A relaxed ocean-view cafe in a quiet coastal village in Oedo-dong, Jeju City. It has outdoor bar seats facing the sea and freshly roasted coffee, and is known for brunch made with house-baked ciabatta and brioche. Nearby: Jeju Haemulbap (제주해물밥, restaurant, about 40 m); Geureom Oedo (그럼외도, cafe, about 60 m).
A value-for-money noodle restaurant near Sanjicheon in Jeju City, close to the airport and popular with locals. Its meat noodles come with a generous topping of boiled pork.

A small local restaurant on Tapdong-ro in Jeju City, known for traditional Jeju dishes. Its signature bomal kalguksu is knife-cut noodles in a rich broth made with wild bomal sea snails caught by Jeju haenyeo divers, plus bomal porridge. Nearby: Dotori Kitchen (도토리 키친, restaurant, about 90 m).

A long-established noodle restaurant in Hwabuk-ilhdong, Jeju City, popular with locals for its generous portions. Its meat noodles have a deep broth and rich meat topping, and it also serves moguk, a traditional Jeju seaweed and pork stew.

A Korean restaurant at the junction of Aejo-ro and Hanbuk-ro in Jeju City, on the site of the old Jukseong village. It is known for stone-pot rice with dried radish greens, and pouring water into the hot pot makes crispy scorched rice. Grilled golden threadfin bream is also popular.

A knife-cut noodle restaurant on the Yongdam coastal road in Jeju City, in front of the Eoyeong village bus stop. Food is served in traditional charong baskets instead of trays. Its abalone and bomal noodle soup has a deep broth and hand-pulled noodles. Nearby: Hophi Workroom (홉히워크룸, cafe, about 10 m).

A hangover-soup restaurant in Hallim-eup, Jeju, known for Jeju-style fern beef soup and moguk. The broths are simmered slowly in the traditional Jeju way, giving a consistent, rich taste. Nearby: Ongpo Byeoljang Garden (옹포별장가든, restaurant, about 80 m).
A seafood hotpot restaurant near Yongdam Port on the Yongdam coastal road in Jeju City. Its signature dish is a whole octopus in a deep, spicy broth, and it also serves grilled and braised hairtail.

A cafe in Songdang-ri with meadows and gardens inspired by the Glenco area of Scotland. Admission is included in the drink price, and seasonal flowers such as hydrangeas, canola, buckwheat, and pink muhly grass can be seen.

A small, quiet cafe at the edge of Dongbaek Forest, a Ramsar wetland site in Jeju. It has exposed concrete walls, window-frame views of the fields, a red door photo spot, and a flower garden and greenhouse.

A small wooden cafe with a triangular roof, set among fields and stone walls in Eoeum-ri, Aewol-eup, Jeju. It mainly serves drip coffee, and on clear days its windows look out toward the sea and Hallasan.

A cafe in Gwangnyeong-ri, Aewol-eup, across from the start of Jeju Olle Trail Route 17, where Route 16 ends. It is known for its strong coffee and handmade milk tea, and has a photo printer and books for travelers to read.

A dessert cafe in Goseong-ri, Aewol-eup, Jeju, known for visually appealing drinks and bakery kits. Its signature dessert box comes in a wooden box and is limited to 40 sets a day. Goods are sold, and four-cut photos can be taken inside.

A brunch cafe in a residential area near Woryang Elementary School in Jeju City, with a red-brick exterior and white, romantic interiors. Popular dishes include meatball and avocado mentaiko rice bowl, mentaiko pasta, and French toast. It is close to the airport and opens early.

A quiet roastery cafe near the welfare center in Geumneung-ri, Hallim-eup, with five tables. Visitors smell four kinds of beans and choose one for hand-dripped coffee. Groups of five or more and children aged 10 and under are restricted, and pets are allowed.

A cafe in a converted two-story house at the Gamun-dong crossroads on Iljuseo-ro, with a lawn and sea views. Visitors can take framed photos of the stone walls and sea, and reservations allow activities such as making aloe soap or pudding. Late afternoon visits offer sunset views.

An ocean-view cafe near Sehwa Beach in Gujwa-eup, Jeju, housed in a remodeled home split into two buildings. Large windows frame the sea, and a photo spot with a TV-shaped frame is popular. Inside, plants and vintage decor create a cozy feel.

A cafe near Gwandeokjeong in Jeju City that makes its own red bean, lemon, and grapefruit syrups for its shaved ice and drinks. It stays open late at reasonable prices. Its signature items include ginger syrup latte and old-style shaved ice. Nearby: Cafe Dandan (카페단단, cafe, about 60 m); Cafe Hyoju (카페효주, cafe, about 60 m).

A coffee spot in Jeju, about 20 minutes from Jeju Airport, known for its super clean espresso and hand-drip coffee. Guests can enjoy art, books, and walks. Its tangerine cappuccino and latte use citrus, and beans, drip bags, and stationery are sold.

A roastery cafe near the back gate of Jeju Je-il High School in Nohyeong-dong, with simple beige interiors and outdoor tables in the alley. It roasts its own beans and serves baked sweets, egg tarts, and drinks such as tomato basil ade.

A Studio Ghibli-themed cafe based on the 1989 film Kiki's Delivery Service. Its character-inspired menu, including cakes shaped like the black cat and ribbon from the film, makes visitors feel they have stepped into the movie.

A Jeju outpost of Chef Song Hun's Seoul restaurant in Sanggari, Aewol-eup, inside Songhun Park. It specializes in Nanchuk Matdon, a rare Jeju native pig breed restored over ten years and served in limited quantities. Signature dishes include pork belly, pork neck, and a pork tomahawk.

A Thai restaurant opposite Daheul Elementary School in Jocheon-eup, serving modern takes on Thai dishes such as tom yum goong, pad thai, and som tam. Its interior was designed by an architect and feels romantic and stylish.

A curry restaurant by Pyeongdae Beach in Handong-ri, Gujwa-eup, set in a traditional Jeju stone house with a small yard. Its curries use locally grown beans and vegetables, and rice and curry can be refilled.

A tea house in Jocheon-eup with a gray modern building, basalt stone walls, and a large ocean-view window. Visitors can choose tea leaves and brew their own tea in a tea program that comes with snacks. Teapots and tea are displayed in the shop.

A small snack shop on the Pyeongdae coast in Gujwa-eup, with vintage decor and a rooftop table overlooking the sea. It uses fresh ingredients, and its fried hanchi (Jeju squid) is a signature dish. Pets are welcome indoors and outdoors.

A black pork restaurant beside Hallasan Arboretum in Noheong-dong, Jeju City, popular with locals and tourists. It uses carefully selected Jeju black pork, and the menu includes black pork belly, in-house cold noodles, and pork neck marinated in a five-fruit sauce.

A handmade burger restaurant in Noheong-dong near Jeju Airport. Patties and buns are made in-house. The signature Fizz Burger has a thick beef patty with grilled onion, grilled paprika, and Swiss cheese, and suits dates, family meals, and group outings.

A factory-style roastery cafe in Josu-ri, Hangyeong-myeon, housed in a remodeled warehouse with an outdoor area. It serves micro-lot specialty coffee, including the signature Josu latte made with house vanilla syrup, and supplies beans to about 300 cafes in and around Jeju.
closed_days: none; closed on Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A Korean restaurant behind Min Oreum, near the Jeju Provincial Government office, known for jeopjjakbbyeo-guk, a traditional Jeju bone soup. Other dishes include homemade pork cutlet, kimchi nabe, and black pork ttukbaegi bibimbap. It is comfortable for family or friend meals.

A small Korean restaurant in Donam-dong, Jeju City, loved by locals and travelers. Its signature gakjaegi-guk is a clean, light soup with jack mackerel and Chinese cabbage. Other local dishes include mel-guk (anchovy soup) and grilled mackerel.

A garden with a cafe in two buildings, near Hyeopjae Port in Hyeopjae-ri, Hallim-eup. The garden has a small concert hall with a grand piano, multi-level paths, a pink muhly grass hill in autumn, and a cave and observation deck.

A local food dining space in Gujwa-eup, Jeju, where haenyeo (women divers) prepare meals from seafood they gather. Set in a remodeled old seaside warehouse, it also features stage performances that tell haenyeo stories.
closed_days: Tue, Wed; closed on Seollal and Chuseok

description_en: A seafood restaurant on the west coast road of Aewol-eup, Jeju, serving fresh seasonal seafood such as abalone, turban shell, and stone sea squirt. Popular cooked dishes include octopus, steamed turban shell, and abalone porridge cooked to order.

A value-for-money restaurant near Jeju Airport that many visitors come to early in the morning. Grilled mackerel is served as a side, and guests can fry their own eggs. Signature dishes are abalone stew and mulhoe (cold raw fish soup), and there is a sea view outside. Nearby: Tokkiwa Geobugi (토끼와거북이, restaurant, about 40 m).

name_en: Haemul Tongramyeon Mungae Hangari, Aewol Coastal Road Branch
description_en: A seafood ramyeon and kalguksu restaurant near Gamun-dong Port on the Aewol coastal road. Its seafood ramyeon is cooked in a tong pan with wild stone octopus that the owner catches in octopus season. It uses fresh noodles, and the broth is made every morning.

A traditional Chinese restaurant in a residential area of Oedo-dong, Jeju City, where every dish uses certified Jeju pork. It is famous for its large-portion sweet and sour pork, and its beef brisket jjamppong is also recommended.

A Japanese udon restaurant near Geumneung Beach in Hallim-eup, in a small green-painted shop among stone-wall houses, with sea views from inside. Its signature cold udon is mixed with lemon juice, daikon, scallions, and tempura bits.

A noodle restaurant near Hyeopjae Beach, Geumneung Beach, and Hallim Park in Hallim-eup, serving clear, rich broth made from Jeju pork and bones. Its boiled Jeju pork is sold only on the day it is made.

A gomtang (ox-bone soup) restaurant in a village alley between Hyeopjae Beach and Hyeopjae Port, known for its clear broth made only from black pork without added seasoning. The boiled pork is served with Jeju-style doenjang and anchovy paste, and the meat dumplings are popular.

A restaurant in Hallim-eup, Jeju, serving seafood ramyeon with stone octopus, horn shell, and a mixed seafood platter. The bar-style interior faces Biyangdo island and suits solo diners. The seafood comes from the owners' own catches.

A seafood ramyeon restaurant in an alley across from Hyeopjae Beach, with a simple exterior and a cute interior. Its signature seafood ramyeon and octopus seafood ramyeon come with plenty of fresh seafood in a clear, rich broth. It often has a waiting line.
opening_hours: 09:00-19:00 (last order 18:00); closes early when ingredients run out

description_en: A popular seafood ramyeon restaurant in Hyeopjae-ri, Hallim-eup, near Hyeopjae Beach. Its octopus seafood ramyeon has chewy octopus, shrimp, squid, and clams. The menu also includes abalone and cheese rice and meat rice bowls for those who prefer rice. Nearby: Dokgaemul Port (독개물항, restaurant, about 60 m).

A Jeju black pork restaurant near Ido Elementary School in Jeju City, where the meat is grilled slowly over coal briquettes. Diners can choose black or white pork, and besides the meat, only kimchi stew is offered. Tables and baby chairs are provided for families and groups.

A restaurant across from Sehwa Elementary School in Jeju City that serves Japanese-style tonkatsu made with Jeju black pork, along with sandwiches on house-made ciabatta. Its generous set meals are popular with travelers.
opening_hours: 11:00-19:00 (last order 18:30); closes early when ingredients run out
closed_days: none; closed during Seollal and Chuseok holidays

description_en: A German-style bakery in a log cabin in Yuusuam-ri, Aewol-eup, with views of Hallasan. It bakes slowly fermented croissants made with house-grown sourdough and sells pretzels and kouign-amann. When full, visits are limited to 90 minutes, and commercial filming is not allowed.

A Jeju home-cooking restaurant run by the second generation of its family, famous for grilled and braised hairtail. Other local dishes include hairtail and squash soup, golden threadfin seaweed soup, and sea urchin soup, with seasonal fish dishes and course meals also available.

A Korean set-meal restaurant near Hamdeok Post Office in Jocheon-eup, in a 1940s house once used as a clinic. It serves good-value meals of seasonal Jeju ingredients, and its signature 9-course banquet includes Jeju pork and grilled mackerel.
opening_hours: 10:30-21:00 (prep time 15:00-17:00; lunch last order 14:00 / dinner last order 20:00); closes early when ingredients run out

description_en: A raw fish restaurant in front of the Hamdeok Beach parking lot in Jocheon-eup. Its mackerel sashimi is caught and prepared right after ordering, and side dishes such as fried shrimp, roe rice, and corn cheese come with the meal. Nearby: Beodeunamujip (버드나무집, restaurant, about 100 m).

A charcoal-grilled restaurant near Hamdeok Beach in Jocheon-eup, serving top-grade Jeju black pork and fresh raw meat. It uses brass griddles, premium charcoal, and Himalayan pink salt, and its signature dishes include Jeju fresh galbi and black pork belly.
